Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Claims Examiner to grow your career at the forefront of Federal Workers Compensation insurance.


Make your mark in Claims

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency.


How you will create an impact

  • Provide technical expertise in proactively directing and resolving Defense Based Act claims in accordance with best claim practice approach, in line with AIGs quality standards.
  • Manage indemnity, medical and legal aspects of assigned claims using available resources.
  • Utilize investigation, claim handling, litigation, and claim evaluation skills to ensure timely cost- effective claim settlements and protect recovery rights when applicable.
  • Provide prompt effective customer service to differentiate AIG from our competitors.
  • You will also proactively identify and review suspect/fraudulent claims on a consistent basis – dealing with such claims in line with our clear guidelines. 
  • Your work will involve regular contact with internal stakeholders and brokers, (medical) experts, clients’ lawyers, injured workers or their legal representatives. We want you to build effective relationships with internal and external customers, while acting as a point of referral.   
  • In addition, you can use the claims experience you gain to help improve our products in collaboration with colleagues in underwriting.

What you will need to succeed

  • Knowledge of legal / regulatory and litigation / procedural requirements for Workers Compensation claims.
  • Specialist knowledge of Defense Base Act claims is preferred.  
  • Experience in settlement evaluation and negotiation.
  • Policy language skills enabling accurate and consistent policy wording interpretation.  
  • Lateral thinking and the ability to problem solve and develop new ideas to improve working practices. 
  • Strong communication, time management, administrative and report-writing skills.

Job.JobTitle: Associate Actuary – A&H Pricing, North America
Job.JobDescription:
Associate Actuary – A&H Pricing, North America 

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as an Associate Actuary – A&H Pricing, North America to take on key responsibilities within a world-class actuarial function. 


Make your mark in the A&H Actuarial Team 

Our A&H Actuaries are on the front lines, quantifying risk, pricing insurance and providing key analyses for AIG’s stakeholders.  We collaborate with multiple functions, including Finance, Claims, Operations, Marketing and Underwriting.  As an AIG actuary, you will be challenged and encouraged to reach your greatest potential to help improve how we predict, manage and mitigate risk. 


How you will create an impact 

Your expertise in A&H risk management and pricing will be key in helping your team provide technical pricing guidance, product development analytics, performance measurement and financial reporting, while ensuring alignment with regulatory standards and corporate goals in support of the A&H business. 

 
Responsibilities include 

  • Support product innovation by collaborating with cross-functional teams to bring new products to market.  Your knowledge of A&H products and analytical techniques will ensure competitive design and pricing. 
  • Support any risk mitigation solutions to ensure alignment with corporate goals and regulatory standards. 
  • Help translate complex data into actionable insights for senior leadership, influencing strategic decisions related to budget, product design, portfolio management, and business segments. 
  • Assist team members, fostering a culture of collaboration and actuarial best practices. 
  • Independently and effectively engage with various internal and external stakeholders. 
  • Manage multiple projects such as: 
  • Transformation projects for Pricing Management Reporting. 
  • Budget and reinsurance planning.  
  • Provide rating and filing support for the new Stop Loss Program 

What we are looking for 

  • BS in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or related area. 
  • ASA / ACAS Designation is preferred 
  • +5 years of actuarial experience, A&H pricing experience preferred. 
  • Advanced experience with Excel, Python, and PowerPoint. 
  • Knowledge with R and/or other data visualization software a plus. 
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills. 

For positions based in New York , the base salary range is $119,000-$149,000. For positions based in New Jersey, the base salary range is $115,000-145,000. The position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. Your actual compensation will be dependent on your skills, experience, and qualifications. In addition, we’re proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits

Job.JobTitle: Regional Production Specialist Sr, Excess & Surplus Lines
Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Regional Production Specialist Sr, Excess & Surplus Lines to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Underwriting


AIG Underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, and Multinational Clients. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.


How you will create an impact

The Senior Regional Production Specialist must be able to illustrate the highest levels of technical proficiency and underwriting acumen combined with marketing and sales skills to meet production underwriting goals while maintaining budgeted loss and expense ratios. Candidates are expected to work effectively in a team environment to develop broker and portfolio strategies in addition to working independently to manage a profitable book of new and renewal business. The Head of Property for the Zone will rely heavily on this position to assist in guiding, mentoring and training more junior members of the team, as well as to assist in planning and budgeting, collaboration across AIG divisions and building a culture of diversity and inclusion across the team. Responsibilities include:


  • Underwrite risks to maintain and profitably grow our E&S portfolio across our desired business segments.
  • Collaborate with colleagues internally and be reliably visible to our wholesale trading partners.
  • Review and negotiate manuscript form wordings and coverages.
  • Act as a senior mentor to train and guide other members of the team within the Zone

What you’ll need to succeed

  • 7+ years' experience in Commercial Property E&S underwriting.
  • Ability to underwrite property risks across the spectrum of E&S Property business while helping to set direction for your team and maintaining a balanced portfolio across both primary and excess placements.
  • Ability to underwrite 100%, primary/shared and layered, and excess structures.
  • A strong understanding of current market conditions, ability to quickly make decisions and turn around quotes and manage multiple prospects at one time are essential.
  • As a member of the senior leadership within Lexington, take on responsibilities beyond everyday management and underwriting, including mentoring, collaboration within the Zone across business divisions and driving a diverse and inclusive culture.
  • Must be able to work with regional Property leadership peers in order to continue to build a nationally renowned team and culture for Lexington.

Ready to take your career to the next level? We would love to hear from you.


For positions based in Illinois the base salary range for this position is $125,000-$170,000 and the position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. Your actual compensation will be dependent on your skills, experience, and qualifications.  If your compensation expectations are above the posted range, we still encourage you to apply- your unique background matters to us. In addition, we’re proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits Overview.

Job.JobTitle: Regional Multinational Accounts Lead, Trade Credit North America
Job.JobDescription:
Regional Multinational Accounts Lead, Trade Credit North America

AIG’s underwriters develop insurance solutions that address the exposures of companies and individuals, and embody AIG’s tradition of innovation, bringing to market groundbreaking insurance solutions for our changing world. AIG’s underwriters help to find insurance solutions for risks from a range of areas including credit, life insurance, aviation, financial lines, casualty, environmental, catastrophic events, high net worth individuals, and boardroom liabilities.

Make your mark in Trade Credit

AIG Trade Credit develops tailored solutions that help multinational clients manage global trade risks and pursue growth opportunities. Drawing on AIG’s heritage of innovation and underwriting excellence, we deliver market leading solutions that address the evolving challenges of an increasingly interconnected world.

How you will create an impact:

  • Set, agree and deliver financial and budgetary goals for the Multinational segment in North America seizing  exceptional growth and profitability gains by capitalizing on the momentum created by identifiable opportunities in the market.
  • Expansion of the portfolio of large Multinational Programs (MN) in North America
  • Implement strategic plans as agreed with Head of Trade Credit for North America and the Global Head of Multinational, Trade Credit.
  • Markets credit insurance within the Multinational segment through a focused distribution system of select producers (focus tier 1 brokers).
  • Enforces and maintains Multinational underwriting guidelines and compliance with AIG MN.
  • Lead, supervise, train and mentor the underwriting teams with the objective to create solutions for companies taking credit risk management into their own hands and cooperating with AIG as partner for sustainable risk sharing solutions.
  • Provide technical advice to underwriters, credit analysts, brokers, clients and claims regarding scope of coverage, interpretation of wordings and applications.
  • Act as Senior Executive on selected accounts, managing and expanding broker and client relationships. Develop and leverage strong relationships with AIGs Multinational network to benefit from the company’s global footprint.
  • Align with regional management and product leaders in other GI lines incl. Distribution.
  • Represent the Multinational business internally at management meetings and committees.
  • The role will be geared at approximately 70% towards commercial activities and 30% towards Multinational process aspects.
  • This is an integral position that provides front-facing external/internal marketing responsibilities as well as management of office underwriting duties and initiatives within their portfolio.

What you'll need to succeed:

  • A proven track record of 10 years’ experience in Trade Credit insurance or other general insurance lines, ideally spanning over multiple countries/regions.
  • Able to demonstrate a global awareness of the global Trade Credit distribution network and channels.
  • Good communication and interpersonal skills.
  • A positive and agile can-do attitude to contribute to our mission to establish the leading XOL MN program underwriter.   
  • A second language would be preferred.
  • The position requires negotiation and technical skills to successfully navigate business inquiries addressing the international markets. 
  • The candidate must demonstrate team management excellence and create an environment for top performance and high retention.

Ready to set the standard? We would love to hear from you.

The Regional Multinational Accounts Lead, Trade Credit North America will be based in our New York office (or Boston, or Chicago), reporting to the Head of Trade Credit for North America, “dotted line” to Global Head of Trade Credit for Multinationals, and is a member of the Trade Credit North America leadership team. With the ability to manage Trade Credit Operations for the Multinational segment, develop strategies, travel when business requires and lead local underwriting team efficiently, contributing to achievement of the U.S. goals and priorities.

For positions based in New York, the base salary range is $105,000-$148,000. For positions based in New Jersey, the base salary range is $99,000-$143,000, For positions based in Chicago, the base salary range is $120,000-$150,000, For positions based in Boston, the base salary range is $122,000-$150,000. Who we are

AIG, Inc. is a leading provider of insurance products and services for commercial and personal insurance customers.  It includes one of the world’s most far-reaching property casualty networks.  AIG, Inc. (“AIG”) offers a broad range of products to customers through a diversified, multichannel distribution network.  Customers value AIG’s strong capital position, extensive risk management and claims experience and its ability to be a market leader in critical lines of the insurance business.

Corporate Finance - Investment Accounting

The Investment Accounting group at AIG is responsible for the accounting and reporting for AIG's Invested Assets of over $95 billion a comprised primarily of fixed maturity securities and includes private equity, hedge funds, commercial/residential loans and equity securities.  In addition, AIG’s derivative portfolio consists primarily of foreign exchange derivatives but also includes interest rate and other derivative instruments. 

The Investment Accounting group’s specific responsibilities include reconciliation of transactional data from various sub-ledgers to the general ledger and ultimately AIG's financial statements as well as all related external reporting for investments (10Q/K, Financial Supplement, STAT Audited Financials, Investment NAIC reporting and various government regulatory reports).  AIG has multiple legal entities around the globe.

The team is also responsible for establishing the accounting for new transactions or new investment products, implementation of new GAAP and STAT accounting standards as it relates to invested assets, the implementation of new accounting systems as it relates to invested assets, and management of the risks, controls and AIG audit as it relates to investments and supporting Investment FP&A.

Responsibilities

  • Execute and manage accounting processes related to the monthly and quarterly accounting close to ensure accuracy of AIG’s invested assets data across all entities
  • Support the review and preparation of certain Investment disclosures for AIG 10Q/K and Financial Supplement, including as appropriate the Investment, Lending, Fair Value, VIE Footnotes and Investment MD&A
  • Support the review and preparation of NAIC statutory reporting and other regulatory reporting requirements
  • Lead the implementation of process improvements, in coordination with other areas of the department/organization
  • Key point of contact and support for the various business unit and corporate controllers
  • Coordinate with various areas in the organization to develop an understanding of new investment transactions and to provide guidance/support that ensures the accounting results from these investments are accurately recorded in the AIG ledgers
  • Perform ad-hoc analytical requests

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting or finance
  • 7+ years’ experience in accounting and reporting for investment products
  • Strong understanding of investment products and accounting treatment for fixed maturity, equity, and other investment products
  • Strong knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principle (GAAP) and the recording of investments-related journal entries
  • Strong knowledge of statutory reporting gained in part by preparation of statutory reporting schedules
  • Experience with foreign currency remeasurement and translation
  • Excellent analytical skills, including experience performing investment data analysis including commentary
  • Experience reviewing work papers supporting disclosures
  • High level of competency using Microsoft Excel including pivot tables and formulas to create/manage investment data, review investment data and perform analysis
  • Ability to work collaboratively with teams in multiple locations
  • Ability to balance multiple projects at once, to prioritize appropriately, and to approach the work with a sense of urgency and strong attention to detail to produce high quality results in a time sensitive environment
  • Team-player mindset geared towards process improvements and the implementation of accounting controls to ensure consistency and data quality of the team’s financial output
  • High level of motivation and initiative, ability to work independently, including strong organizational skills
  • Comfort level working within a dynamic and complex organizational structure
  • Excellent interpersonal skills with ability to maintain relationships at all levels within the organization
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to communicate effectively with staff, peers, senior management and other external and internal audiences
  • Computer proficiency with a strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office, database experience a plus
  • Experience with PAM/Aladdin a plus

For positions based in New York, the base salary range is $112,000-$140,000. For positions based in New Jersey, the base salary range is $110,000-$138,000. The position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. Your actual compensation will be dependent on your skills, experience, and qualifications. The Central Reserving team is seeking a highly analytical and innovative professional to help advance our reserving capabilities through the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and advanced analytics. This role will be responsible for developing tools and models that identify and quantify key drivers of claims outcomes, uncover insights into loss development behavior, and enhance reserving accuracy across multiple lines of business.

In addition, this role will support the analysis, determination, and reporting of reserves for Extra-Contractual Obligations (ECO) and Corporate-Level Unallocated Loss Expense (ULE).

The successful candidate will partner with reserving actuaries, claims professionals, data scientists, and business leaders to transform complex datasets into actionable insights, modern analytical tools, and next-generation reserving methodologies.

This position offers a unique opportunity to influence the future of actuarial reserving by combining traditional actuarial expertise with cutting-edge AI and advanced analytics capabilities.

 

Key Responsibilities:

  • Support the quarterly process of determining the appropriate amount of IBNR to be booked across assigned reserving segments, including Extra-Contractual Obligations (ECO) and Corporate-Level Unallocated Loss Expense (ULE).
  • Analyze information to determine, document, and communicate the adequacy of loss and loss expense reserves.
  • Develop and apply advanced analytics, predictive modeling, and AI-based tools to identify and quantify key drivers of claims outcomes, improve reserve estimates, and generate business insights into loss development behavior.
  • Research, develop, and enhance reserving methodologies and models to improve reserve accuracy and support actuarial transformation initiatives.
  • Analyze and monitor loss development trends, claims emergence patterns, and relevant industry, regulatory, and operational changes, and effectively communicate findings to management.
  • Partner with Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) to analyze reserve risk for use in capital modeling purposes.
  • Assist with quarterly financial and regulatory reporting (quarter close) and provide data and exhibits for annual statement reporting, including ECO and ULE reporting requirements.
  • Collaborate with Claims, Finance, Pricing, Data Science, and Technology teams to improve data quality, streamline processes, and achieve reserving modernization objectives.
  • Work effectively both independently and as part of a team to achieve the organization's financial, strategic, and operational objectives.

Qualifications:

  • BS in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or related area
  • ACAS or FCAS
  • 4 or more years of experience in reserving and/or pricing
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Work well both independently and as part of a team
  • Proficiency in Excel, SQL, SAS, Python, R, or other programming languages preferred
  • Strong business and collaboration skills and responsive to service needs and operational demands
  • Effective time management skill
  • Strong communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills
  • Strong work ethic

For positions based in New York and Connecticut, the base salary range is $105,000-$130,000. The position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. Who we are:

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. Building on 100 years of experience, today AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance, life insurance, retirement solutions, and other financial services to customers in more than 80 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets, manage risks and provide for retirement security.


About the role:

Supporting the firm’s Chief Executive Officer, Americas and Global Personal Insurance, the Senior Executive Assistant provides extensive, targeted management of day-to-day administrative needs for the executive leader, working closely with the leadership team and other senior management Executive Assistants. Additionally, this role coordinates broader administrative activities such as helping organize staff meetings, distributing group communications, and materials often under short notice. The role requires professional demeanor, impeccable judgement and interpersonal skills, flexibility and a high level of discretion and confidentiality.


Responsibilities:

  • Be a trusted and highly reliable support on the full spectrum of administrative responsibilities and provide some broader team support as appropriate.
  • Interact in a professional manner with senior executives and team members, clients, brokers, and visitors, as a trusted and reliable support person for the executive and leadership team.
  • Partner with administrative peers and other colleagues around the firm to provide a teamwork approach for executive coverage and follow-through.
  • Extensive calendar management and meeting coordination using Microsoft Outlook.
  • Focus on priorities and deadlines, reviewing them with manager with advanced notice and updating the manager on calendar changes, emails and attachments, or any important items.
  • Handle all meeting logistics and preparation of meeting and conference materials ensuring the Executive Leader is prepared. Responsibilities may include, gathering necessary materials, conducting online research or providing briefings where necessary; take notes and follow up on action items when appropriate.
  • Respond and prioritize inquiries, including communicating with direct reports on manager’s behalf.
  • Coordinate complex travel arrangements to include different time zones and prepare itineraries with point-to-point details adhering to company policies.
  • Prepare and submit accurate and timely expenses reports using Concur.
  • Draft and produce grammatically accurate documents and correspondence in Word, PowerPoint presentations, and Excel spreadsheets for internal and external use.
  • Manage phones, transferring, conferencing and routing all business related calls in a discreet and professional manner.
  • Coordinate meetings and strategic activities with leadership team; and assisting in the coordination of agendas for senior management team meetings, internally and externally.

Requirements:

  • Minimum of seven (7) years of direct experience supporting senior executives, preferably in a large, multi-national environment.
  • Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent preferred, but not required.
  • Proven discretion and demonstrated ability to assume autonomy and use independent judgement.
  • Ability to anticipate problems in advance and proactively offer solutions.
  • Advanced ability to prioritize tasks and work with minimal supervision in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills.
  • Dependable; proficient in multitasking and extremely detail oriented.
  • Ability to provide support with a highly specialized knowledge of administration and clerical functions while maintaining confidentiality.
  • Ability to adapt quickly, build and maintain relationships and engage people across the businesses.
  • Technologically savvy with proficiency in Microsoft Office software including Word, PowerPoint, Excel.
  • Working Knowledge of SAP, Concur, Ariba, SharePoint, Fieldglass.
  • Exceptionally clear communicator with solid interpersonal skills.

Job.JobDescription:
About the role

The Senior Representative, Customer Support provides timely, accurate, and professional support to brokers and other authorized business contacts across assigned AIG businesses. Through telephone, email, chat, and case management channels, the representative handles billing inquiries, broker service requests, and administrative support for multiple systems.


This role requires strong communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to research inquiries, navigate multiple applications, and coordinate with internal teams to resolve requests.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Respond to broker inquiries through calls, emails, and chats, providing clear information and timely assistance.
  • Research billing questions involving invoices, payment status, account balances, and billing documents; coordinate with billing teams when additional action is needed.
  • Process and follow up on loss run requests, policy document inquiries, and other assigned broker service requests.
  • Perform authorized administrative tasks across supported systems, including user registration, account maintenance, and access and entitlement management.
  • Assist users with system access, password reset procedures, navigation, and basic troubleshooting.
  • Research service and access issues, escalating complex requests to the appropriate business team or system owner.
  • Maintain accurate interaction records, case notes, and documentation of administrative actions.
  • Follow confidentiality, identity verification, information security, and access approval requirements.
  • Meet established expectations for service quality, productivity, response times, attendance, and schedule adherence.
  • Participate in training and coaching, collaborate with colleagues, and identify opportunities to improve the broker experience.
  • Broker Services supports multiple AIG businesses. Responsibilities may evolve to include additional lines of business, acquired or integrated businesses, products, systems, and service channels. Learning and supporting these assignments within the scope of the role, through provided training and cross-training, is an ongoing expectation of the position.

Qualifications:

  • Prior customer service, contact center, or administrative support experience; insurance or broker support experience preferred.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills and a professional approach to customer interactions.
  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to research and follow requests through resolution.
  • Ability to navigate multiple applications and learn billing processes, insurance terminology, and system administration procedures.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, follow established procedures, and work independently and collaboratively. Experience with Salesforce, Genesys, or user access administration is a plus.
  • High school diploma or equivalent.

Job.JobTitle: Assistant General Counsel, Bad Faith Litigation
Job.JobDescription:
Who we are:

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. Building on 100 years of experience, today AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance and other financial services to customers in more than 80 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets, manage risks and provide financial security.

Get to know the business:

AIG’s Global Legal, Compliance, Regulatory and Government Affairs (GLCR) department is comprised of attorneys and other professionals providing high-quality advisory and transactional support with integrity and objectivity across all parts of the organization. The team ensures an operating environment that minimizes legal, regulatory and reputational risks, complies with all laws and regulations, and enforces AIG policies and procedures. 

This is a global, diverse and award-winning team that has been recognized for its leadership and innovative solutions. You will also be eligible to participate in AIG’s award-winning pro bono program.

AIG’s GLCR department is looking for an experienced attorney to serve as an Assistant General Counsel managing bad faith litigation and providing advice to AIG’s claims organization in the New York office.  

Specific Responsibilities Include:

The primary purpose of the position is to manage an active litigation docket consisting of bad faith and extra-contractual matters arising from the handling of claims under casualty, financial lines, property and specialty policies issued to commercial and personal lines insureds.  The attorney will also be responsible for providing timely advice to claim handlers in order to avoid and/or mitigate extra-contractual exposures. 

  • Manage an active litigation docket consisting of bad faith and extra contractual matters;
  • Develop resolution strategies and make recommendations to senior management;
  • Direct and supervise outside counsel with respect to the implementation of litigation strategies;
  • Ensure that high-quality written work product is filed on behalf of the AIG member insurance companies;
  • Collaborate with business partners in the claims organization on strategic decisions and provide timely advice to claim handlers to avoid and/or mitigate bad faith exposure;
  • Prepare and conduct regularly scheduled training presentations to claim handlers.
  • On occasion and as necessary, travel for mediations, trials;

Education / Experience:

  • Attorney with at least 7+ years of law firm litigation experience strongly preferred;
  • J.D. from an accredited law school and strong academic credentials;
  • Admitted to practice in at least one state;
  • Litigation experience should include preparing witnesses for, taking, and defending depositions, as well as drafting and arguing dispositive motions;
  • Trial experience very useful but not required
  • In-house experience with another insurer is also useful but not required.

 

To succeed in this position, the successful candidate must possess the following skills:

  • Strong initiative and work ethic; 
  • Focused attention to detail and honed analytical skills; 
  • Superior oral and written communication skills; 
  • Strong interpersonal skills; 
  • Ability to be a self-starter and work independently; 
  • Flexibility and a willingness to adapt to changing needs of the organization and/or business clients; 
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills, including the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment; 
  • Ability to deliver creative and well-reasoned plans to resolve challenges and to execute on such plans; 
  • Ability to thrive in an environment where coordination and teamwork is a priority while also being committed to individual accountability and results; 
  • Willingness to be mentored and trained to meet the needs of the organization; and 
  • Sound legal and business judgment. 

  


A look at our benefits

At AIG, we have a 100-year legacy of working to make the world a better place.  And that begins with our employees. We’re proud to offer a range of employee benefits and resources that help you protect what matters most – your health care, savings, financial protection, and wellbeing. We provide a variety of leaves for personal, health, family, and military needs. For example, the “Giving Back” program allows you to take up to 16 hours a year to volunteer in your community.

We also believe in fostering our employees’ development and offer a range of learning opportunities for employees to hone their professional skills to position themselves for the next steps of their careers. AIG also has a tuition reimbursement program for eligible employees to enhance their education, skills, and knowledge in areas that relate to their current position or future positions to which they may transfer or progress.

We provide equal opportunity to all qualified individuals regardless of race, color, religion, age, gender, gender expression, national origin, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected categories. At AIG, we believe that diversity and inclusion are critical to our future and our mission – creating a foundation for a creative workplace that leads to innovation, growth, and profitability. Through a wide variety of programs and initiatives, we invest in each employee, seeking to ensure that our people are not only respected as individuals, but also truly valued for their unique perspectives.

Job.JobTitle: Head of Financial Lines Technical Claims
Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as the Head of Financial Lines Technical Claims to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Claims

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency.


How you will create an impact

As the North America Head of Financial Lines Technical Claims you will report to the North America Head of Financial Lines Claims, and be responsible for technical oversight of Financial Lines Claims in North America. You will be responsible for driving Claims technical excellence and be a recognized subject matter expert within and outside of the Claims function in the relevant business lines.  You will collaborate directly with senior claims, underwriting, actuarial, legal and compliance leaders to ensure effective development and management of strategic objectives and policies for those lines of business, and be responsible for leading the development of clear and effective strategies for resolving high complexity and severity claims, for identifying claim and coverage trends, and for driving technical excellence and internal business partner communication within specific business lines.  You are also responsible for setting strategic vision for the approach to and resolution of these claims, driving claims consistency by product, partnering with underwriting on trends and exposures and working with actuarial to develop a robust and consistent approach to claims exposure assessment and reserving.

  • Providing oversight of complex, high severity claims across D&O, E&O/MPL, Fiduciary, Fidelity, Financial Institutions, Employment Practices Liability products, focusing on overall claims consistency, thought leadership, best practices, lessons learned and technical trainings across all regions and products in North America.
  • Monitoring of, and escalation/referral for guidance, direction and authority on, matters involving high severity and/or complex coverage issues and matters involving high profile insureds or events or of significant impact.
  • Active involvement in highest severity or high profile claims, at the direction of senior claims management, including direct involvement in negotiation of settlements with Insureds and Claimants, based on sensitivity, severity, complexity or age of matter, as necessary.
  • Assisting the Head of Financial Lines Claims with the effective management and implementation of strategic claim objectives and policies for a line of business, in accordance with the company's strategic plans. ·
  • Claims trend and legal development identification, analysis and reporting, including regular LOB reports for senior claims management and internal business partners and similar LOB-specific reporting; coordination with IT/claims data functions to ensure necessary/correct data views.
  • Providing oversight and management of systemic and quasi-systemic claim issues that cross all lines of business; generating periodic reports and updates regarding exposures to senior claims, actuarial and underwriting management.
  • Reviewing, developing and/or delivering technical claims training content; developing a formalized “lessons learned” capability fit for purpose for Financial Lines to ensure claim insights are communicated consistently with stakeholders in Underwriting and Actuarial.
  • Communication of, education and training regarding existing or developing coverage issues to ensure accuracy and consistency of position/approach.

What you’ll need to succeed:

  • Extensive knowledge in several diverse disciplines or recognized professional fields, i.e. commercial insurance policy coverage and controlling laws, litigation management governance/control and comprehensive understanding of critical issues in other related areas.
  • Advanced communication skills which are critical to building consensus across areas of influence (external and/or internal relationships), team, and/or matrix environment.
  • Superior leadership and management skills demonstrating integrity and professionalism.
  • Proven ability to drive results by identifying and resolving significant problems within scope of responsibility.
  • Extensive knowledge of the insurance industry, its products and services.
  • 15+ of related work experience with commercial or Risk Management claims including technical claim handling, coverage interpretation, and claim/litigation.
  • The ideal candidate will have a Bachelor’s Degree with a Master’s Degree or JD preferred.

Ready to take your career to the next level? We would love to hear from you.

Job.JobTitle: Underwriting Team Lead, Lexington Middle Market Property
Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as an Underwriting Team Lead to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Lexington


AIG underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, Multinational Clients, and High Net Worth individuals. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model, and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.


How you will create an impact


  • Ability to exercise judgment, negotiate and make sound business decisions effectively based on increased level of authority.
  • Renders alternative outcomes for more difficult situations and makes real-time decisions in a fast-paced environment characterized by ambiguity and change.
  • Support consistent underwriting best practices, in accordance with underwriting guidelines, to ensure rating, pricing, profitability, and structuring adequacy.
  • Responsible for assigning and managing the work of a team of underwriters.
  • Assist underwriters in executing on strategic initiatives.  Provide support and develop solutions to their issues/concerns (system, guidelines, training, reports, new project request, product amendments). 
  • Assist underwriters in collaborating with Distribution, Territory Managers, and other line(s) of business underwriters to target desirable accounts and cross selling opportunities from brokers.
  • Utilize various daily reports and constant monitoring of adherence to underwriting requirements and guidelines to oversee assigned book of business.
  • Keep abreast of developments in assigned territories to determine their effect on current accounts and potential new business opportunities.
  • Work with management, the Insured, its broker and outside counsel on contract terms and conditions, as well as pricing, terms & conditions, and deal structure for complex risks.
  • Develop strong, long-term relationships with brokers and clients to profitably grow a book of business.
  • Identify the need for and manage special underwriting projects as needed.
  • Provide superior customer service to brokers and clients.
  • Produce, underwrite, manage and service a profitable book of business.

What you’ll need to succeed


  • Effective Team and People Manager, able to attract, engage, retain, and develop a high performing team to meet current and future business needs with ability to clearly articulate and execute plans.
  • Commercial Insurance Company, Agency or Brokerage experience
  • Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university preferred.
  • Proven ability to build and maintain strong professional relationships.
  • Advanced knowledge of Excess & Surplus Property line of business, including product features, forms, regulatory environment and risks etc.
  • Demonstrated sales, marketing, and relationship building experience.
  • Highly motivated and results oriented
  • Very strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to work in dynamic, rapidly changing environment, adapting to changing requirements and collaborating with a wide range of colleagues to quickly deliver solutions.
  • Proficient with underwriting analytical tools and technology.

Ready to solve bigger problems? We would love to hear from you.

UW - UnderwritingLexington Specialty Insurance Agency, Inc.

Join us as Director, Personal Lines Programs to play a key leadership role that will drive business growth.


This role provides active governance and direct oversight for a key Managing General Underwriter (MGU) partner. This role is the primary safeguard for the program’s systemic integrity, ensuring that the MGU’s execution across a diverse & complex portfolio of products aligns with AIG’s standards for regulatory health and operational excellence.


The role focuses on rigorous oversight of the MGU’s internal control environment and the operational infrastructure supporting a $1.7B portfolio. The ideal candidate brings a strong operations background and the technical intuition to ensure that compliance mandates and IT controls are translated into system reality - guaranteeing that the MGU partner remains compliant, profitable, and positioned for growth.

 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:


Regulatory & Compliance Governance

  • Mandate Accountability: Act as the central point for regulatory requirements issued by the AIG Compliance Officer. Ensure the MGU is not only aware of these mandates but has successfully integrated them into their programming and workflows.
  • Audit Management: Lead the oversight of both internal and external (regulatory) audits. Ensure the MGU has the right practices in place to pass audits and proactively remediate any operational gaps.
  • Milestone Tracking: Utilize project management expertise to hold the MGU accountable for critical timelines, including rate filings, form & contract updates, and defect resolution.

Controls & Systemic Integrity Oversight

  • Rating Integrity & Quality of Issuance: Oversee the MGU’s internal processes to ensure rating integrity. Validate that the MGU is conducting proper testing and that all rate updates are implemented correctly within their systems.
  • Systems & IT Controls: Audit the MGU’s systems and controls to ensure the operational framework is sound. This includes verifying the accuracy of system-generated outputs and the robustness of the MGU’s IT control environment.
  • Process Validation: Act as the final check on MGU operational changes, ensuring that systemic updates do not create financial leakage or regulatory risk.

Performance Monitoring

  • Results Analysis: Monitor program performance to ensure the business remains compliant, profitable, and on a growth trajectory.
  • Root-Cause Inquiry: Conduct "deep dive" reviews into business results. When performance fluctuates, investigate & identify whether shifts are driven by underwriting trends, system errors, or market conditions.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Executive Operational Track Record: 10+ years of progressive experience in Insurance Operations, Compliance, Project Management, or MGU/Carrier Oversight.
  • Systemic Proficiency: A strong understanding of how rating engines and policy administration systems function, with the "technical intuition" to audit complex systems and mechanics.
  • Project Management Excellence: Proven ability to track high-stakes deliverables across multiple work streams and hold external partners accountable to deadlines.
  • Analytical Curiosity: A natural drive to look beneath the surface of data to find operational inconsistencies or opportunities for improvement.
  • Governance Mindset: Strong experience in managing compliance audits, IT controls, and quality assurance frameworks.
  • Strategic Communication: Proven ability to hold external partners (MGUs) accountable while fostering a productive, growth-oriented relationship.
  • Specialized Product Knowledge: Working knowledge of both Admitted and Excess & Surplus Lines (E&S) products, rates, and regulatory requirements.
  • Data Fluency: Strategic ability to leverage analytical tools and complex reporting to derive business insights and evaluate emerging insurance technology solutions.

Ready to prove your leadership skills? We would love to hear from you.

Join us as a Claims Analyst III, E&O to take on key responsibilities within a world-class claims function.


Make your mark in Claims

As a Claim Analyst III, E&O, you will be responsible for handling all aspects of multi-line, financial lines claims from inception through conclusion brought against insureds. You will determine coverage, evaluate liability and assess damages on claims tendered to multiple Errors & Omissions policies, including School Leaders, Public Officials, Lawyers, Media, Cyber. Establish timely reserves. Interface with insureds, brokers, and counsel to resolve claims. Communicate with underwriting as necessary and with senior claims management.


How you will create an impact

  • You will be responsible for a portfolio of claims from coverage inquiry through legal liability assessment and quantum analysis, to timely and accurate resolution.
  • Your goal will be timely, accurate and customer-focused claim resolution, minimizing indemnity exposure and mitigating vendor and legal expense – you will actively promote and demonstrate the principles of ‘Treating Customers Fairly’ in claims handling. 
  • You will communicate regularly with internal and external stakeholders in your role as a Errors & Omissions claims expert and thought leader.
  • As a valued member of the team, you will work closely with our underwriting partners to provide feedback on claim exposures and trends to inform decisions on the portfolio.
  • Work with underwriting on policy renewals and promoting client relationships
  • You will also contribute to continuous improvement in Claims by supporting Quality Assurance / Regional Audit processes, ensuring mitigation of indemnity and expense exposure while communicating developments and outcomes as necessary to all key internal and external stakeholders.

What you’ll need to succeed

  • Experience handling third-party claims, litigation or other related experience.
  • Knowledge of legal / regulatory and litigation / procedural requirements for professional liability and/or construction claims.
  • Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent required. Multi-state adjuster licenses and/or JD preferred.
  • Experience in negotiation, mediation, arbitration and ADR skills on higher value complex claims.
  • Policy language skills enabling accurate and consistent policy wording interpretation.
  • A track record of following up effectively on recommendations from technical claims audits and continuous file handling improvement.
  • The ability to influence claims and non-claims stakeholders by effectively directing claims strategy.

Ready to take your career to the next level? We would love to hear from you.

Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Claims Analyst III - EPL and D&O to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Claims

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency. 


How you will create an impact

As a Claims Analyst III, you will be responsible for handling Employment Practices Liability claims with opportunity to handle Director & Officers claims, which includes identifying, investigating, and resolving multiple coverage issues at the earliest appropriate time and providing clear and concise written and verbal communication of policy coverage issues to insureds, brokers, underwriters and risk managers. Additional responsibilities include:

  • Timely investigating claims for coverage, liability and damage analysis;
  • Being thoughtful and working with the Insured and defense counsel to formulate effective and cost-effective claims resolutions;
  • Effectively analyzing and budgeting the litigation of each claim through timely and regular discussions with counsel, vendors and Insureds through the life of the claim;
  • Valuing claims within a reasonable time frame and making presentations to management as necessary; and
  • Managing reserve adjustments and payments to avoid deficit payments.

What you’ll need to succeed

  • Claims and/or litigation experience.
  • Financial Lines experience (EPL, D&O, ERISA claims) preferred.
  • Ability to analyze policies of insurance and legal documents.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal and organizational skills.
  • Strong computer skills (Microsoft Office).
  • Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent required. JD highly preferred.

Job.JobTitle: Mass Tort and Complex Casualty - Complex Claims Director
Job.JobDescription:
Mass Tort and Complex Casualty - Complex Director


At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Mass Tort and Complex Casualty - Complex Director to play your part in that transformation. You’ll work with some of the best claims and underwriting minds in the industry addressing challenging claims and sophisticated coverage issues, and helping our businesses develop products to address the rapidly evolving risk environment. Grow your career at the forefront of Casualty insurance.


In Mass Tort and Complex Casualty Claims, we strive to live AIG’s corporate values: Take Ownership, Set the Standard, Win Together, Be an Ally, Do What’s Right. At AIG, we are committed to creating a culture that truly respects and celebrates each other’s talents, backgrounds, cultures, opinions and goals. We foster a culture of inclusion and belonging through our flexible work arrangements, diversity and inclusion learning, cultural awareness activities and Employee Resource Groups (ERGs). With global chapters, ERGs are a cornerstone for our culture of inclusion. The diversity of our people is one of AIG’s greatest assets, and we are honored that our drive for positive change has been recognized by numerous recent awards and accreditations.


Make your mark in Casualty Claims

As a seasoned industry professional, in this role you’ll deal with sophisticated litigation and coverage issues, including long-tail bodily injury and property damage exposures, claims arising under Coverage B of Primary/Excess CGL policies, as well as environmental and toxic tort claims. You’ll handle emerging risks; this team has been at the forefront of managing exposures from PFAS, opioids, and other cutting-edge issues. You’ll also be a coverage resource for Casualty adjusters, managers and underwriters.  You’ll be supported by a management team that’s deeply invested in achieving the right outcomes for claims and that’s also invested in your success:  


You will:

  • Evaluate coverage on sophisticated insurance products
  • Hire and manage counsel to help evaluate coverage and to defend our insureds.
  • Assess damages with support of outside experts
  • Evaluate financial impact to AIG and to our insureds 
  • Formulate and execute strategies for favorable claim resolution; negotiate with insureds and third parties.
  • Advise business partners concerning exposures and concerning potential product changes and enhancements.
  • Advise claims and business leaders on emerging risks.

What you’ll need to succeed

  • 6+ years of Legal, Insurance, Construction Defect or Environmental experience preferred.
  • The ability to handle complex claims involving diverse coverage issues related to GL and Environmental policies.
  • Strong analytical and organizational skills, along with excellent communication, negotiation and investigation skills.

Ready to take your career to the next level? We would love to hear from you.

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as an Senior Underwriter, AIG Risk Management (AIGRM) to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make you mark in Underwriting


AIG underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, Multinational Clients, and High Net Worth individuals. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model, and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.


How you will create an impact


  • The Senior Underwriter will be responsible for underwriting the Workers’ Compensation, General Liability and Auto Liability primary Casualty product lines and typically manages accounts/clients that are most complex.
  • Develops and manages underwriting strategies for both renewals and prospects within his/her portfolio of accounts. This includes knowledge of the current market penetration of AIGRM products and the development of specific plans to increase portfolio share. 
  • Develops and implements negotiation strategies. Makes independent sales calls to market and cross-market products. Identifies target markets, designs, and implements strategies for lead development and builds prospect lists.
  • Provides technical direction to management, less senior specialists, producers, and claims adjusting personnel. Communicate risk appetite and AIGRM Value Proposition to brokers. 
  • Collaborate with Distribution, Territory Managers, and other line(s) of business underwriters to target desirable accounts and cross selling opportunities from brokers.
  • Rapidly evaluate, prioritize, and select submissions to be underwritten.
  • Recognize and create cross sell opportunities for other Commercial products.
  • Collaborate with broker to understand the deal structure, terms, and AIG Services that best meets clients’ needs. 
  • May review, evaluate and make recommendations to underwriting guidelines. 
  • May direct or conduct internal underwriting audits. 
  • Negotiate pricing, terms & conditions, and deal structure with brokers and clients.
  • Participate in special underwriting projects as needed. 

What you’ll need to succeed


  • 5+ years of Commercial Insurance Company, Agency, or Brokerage experience. 
  • Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university. 
  • Proven ability to build and maintain strong professional relationships.
  • Advanced working knowledge of US Casualty lines of business (Workers’ Compensation, Auto Liability, and General Liability) including product features, forms, regulatory environments, and risks etc. 
  • Demonstrated sales, marketing, and relationship building experience. 
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills. 
  • Highly motivated and results oriented. 
  • Ability to work in a dynamic environment, adapting to changing requirements and collaborating to deliver solutions quickly
  • Strong skills evaluating large quantities of data in Microsoft Excel.
  • Expert with underwriting analytical tools and technology.

Job.JobDescription:
Your future team

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Casualty Coverage and Mass Tort Assistant Vice President to play your part in that transformation. You’ll work with some of the best claims and underwriting minds in the industry addressing challenging claims and sophisticated coverage issues, and helping our businesses develop products to address the rapidly evolving risk environment. Grow your career at the forefront of Casualty insurance.

In Complex Casualty Claims, we strive to live AIG’s corporate values: Take Ownership, Set the Standard, Win Together, Be an Ally, Do What’s Right. At AIG, we are committed to creating a culture that truly respects and celebrates each other’s talents, backgrounds, cultures, opinions and goals. We foster a culture of inclusion and belonging through our flexible work arrangements, diversity and inclusion learning, cultural awareness activities and Employee Resource Groups (ERGs). With global chapters, ERGs are a cornerstone for our culture of inclusion. The diversity of our people is one of AIG’s greatest assets, and we are honored that our drive for positive change has been recognized by numerous recent awards and accreditations.

Make your mark in Casualty Claims

As a Manager and Leader within the Casualty Coverage and Mass Tort Claims Department, you are respected for your deep technical expertise and ability to oversee employees, programs and processes, as you manage a team of approximately 6-8 claims adjusters. Your team will address sophisticated litigation and coverage issues, including long-tail bodily injury and property damage exposures, claims arising under Coverage B of Primary/Excess CGL policies, as well as environmental and toxic tort claims. The team also handles emerging risks, and has been at the forefront of managing exposures from PFAS, opioids, and other cutting-edge issues.  You and your team will be a coverage resource for Casualty adjustors, managers and underwriters. You will be supported by a management team that is deeply invested in achieving the right outcomes for claims and that’s also invested in your success. This position reports directly to a Vice President of the Casualty Coverage and Mass Tort Claims Department.

You will:

o   Monitor and guide appropriate reserving, expense and payments within your claims team

o   Develop your team’s claims handling skills, with a focus on proactive investigate, evaluation, and resolution

o   Manage and oversee communication between your team and Insureds and other external clients

o   Empower and lead the claims adjusters to embody AIG’s corporate values

o   Identify and escalate complex claims to senior management with significant coverage, loss, or other issues

o   Support departmental initiatives focusing on improved claim processes, claims results and financial results

o   Lead training and development initiatives to educate and instruct claims adjusters on trends and emerging issues

o   Communicate clearly with Actuarial and Underwriting on relevant claims, case law, and other trend information

o   Participate in a robust feedback loop with Underwriting on client renewals and new business opportunities

What we are looking for

o   10+ years of Legal or Insurance experience preferred

o   Demonstrated experience with evaluations and investigations addressing coverage, liability and damage issues

o   Strong communication skills, in addition to the ability to prepare and present information in a concise and persuasive manner

o   Drive collaborative behavior with leadership team across the wider business

o   Ability to develop and execute creative solutions to difficult problems impacting our business partners

Job.JobTitle: Senior Manager -Internal Audit Business Intelligence & Analytics
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Internal Auditor, Accounting / Finance, Data Engineer
Job.JobDescription:
Role Summary


The Senior Manager– Business Intelligence & Analytics is responsible for leading the development and delivery of enterprise analytics, reporting, and data-driven insights for Internal Audit Department within AIG.
This role partners with senior leaders and internal auditors to transform complex operational, risk, and performance data into clear, actionable insights. The position combines strong technical expertise in business intelligence and data modeling with business acumen, stakeholder management, data governance, and analytical storytelling.
The role will lead the design of scalable reporting solutions, executive dashboards, KPI frameworks, thematic and root-cause analysis, and analytics capabilities that help leadership identify emerging risks, understand performance drivers, prioritize remediation, and make informed business decisions.


Key Responsibilities


Business Intelligence & Analytics Ownership


  • Lead the design, development, and delivery of enterprise BI and analytics solutions supporting Internal Audit Operations, and senior management.
  • Translate complex business requirements into scalable reporting, analytics, and data solutions.
  • Establish reporting strategies, KPI frameworks, scorecards, and analytical approaches aligned with business and regulatory objectives.
  • Identify opportunities to improve decision-making through advanced analytics, automation, and AI-assisted analysis.
  • Provide technical and analytical leadership to other team members.


Executive Reporting & Data Storytelling


  • Develop executive-level dashboards and management reporting that communicate key trends, risks, performance indicators, and areas requiring management attention.
  • Translate complex datasets into concise, actionable narratives for senior leadership and governance committees.
  • Present analytical findings, emerging trends, and business implications to senior management.

Power BI & Data Visualization


  • Design and develop enterprise Power BI dashboards, scorecards, and analytical applications.
  • Build scalable semantic models using dimensional/star-schema modeling principles.
  • Develop advanced DAX measures and reporting logic to support complex business requirements.
  • Create intuitive visualizations that enable both executive-level monitoring and detailed analytical investigation.

Data Engineering & Integration


  • Use SQL Server and other enterprise data sources to extract, transform, integrate, and analyze data.
  • Integrate information from platforms such as ServiceNow IRM and other data sources such as SharePoint and Snowflake databases.

Data Quality & Governance
 

  • Identify source-system data quality issues and assess their impact on downstream analytics and reporting.
  • Develop data-quality reports.
  • Partner with Auditors and technology teams to drive remediation of recurring data issues.
     

Advanced Analytics & AI


  • Identify opportunities to apply AI and advanced analytics to improve analytical efficiency and insight generation.
     

Stakeholder & Team Leadership


  • Lead requirements-gathering sessions and translate business questions into analytical solutions.
  • Manage competing reporting priorities and establish delivery roadmaps.
  • Mentor other team members and promote best practices in analytics, visualization, data modeling, and data storytelling.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert to business and senior leadership.

Required Qualifications


  • 8+ years of experience in Business Intelligence Reporting, Data Management, or related disciplines.
  • Significant experience delivering analytics and reporting solutions within complex enterprise environments.
  • Advanced experience with Power BI, SQL Server, DAX, and dimensional data modeling.
  • Strong understanding of data quality, governance, KPI development, and enterprise reporting.
  • Experience supporting  Internal Audit Operations, or regulated business functions.
    Strong experience developing executive dashboards and presenting insights to senior leadership.
  • Ability to translate complex technical and analytical findings into clear business narratives and recommendations.
  • Strong stakeholder management, communication, problem-solving, and leadership skills.


Preferred Qualifications


  • Experience in Internal Audit domain.
  • Experience with ServiceNow IRM or similar Governance, Risk, and Compliance platforms.
  • Experience establishing reporting standards, and enterprise analytics operating models.


Core Competencies


Business Intelligence | Power BI | SQL | Data Modeling | Executive Reporting | Data Storytelling | Internal Audit Analytics | KPI & Scorecard Development | Data Quality | Data Governance | ServiceNow IRM | Automation | Stakeholder Management

Data Engineer Lead

AIG | Data Office · Data Engineering


About The Role

The Data Engineer Lead is a hands-on engineering role within AIG's Data Engineering organization. You will design, build, and operate production-grade data pipelines and platforms — and bring sound engineering judgment to every solution you deliver.

We actively leverage GenAI tooling — including Claude Code and Snowflake Cortex — as a genuine productivity multiplier across the development lifecycle. We want someone who is motivated to learn, keeps up with a fast-moving space, and continuously finds new ways to put these tools to work.

You will collaborate closely with the product owner, business stakeholders, and fellow engineers. Strong communication and analytical skills matter here as much as technical depth — the ability to ask the right questions, think through trade-offs clearly, and explain your reasoning is part of the job.

 

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and operate production-grade PySpark and Python pipelines on AWS EMR, Glue, and S3 with integrated data quality checks and observability.
  • Own end-to-end delivery of data products from requirements through production, working within an Agile/Scrum framework — including sprint planning, CI/CD, release management, and production readiness
  • Translate business and product requirements into concrete technical designs, defining pipeline structure, data models, and SLAs.
  • Demonstrate a sound understanding of architecture and design patterns, evaluate trade-offs of design decisions, and articulate clear rationale to peers and stakeholders.
  • Set and enforce engineering standards — coding conventions, data quality frameworks, reusable pipeline patterns, and observability hooks — across the team.
  • Conduct thorough code reviews and pair with engineers on hard problems, raising the technical quality of the whole team.
  • Leverage GenAI tooling — such as Claude Code CLI, Snowflake Cortex — throughout the development lifecycle to write better code faster and improve solution quality.
  • Collaborate with product owners to refine requirements, surface trade-offs, and push back constructively when scope is technically unworkable.
  • Communicate design decisions and delivery updates clearly to both engineering peers and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Mentor junior engineers through review, pairing, and knowledge sharing, building team capability alongside product delivery.
  • Produce clear technical documentation — Architecture Decision Record (ADR), runbooks, data dictionaries, and pipeline lineage notes — as a standard part of delivery, not an afterthought.
  • Evaluate and drive adoption of productivity tooling and best practices, setting team norms for safe and effective use.

Experience/Skills

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • 7+  years of hands-on data engineering experience with a consistent track record delivering production data pipelines end-to-end.
  • Strong command of PySpark, Python, and SQL — including Spark optimization, partition management, and query performance tuning in Snowflake.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS data services: S3, Glue, EMR, Aurora, Lambda, IAM, and CloudWatch.
  • Working knowledge of architecture and design principles — Lakehouse patterns, data modeling, fault-tolerant ingestion — with demonstrated ability to apply them in practice.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills: able to decompose complex requirements, reason through design trade-offs, and arrive at practical, well-justified solutions.
  • Clear communicator — able to explain technical decisions and design rationale in plain language to both engineering peers and business stakeholders.
  • Self-motivated learner with a genuine interest in staying current with evolving tools, frameworks, and engineering best practices.
  • Demonstrated use of GenAI tooling (e.g. Claude Code CLI or Snowflake Cortex) to improve productivity or solution quality.

Preferred/Nice To Have


  • AWS certification — Solutions Architect Associate or equivalent.
  • Domain familiarity with insurance or financial services data — claims, policy, risk, or actuarial structures.
  • Experience writing ADRs, design notes, or technical documentation in a collaborative engineering team.

Our Culture

AIG's Data Office is a team of builders, thinkers, and pragmatic problem-solvers. We move with the urgency of a technology company and the accountability of a global insurer.

Great data engineering is a team sport here. We write documentation as carefully as we write code, review designs together, mentor across every level, and keep business stakeholders close to the work. We lean into GenAI not as a novelty but as a genuine force multiplier — and we want people who share that mindset.

AIG is committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and encourages candidates from all backgrounds to apply. We offer competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and hybrid flexibility.

Job.JobTitle: Head of Lexington Middle Market Property
Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as the Head of Midmarket Property Underwriting to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Lexington Midmarket Property


AIG underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, Multinational Clients, and High Net Worth individuals. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model, and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.


How you will create an impact


  • Drive Lexington’s Excess and Surplus Property Midmarket vision and value proposition that recognize changing business and competitive environment dynamics, key business drivers, and financial elements and demonstrate the value we bring to the different segments of our producer delivery network. 
  • Responsible for the GWP and P&L of the Midmarket Property book of business; assessing line of business ROE and allocation of  capital as necessary 
  • Monitor Catastrophe modeling results within the portfolio to ensure we are in line with corporate mandates for risk aggregation in aggregate and by zone 
  • Strategically review use of reinsurance to reduce volatility and as an alternative form of capital within the book and supports our risk appetite for per risk and aggregation across all product lines 
  • Develop, position, market, and deliver innovative, market-leading products and services through a zonal  framework to a network of producers in a manner that effectively leverages our strengths as a competitive differential in the marketplace.  
  • Established business strategies to deliver a profitable shift of business mix, and support efforts to become our Clients’ most Valued Insurer, all while maximizing synergy with other AIG business partners 
  • Lead the Midmarket platform for Property business, working closely with Head of Wholesale Property to enhance and integrate all complimentary product offerings 
  • Establish and implement a long-term business strategy for Midmarket Property focusing on risk appetite that effectively manages risk 
  • Drive consistent distribution and underwriting best practices and guidelines to ensure rating and pricing adequacy of the business 
  • Develop sustainable relationships with key wholesale brokers throughout the zonal framework. 
  • Develop and ensure effective utilization of detailed monitoring standards including quality reviews to assess underwriting results and loss ratios down to the account level 
  • Understanding of regulatory and compliance processes 
  • Establish strong relationships with Lexington leadership; create mutual understanding of overall parameters and goals to drive effective execution of business model. 
  • Develop tools and strategies, in collaboration with HR, to attract and retain top industry talent and develop high performing teams. 
  • Drive a culture that promotes collaboration, diversity and inclusion. 
  • Ensure a reputation of Claims excellence in the marketplace. 

What you'll need to succeed


  • At least 15 years insurance leadership experience in Property Insurance. 
  • Knowledge of market segmentation, portfolio management, acquisition and distribution 
  • Proven Strategic Leadership skills in developing vision and purpose, driving for results and leading effective teams 
  • Established strong relationships with brokers 
  • Skilled leader of change; versatile, client focused, results oriented 
  • Demonstrated business savvy, analytical and quantitative skills 
  • Expert technical underwriting background with advanced knowledge of first party insurance for all industries 
  • Strong problem solving and conflict resolution 

Ready to take your career to the next level? We would love to hear from you.
