Job.JobDescription:
Associate Actuary - Retail Excess Casualty

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as an Associate Actuary – Retail Excess Casualty to take on key responsibilities within a world-class actuarial function.


Make your mark in Actuarial

Our Actuaries are on the front lines, quantifying risk, pricing insurance and reserving losses for AIG’s major insurance operating companies, globally. We collaborate with Finance, Claims, Operations, Marketing and Risk Management, among other functions. As an AIG actuary, you will be challenged and encouraged to reach your greatest potential to help improve how we predict, manage and mitigate risk.


How you will create an impact
We are seeking an actuary with industry expertise to support the Pricing function within our Retail Excess Casualty segment.  The position involves profitability analysis/ deep dive, rater development and maintenance, large accounts pricing review, monthly business KPI reporting, assisting with annual budget and setting portfolio strategy.  Additional duties include quarterly earnings-related reporting, business AvE, diagnostics and large loss reporting.   They will partner with other actuaries in implementing best practices, analytical techniques and assessing the impact of loss trends and claims emergence.   Also, they will be responsible for one direct report.


    • Collaborate with underwriting to develop pricing, underwriting strategies, identify pockets of profitable growth opportunities and future underwriting actions.
    • Support the business review process and portfolio deep dives, which include reviewing underwriting actions impacting loss ratios to access impact on current and future performance.
    • Ensure accuracy of quoting and rating systems by working with Underwriters.
    • Ensure execution of rate level indications, portfolio profitability exercise and rate reviews within planned time frame
    • Collaborate with data team to drive process improvement and achieve actuarial transformation goals
    • Development and production of premium adequacy reports and budget loss ratio estimates for various segments.
    • Perform peer review for actuarial work products.
    • Communicate with and advise Retail Excess actuarial lead, underwriters, comptrollers, claims department. 
    • Work effectively as part of a team and train junior staff to achieve AIG’s financial, strategic and operational objectives

What we are looking for

    • BS in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or related area
    • ACAS preferred or close
    • +5 years or more experience in commercial casualty pricing preferred
    • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
    • Work well both independently and as part of a team
    • Proficiency in Excel, SQL, SAS, Python, R, or other programming languages preferred
    • Strong business and collaboration skills and responsive to service needs and operational demands
    • Effective time management skills
    • Strong communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills

The base salary range for this position is $120,00-$150,000 and the position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. In addition, we’re proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits Overview


Ready to set new industry standards? We would love to hear from you.

Job.JobDescription:
Associate Actuary - North America Property Pricing

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Associate Actuary - North America Property Pricing to take on key responsibilities within a world-class actuarial function.


Make your mark in Actuarial

Our Actuaries are on the front lines, quantifying risk, pricing insurance and reserving losses for AIG’s major insurance operating companies, globally. We collaborate with Finance, Claims, Operations, Marketing and Risk Management, among other functions. As an AIG actuary, you will be challenged and encouraged to reach your greatest potential to help improve how we predict, manage and mitigate risk.


How you will create an impact
We are seeking an actuarial professional to support North America Property, including Retail, Lexington, and Canada.   The individual will work to streamline processes across the different Property segments. They will also partner with other pricing actuaries in implementing best practices analytical techniques, catastrophe modelers to incorporate results into pricing and quantify portfolio risk, and reserving actuaries in assessing the impact of loss trends and claims emergence. 


  • Work closely with the Chief Underwriting Office to develop pricing and underwriting strategies and identify pockets of opportunity for profitable growth as well as profitability-challenged areas.
  • Review the parameters in the pricing systems, actively work to improve the pricing systems, and monitor underwriter adherence to pricing procedures and methodologies
  • Coordinate pricing, planning, and accumulation management efforts with cat modeling team to ensure adequate risk-adjusted returns contemplating expected loss, reinsurance costs, and increased capital needs associated with cat-prone business
  • Develop analytical tools to help underwriters assess the risks posed by insureds, aligning the pricing framework across the different underwriting platforms and business classes written in Lexington’s property operations.
  • Work closely with reserving actuaries to understand sources of reserve development and ensure appropriate recognition of pricing and underwriting actions impacting those estimates. 
  • Provide recommendations on rating methodologies, parameters and tools to improve accuracy of technical pricing reflecting latest market and economic conditions and product offerings.
  • Ensure alignment of tools, reporting metrics and goals with other property teams organizationally to optimize team efficiency while maximizing value and consistency across the property portfolios

What we are looking for

  • At least an Associate of the Casualty Actuarial Society (ACAS)
  • At least 5 years of commercial lines actuarial experience, preferably with significant commercial property pricing experience.
  • Exceptional communication skills, including ability to develop and present clear and concise analysis and recommendations to senior management.
  • Willing and able to continuously learn and adapt in a dynamic and fast changing environment. 
  • Solid understanding of catastrophe modeling fundamentals
  • Timeliness and attention to detail.

For positions based in New York, the base salary range is $120,000-$150,000, for the positions based in New Jersey, the base range is $115,000-$148,000, and for positions based in Illinois, the base range is $110,000-145,000. In addition, the position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. In addition, we’re proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits Overview

Be A Part Of Something Groundbreaking 


 AIG is seeking a detail oriented and proactive Data Privacy professional to support the organization's commitment to protecting personal information. This role is responsible ensuring compliance with global data protection regulations, managing privacy risk and promoting best practices across the business. The successful candidate will collaborate with cross functional teams to strengthen privacy governance, support regulatory requirements and help maintain customer and stakeholder trust through effective data protection practices.   

How you will create an impact


  • Providing advice and guidance to business units and corporate functions on Privacy program risks.
  • Maintaining current knowledge of Americas laws and regulations relating to Privacy governance, operational and compliance risks, and implementing appropriate changes to existing policies, standards and compliance programs.
  • Participating as a key resource in AIG’s Privacy Governance structure, including responsibilities relating to individual data subject rights, regulatory and individual notifications, records of data processing activities, privacy notice review, and Privacy Impact Assessments.
  • Participating in the development, implementation and maintenance of policies, standards, procedures, assessment processes and response plans, and related team contact information.
  • Interacting with Legal and Compliance stakeholders, and other liaisons;
  • Developing and reviewing privacy training program content.
  • Participating in the development and implementation of ongoing monitoring of Privacy risk programs.
  • Coordinating approvals for eDiscovery and other forensic investigations; working on the review and completion of the Global Compliance Risk Control Self-Assessment process for Americas Privacy.
  • Assisting the other members of the Global Privacy Team with the management, operation and maintenance of regional Privacy Team networks and Privacy Risk Incident (“PRI”) response plans in Americas.
  • Participate in the assessment, supervision and fulfilment of legal and compliance actions to be undertaken prior to new technology, cloud and mobile app implementations.

What We Are Looking For

  • Previous Privacy experience required, such as relevant experience as a privacy professional, risk officer, or compliance officer in a corporate environment.
  • Demonstrable experience in designing and implementing new privacy processes and procedures.
  • Ability to record and disseminate complex information in succinct and meaningful summaries.
  • Analytical skills, with an inquisitive mind to explore data and identify critical issues and trends.
  • Competency with Microsoft Office 365 products Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint, and other data repository and presentation tools.
  • Interest in new technology, devices, apps, Internet of Things, data science, Artificial Intelligence and other uses of data.
  • Excellent relationship management, empathic and with influencing skills demonstrated at all levels of the organization.
  • Team player and builder, supporting members of the team to attain their goals and objectives as a group.
  • Confident, engaging, authoritative and pragmatic approach.
  • Excellent communication skills, dynamic speaker and presenter, with ability to adapt style and approach appropriate to the situation.
  • Proven organizational, prioritization and forward planning skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail.
  • Self-motivated, enthusiastic and consistent focus on business goals.
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Qualifications

  • At least five years of privacy experience
  • IAPP certifications preferred (CIPP/E, CIPP/US, CIPM)
  • Previous experience working with diverse teams across Americas a plus

Casualty Specialist III

Make your mark in Claims.

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency. 

The ideal candidate possesses advanced technical expertise in coverage analysis, liability assessment, reserve management, litigation strategy, and claim resolution. Working independently and exercising a high degree of judgment, the Complex Claims Director partners closely with insureds, brokers, underwriters, defense counsel, and senior business leaders to develop effective claim strategies, mitigate risk, and achieve timely, cost-effective outcomes. This role serves as a technical leader within the claims organization and is expected to provide insight, guidance, and strategic direction on high-profile and complex matters.

What you need to know:

As a Claims Specialist III, you will manage and investigate moderate-complexity general liability and trucking liability claims, including litigated bodily injury and property damage exposures. This role is responsible for delivering timely, fair, and cost-effective claim resolutions while ensuring compliance with company standards, industry best practices, and client service expectations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Investigate, evaluate, and manage general liability, commercial auto, and trucking claims, including bodily injury, property damage, and litigation-related exposures.
  • Conduct timely and thorough investigations, including analysis of accident reports, witness statements, police reports, medical records, driver qualification files,
  • Develop and execute strategic action plans designed to achieve prompt and cost-effective claim resolution.
  • Coordinate and direct independent adjusters, accident reconstruction experts, and other vendors while effectively managing expenses.
  • Analyze policy coverage and identify coverage concerns involving commercial auto, trucking, and general liability exposures; prepare coverage position letters and collaborate with coverage counsel as needed.
  • Evaluate liability, damages, and litigation risk, including comparative negligence and exposure analysis for transportation-related losses.
  • Partner with defense counsel to develop litigation strategies, monitor case progress, and drive favorable outcomes.
  • Maintain accurate and timely claim documentation, including clear analysis of coverage, liability, damages, reserves, and resolution strategies.
  • Manage claim diaries and meet all service, compliance, and reporting requirements.

What You'll Bring

  • 3+ years of General Liability, Commercial Auto, or Trucking Liability claims experience, including litigated bodily injury claims.
  • Experience handling transportation, commercial trucking, fleet, or motor carrier claims, including moderate-to-severe injury exposures.
  • Working knowledge of trucking and transportation regulations, including familiarity with FMCSA requirements a plus.
  • Demonstrated ability to evaluate liability, damages, and complex coverage scenarios and negotiate effective claim resolutions.
  • Strong litigation management skills and experience working with defense counsel, experts, and other claim professionals.
  • Effective decision-making and analytical skills, with the ability to assess exposure and establish appropriate reserves.
  • Proven ability to manage competing priorities and perform effectively in a flexible work environment.
  • A continuous-improvement mindset with the ability to leverage technology and data to improve claim outcomes.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, organizational, and relationship-management skills.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.
  • Multi State licensing a plus.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain required multi-state adjuster licenses within six months of hire.

The ideal candidate brings a strong background in commercial auto and trucking claims, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and has experience handling claims involving motor carriers, fleet operations, transportation litigation, and complex bodily injury exposures. They are comfortable partnering with clients, defense counsel, and experts to drive optimal claim outcomes while providing exceptional customer service.

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Senior Program Manager to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Programs
AIG underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, Multinational Clients, and High Net Worth individuals. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model, and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.

How you will create an impact

Program Manager reports directly to the (Senior Director). A Program Manager is highly motivated, results oriented problem solver who exemplifies a willingness to be flexible, learn on the job and maintain a “can do” attitude.  A Program Manager is responsible for the underwriting, marketing & portfolio management of each assigned Program.


As a Program Manager you will be responsible for:

  • Developing and negotiating business plans for each assigned program, including plans for new business, renewal rate management, expected retentions to position the division to achieve profit objectives. 
  • Participating in Underwriting Quality Reviews; conduct additional file reviews as needed.
  • Positioning program growth in jurisdictions that are deemed rate adequate and managing to the technically correct price.
  • Coordinating and ‘chair’ Stewardship meetings for assigned Programs.
  • Identifying and marketing new products to round out existing portfolios and incrementally enhance portfolio of products afforded to our clients. 
  • Incorporating data and analytics to closely manage all programs and position each to achieve their profitability objectives. 
  • Monitoring renewals, rate targets vs. achieved, retentions, trends, lost business, etc. on a monthly basis to assure achievement of business plan and profitability targets.
  • Resolve commission exceptions identified for assigned programs.
  • Understanding each assigned program:  the industries and their exposures to loss, updating program ‘eligibility’ and coverages afforded as needed to minimize adverse exposures to unanticipated loss. 
  • Actively identify training opportunities at the PA level to enhance their LOB knowledge and successfully guide Program Administrators in their execution on risk selection, pricing, coverage terms and conditions in a manner that is aligned with authorities granted by AIG.
  • Actively understanding and managing the authority delegated by the PA to the underwriters assigned to our program(s).
  • Oversight and monitor PA ‘peers review’ process.
  • Developing a strong working knowledge of AIG operating systems (rating and policy issuance) at the PA level.
  • Understanding, managing and minimizing AAL for each program.
  • Having a working knowledge of data feeds, affirming receipt of data in the required format and frequency.
  • Developing   line of business expertise for assigned Program(s).
  • Identifying trends in the program profiles, communicating & implementing appropriate measures by LOB in order to protect the portfolio and AIG from adverse exposures.
  • Demonstrating an understanding of industry changes and potential impact by r LOB through clearly articulated recommendations for actions during the account referral process.
  • Ensuring Program Administrator is meeting AIG’s underwriting expectations and is aligned with program business plans through the execution and management of their underwriting authority including the participation in file reviews, UQR Audits and Stewardship meetings.
  • Reviewing and approving account referrals that exceed the Program Administrator’s Authority.
  • Participating in insurance & industry specific association training/meetings to enhance knowledge by class of business to stay current with industry specific market trends as it pertains to assigned Program(s).
  • Collaborating with Actuarial, Accounting, Claims, Operations, Program Development, Risk Management and Underwriting as necessary.
  • Overseeing the implementation of new business programs assigned to you including coordination with Operations, IT and other functional support areas.
  • Maintaining current industry knowledge, market intelligence and competitor analysis through regular communication with assigned Program Administrator(s) and participation in external conferences, trade shows, etc.
  • Working with Product Development to address policy form enhancements, rule and rate changes.
  • Developing & providing superior customer service and maintaining strong working relationships with Program Administrator(s) to sustain portfolio profitability through regular on-site visits, conference calls, etc.

What you'll need to succeed

  • 10+ Years of Commercial Underwriting Experience focused on Multi Line Package portfolio management.
  • Ability to manage by influence demonstrating strong communication, relationship management, organizational and analytical skills.
  • Demonstrated proficiency on AIG policy rating/issuance platforms (i.e. Cover-All).
  • Working knowledge of ISO, Admitted and Non Admitted product execution.
  • Proven understanding of manuscript, admitted form language and policy coverage analysis.
  • Demonstrated ability to understand and work with analytical tools, reports and technology.
  • Ability to work in dynamic, rapidly changing environment, adapting to changing requirements and collaborating with a wide range of colleagues to quickly deliver solutions.
  • Willingness to be flexible, learn on the job, and maintain a can-do attitude.
  • Highly motivated and results-oriented, proven creative problem solver.
  • Very strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Travel – 30%

Ready to maximize your impact? We would love to hear from you.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Loss Control Consultant, Risk Management / Loss Control
Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Senior Field Risk Engineer to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Risk Engineering

Through our global, world-class engineering capabilities, AIG provides risk engineering and specialist services to help identify and reduce risks at AIG insured clients and properties. We perform comprehensive risk evaluations and recommend solutions that combine cutting-edge thinking and common-sense practicality to avoid or mitigate exposures. Our mission is to make a difference that directly contributes to our customers’ success. We also actively participate in, and contribute to, the development and fine-tuning of industry standards and codes.


How you will create an impact

·         Travel (~25% overnight) to conduct property loss prevention surveys at commercial facilities

o    Determine building construction and assess the impact of plastics on construction 

o    Analyze water supplies and sprinkler system demands to determine water supply and sprinkler system adequacy 

o    Identify occupancy hazards and assess the adequacy of their protection features

o    Identify and assess the impact of external exposures on a facility 

o    Determine fire and natural catastrophe loss estimates for a facility 

·         Conduct consultative visits at customer facilities 

·         Conduct plan reviews 

·         Witness fire protection equipment testing 

·         Document survey results in a data-driven report writing application 

·         Mentor and train lesser experienced staff 

What you’ll need to succeed

·         Bachelor’s degree in Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics  

·         Minimum five (5) years of highly protected risk, specialized industry and/or boiler and machinery field experience 

·         Knowledge of a wide range of occupancies

·         Strong communicator (both oral and written)  

·         Position is expected to travel and attend meetings at various office, field, and construction sites 


Strengths for the position:

Soft Skills:

  • Highly motivated and works well without close supervision.
  • The individual must be able to make decisions with and without established guidelines and to provide technical support to underwriters and clients.   
  • Ability to work closely with various Account Teams including Account Engineers and Underwriters 
  • Ability to complete assignments on-time. 

Hard Skills:

  • Professional Engineer or Certified Fire Protection Specialist Designation (desired but not required). 
  • Ability to perform inspections of buildings and other structures, both visually and with instruments 
  • Ability to read construction drawings, diagrams, printed materials
  • Possess at minimum of at least one year of driving experience with a valid U.S. driver’s license  

Additional Requirements:

  • Ability to perform physical activities required for the position (i.e., be on feet and walking 8-10 hours a day, safely work at heights) 
  • Ability to understand and appreciate safety training specific to numerous workplace and construction hazards 
  • Ability to safely use ladders, scaffolds, lifts and other access equipment
  • Ability to lift and carry materials and equipment up to 50 lbs
  • Ability to perform work in the outdoors
  • Ability to wear safety equipment required for the position (hard hat, safety shoes, safety glasses and hearing protection)
  • Ability to safely work in a variety of occupationally hazardous locations
  • Ability to type at a computer for several hours a day
  • Ability to drive and safely operate a motor vehicle

Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as an Underwriter I, Specialty Energy Middle Market to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Underwriting, Specialty Energy Middle Market


AIG underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, Multinational Clients, and High Net Worth individuals. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model, and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.


How you will create an impact

AIG is seeking a motivated Underwriter to contribute to our industry leading SEMM Retail Casualty team. AIG’s strong brand in the market has provided for strong growth and thus the need for underwriting resources. We consistently provide clients with innovative products, use of technology, and a world-class platform. Our underwriters constantly deliver in an ever-changing marketplace and world.  In this role, you will be responsible for underwriting and servicing an existing renewal book with assistance to other team members who will solicit new business opportunities. This role includes constant interaction with top nationwide, regional, local and wholesale brokers and insureds. Through this role, underwriters gain experience in a wide variety of coverages, client industries and specializations. This role underwrites NA Casualty Products under general supervision, issuing quote and policies while ensuring standards and compliance guidelines are met. These individuals will analyze information and have the opportunity to connect with clients and brokers.


  • The role will be responsible for underwriting a specific line of business within NA Casualty (i.e. Environmental, Excess or Primary Casualty, NA Auto, WC, AL, GL, DBA, Foreign Casualty)
  • Evaluating, prioritizing and selecting submissions to be underwritten.
  • Identifying risk exposures, special or common hazards, claims experience and appropriate controls.
  • Analyzing claims and quantifying losses.
  • Adhering to guidelines and underwriting discipline to minimize exposure and appropriately price risks.
  •  Ensuring underwriting files and services standards and compliance guidelines are adhered to on assigned accounts.
  • Offering coverage, terms and conditions which generate a profit for the Company while meeting the needs of the customer.
  • Capturing market intelligence and broker feedback on accounts.
  • Begin demonstrating technical expertise with product(s) in the Financial Lines portfolio.
  • Providing superior customer service to brokers and clients (internal & external).


What you'll need to succeed


  • 1+ years of relevant professional experience; Insurance experience preferred.
  • Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university, preferred
  • Working knowledge of financial statements and analysis.
  • Excellent interpersonal, communication and analytical skills.
  • Excellent organizational skills and ability to handle multiple tasks in a high-volume, fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to work in dynamic, rapidly changing environment, adapting to changing requirements and collaborating with a wide range of colleagues to quickly deliver solutions.
  • Ability to facilitate cross-function collaboration, especially regarding technical aspects.
  • Detail-oriented with demonstrated ability to self-direct, prioritize work, and meet deadlines.
  • Takes initiative on projects and assignments, seeks alternate solutions when necessary.
  • Highly motivated and results-oriented.
  • Exposure to NA Casualty products is preferred. (i.e. Environmental, Excess or Primary Casualty, NA Auto, WC, AL, GL, DBA, Foreign Casualty).

Claims Intake Analyst (FNOL)


At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk.  Join us as a Claims Intake Analyst (FNOL) in the Claims Department to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Claims


Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency. 


How you will create an impact


This role is responsible for handling initial claim reports from policyholders, agents and third parties and ensuring timely and accurate claim setup into claims management system to facilitate smooth claims processing.  Some of the key responsibilities of this position include:


Key Responsibilities

  • Monitor FNOL inbox.
  • Capture complete and accurate information about incidents, damage and parties involved into claims management system with high accuracy.
  • Create detailed, clear notes documenting claims information.
  • Assign claims to appropriate team based on claim types and complexity.
  • Assists with claims payments occasionally.
  • Identify potential fraud indicators and escalate appropriately.
  • Follow established workflows and procedures.
  • Meeting productivity targets while maintaining accuracy standards.
  • Participate in quality assurance reviews.
  • Any other job related responsibility / project required by AIG.

What you’ll need to succeed


The ideal candidate should enjoy working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment with constant change and possess the following skills:    


Qualifications

  • Associate's degree or equivalent of a combination of experience and studies.

Snowflake Platform Leader

Responsibilities

  • Hire and retain world class talent to deliver Snowflake platform projects

  • Expertise in Snowflake management, internals, billing, query tuning.

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a the Director of Warranty Data Governance to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Warranty


AIG Warranty delivers a full range of service solutions including warranty management administration, extended service contracts and mobile insurance theft/loss programs, customer service support, service network management, claims processing services, and service contract underwriting. With over 20 years of experience, we are one of the Warranty and Service industry's leading providers, which is why many of the world's largest and most respected brands choose us. When retailers or manufacturers want flexible and innovative service solutions that will ensure the focus of building customer retention and customer satisfaction, they turn to us.


The Director Warranty Data Governance is a critical role within the division of US Warranty that will report directly into the Head of Underwriting US Warranty, General Insurance. The role is responsible for the governance, oversight, and management of all data related activities for Warranty North America including training and development of the data subject matter experts and data stewards committee, oversight of data controls and quality of data, report development, and matters related to business intelligence. The position ensures that all Warranty Operations adheres to the General Insurance data governance bulletins, standards, policies, procedures, and guidelines while operating within approved limits and best practices for the Warranty data operating model.


The candidate is responsible for leading a team of data analysts with cross-functional team oversight. The successful candidate should have previous experience in leading a team of data analysts, supporting offshore or near shore teams, and have influence over operational units to support the enterprise. This position will oversee the Warranty data operations and business intelligence strategy for a high transactional business unit within the General Insurance business unit at AIG. The successful candidate will meet the following criteria:


How you will create an impact


  • Previously led a data support and business intelligence team or teams or have other translatable data management experience.
  • Provide input into the general operating budget process and IT budget strategy.
  • Fiscally responsible for both creating and adhering to operational budgets and ROI tracking.
  • Maintain and provide expertise in data strategy efforts including data warehousing, data lakes, or other data storage and recall techniques.
  • Manage day-to-day data operations including data management support tickets and other reporting or business intelligence needs.
  • Train and mentor team and business units on best practices for driving a culture of data excellence.
  • Participate in business reviews as-needed with clients and senior leadership.
  • Proactively identify data and process improvements. 
  • Make recommendations to bring about efficiency and change.
  • Maintain good working relationship with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Focus on continuous improvement to offer the best-in-class service.
  • Strong communication skills.
  • Perform additional managerial and leadership duties as assigned.

What you'll need to succeed


  • Strong working PC knowledge – Microsoft Word, Excel, Access, Outlook, Power Point and Visio.
  • Can apply systems thinking to generate solutions, focus on process rather than isolated events to identify root cause, and evaluate alternative solutions.
  • Exhibit a “can-do” attitude approach and inspire others to excel. 
  • Prior experience and an understanding of digitization and technology transformation.
  • Able to perform in a fast-paced environment and perform a wide variety of tasks and change focus quickly as internal and external demands change.
  • Understands virtual and remote management best practices.
  • Experience with cloud data and AI ecosystems (Azure, AWS, and CoPilot) and common platforms/tools (Snowflake, SSRS, Power BI, and SSAS).
  • Familiarity with Data Governance and Responsible AI practices (e.g., data quality, privacy, security, data modeling, etc)
  • Understanding of Warranty or Insurance products is strongly recommended.
  • Previous experience in supporting internal and external data audits.
  • Understanding of technology product delivery and product roadmaps.
  • Ability to process map, document, and build models/presentations of current and future state data strategies.
  • Advanced understanding of data gathering and manipulation is preferred.
  • Has previously led on and offshore data teams.
  • Advanced to expert experience with SQL, PowerBI, SSAS, SSRS, AWS Cloud, SharePoint, Teams, and other relevant tools and environments
  • Master’s degree in Business, Information Technology, Data Sciences or Analytics, or other related fields is preferred.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Technology, Data Sciences or Analytics, or other related fields is required.
  • A proven track record of five years or more in leadership
  • Equivalent work experience of five years or more will be considered in lieu of educational requirement.

SM - Sales & MarketingService Net Warranty, LLC

Who we are

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance in approximately 70 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets and manage risks.

We’re also committed to making a positive difference for our colleagues and in the communities where we work and live. We encourage colleagues to give back to the causes they care most about, supporting these efforts through our Volunteer Time Off and Matching Grants Programs.


Get to know the business


At AIG, technology is at the heart of everything we do, from underwriting risks to processing claims. The Information Technology team equips our colleagues with the latest tools to complete their work efficiently and with the highest standards of excellence. The team is responsible for shielding the company’s systems from security risks, while designing technology strategies that enable AIG’s businesses to achieve their goals. AIG’s Information Technology functions include enterprise architecture, software and systems engineering, cybersecurity, and technology risk and compliance.


About the role


The Identity and Access Management (IAM) team at AIG is seeking a highly skilled IAM engineer with expertise in the Idira (CyberArk) vaulting solutions and strong system integration skills.  As the IAM Principal Privileged Access Engineer, you will play a critical role in designing, implementing, and maintaining our enterprise IAM infrastructure for Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions.


  • Own the PAM technical architecture, platform standards, and engineering roadmap — defining how the PAM solution and complementary technologies are deployed, integrated, and evolved across the enterprise.
  • Architect integrations between the PAM solution stack and adjacent systems: Entra ID / Active Directory, SIEM/ITDR platforms, cloud IAM (AWS, Azure, GCP), ticketing systems (ServiceNow), and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Evaluate and recommend emerging PAM, ISPM, and NHI tooling to inform investment decisions and platform strategy.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to gather IAM requirements and translate them into technical solutions.
  • Responsible for the configuration and deployment of vault, safes, platforms, workflows, connectors, automations, and other components to support account lifecycle protection and compliance with regulations.
  • Manage integrations from the PAM solution with various systems and applications, including but not limited to Active Directory, servers, databases, mainframes, and other applications.
  • Implement and maintain password policies and platforms and corresponding account password management within the PAM solution.
  • Collaborate with infrastructure, application, and development teams to ensure smooth integration of IAM solutions via API protocols.
  • Conduct integration testing to verify the functionality, performance, and security of IAM solutions.
  • Stay current with industry best practices and emerging trends in IAM and contribute to the continuous improvement of IAM processes and technologies.

What we’re looking for


  • 10+ years of in-depth IT experience with designing, developing, and supporting PAM solutions with several years focused on IAM solutions (specifically Idira, CyberArk).
  • 10+ years of experience deploying and configuring common Idira PAM (CyberArk) connectors and plug-ins, including Active Directory (AD), Azure AD, servers, databases, mainframe, and other applications as well as creating custom connectors.
  • Familiar with software development lifecycles (SDLC) and Agile development methodologies.
  • Intellectual curiosity about the evolving NHI, agentic AI, and cloud identity security landscape — and a bias toward building program capability ahead of the threat
  • Candidates must possess excellent verbal communication, decision making and customer service skills.
  • Ability to work in a team environment, adapt quickly to change and learn new applications or environments is required.
  • Must be highly organized and maintain quality work while meeting deadlines.
  • Extreme attention to detail is necessary due to audit and regulatory requirements.
  • Proven experience in integration testing, ensuring the seamless integration of IAM solutions with various systems and applications.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to troubleshoot complex technical issues.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.
  • Proactive and self-motivated with the ability to work independently and manage multiple tasks simultaneously.
  • Valid Guardian certification in Idira (CyberArk) preferred
  • Bachelor's degree in a Cybersecurity, Information Technology, or related field, such as Computer Science or Information Technology.

Job.JobTitle: Assistant Regional Underwriting Manager, Professional Liability/Cyber, Financial Lines
Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as Assistant Regional Underwriting Manager, Professional Liability/Cyber, Financial Lines to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make you mark in Underwriting


AIG Underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial

Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, and Multinational Clients. We are

reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model

and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the

full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance

professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.


How you will create an impact

  • Able to exercise judgment, negotiate and make sound business decisions effectively based on increased level of authority.
  • Deliver profitable growth through effective risk selection; execute on rate, coverage and limits management strategies; drive targeted correction or remediation strategies as needed
  • Responsible for helping to assign and manage the work of a team of underwriters
  • Monitor the adherence to underwriting requirements and guidelines for assigned book of business
  • Support the delivery of consistent underwriting best practices, in accordance with underwriting guidelines, to ensure rating, pricing, profitability, and structuring adequacy
  • Assist underwriters in executing strategic initiatives; provide support and develop solutions to their issues/concerns (system, guidelines, training, reports, new project request, product amendments)
  • Serve as referral point for field underwriting staff within stated authority; apply knowledge of market and industry to provide guidance on complex risks, exposures, and decisions
  • Stay abreast of developments in competitive and risk landscapes to determine effect on renewals and new business opportunities
  • Provide superior customer service to brokers and clients
  • Develop strong, long term relationships with brokers and clients to profitably grow a book of business
  • Work collaboratively with all members of the North America Financial Lines leadership team as well as Actuarial, Legal and Claims departments
  • Promote a healthy risk culture through staff meetings, trainings, and promotion of regular risk reporting
  • Help create a culture that promotes collaboration, innovation, diversity and inclusion; successfully conduct talent acquisition, employee engagement and performance monitoring/evaluation work
  • Serve as role model to all colleagues, leading by example as a senior member of the team

What you'll need to succeed

  • Strategic orientation, managing vision and purpose, developing organizational capability
  • Commercial in approach; goal-oriented but flexible enough to value different methods of achievement
  • Strong influencing and communications skills; able to work across multiple areas both internally and externally
  • Demonstrable experience formulating initiatives that support broader organizational aims
  • Experienced in building relationships externally and internally and managing key stakeholder relationships at executive and board level and with clients
  • Highly developed leadership skills that inspire teams to realize their potential
  • Ability to challenge effectively both people and portfolio strategy with the ability to effect change where appropriate
  • External thought leadership

Technical Skills and Experience

  • 7+ years of Financial Lines Underwriting, Agency or Brokerage experience
  • Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university
  • Advanced knowledge of the Financial Lines business (D&O, EPL, PTL, Fidelity) including product features, forms, regulatory environment and risks
  • Strong ability to identify, analyze and solve problems as well as the ability to learn rapidly, adapt quickly to change, exercise influence, and manage and prioritize multiple concurrent projects
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to work in s dynamic, rapidly changing environment, adapting to changing requirements and collaborating with a wide range of colleagues to quickly deliver solutions
  • Proficient with underwriting analytical tools and technology
  • Collegial and collaborative in approach and style
  • Understanding of how to be effective within a matrixed structure
  • Ability to adapt quickly in an evolving market
  • Approaches a challenge with a “can-do” attitude
  • Available to travel when required

Ready to make a bigger impact? We look forward to reviewing your application.


For positions based in Los Angeles, California, the base salary range is $150,000-$190,000 and the position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. In addition, we’re proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits Overview.

Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as Head of Energy, US South - Specialty Underwriting to play your part in that transformation and drive business growth. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Underwriting

AIG Underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, and Multinational Clients. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.

Your contribution at AIG:

The quality of Senior Leadership is a defining factor for a company’s success. Senior Leaders are responsible for developing business strategies and/or translating those strategies into meaningful outcomes and ultimately, business results.  As a Senior Leader, you reach across geographical and functional boundaries to create alliances that further the organization’s objectives and market position. Your deep and broad industry knowledge allows you to foresee external conditions that could potentially affect AIG’s future.


How you will make an impact

  • Manages all Divisional Underwriting for AIG’s South region, with national scope for Oil & Petrochemicals (Downstream), and North America scope for the Upstream line.  Establishes, implements, and evaluates production and profitability goals.
  • Direct accountability for the business results for the South region and the Upstream line with respect to profitability, penetration and/or volume.
  • Responsible for developing strategic client and broker relationships.
  • Represents AIG at industry events and seeks opportunities for speaking engagements to further AIG’s reputation in the Energy and Upstream/Downstream space.
  • In partnership with the Global Product Line Executives for O&P and Upstream, drive and execute the long-term business strategy for the US.
  • Serve as a technical expert, exercising technical authority with regards to the Downstream and Upstream lines within NA Energy.
  • Oversee multiple managers and senior underwriters; makes decisions regarding pay, performance management, development, employment, and staffing.

LEADERSHIP SKILLS:

  • Strategic orientation, managing vision and purpose, developing organizational capability.
  • Talent assessment and development for bench strength and succession planning.
  • Proven collaborative leadership skills.
  • Strong influencing and communications skills and ability to work across multiple areas of company and industries.
  • Change management and team leadership.
  • External thought leadership.

What you will need to succeed

  • Broad based insurance industry experience
  • Preferred minimum of 15+ years of insurance operational management experience
  • Knowledge of Energy market segmentation, portfolio management, acquisition and distribution
  • Process and system skills
  • Strategic orientation, managing vision and purpose, developing organizational capability
  • Strong influencing and communications skills and ability to work across multiple areas of company and industries
  • Change and team leadership, as well as external thought leadership

Ready to put your ideas into action? We would love to hear from you.

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Technical Solutioning Engineer to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Make your mark in Information Technology

At AIG, technology is at the heart of everything we do, from underwriting risks to processing claims. The Information Technology (IT) team equips our colleagues with the latest tools to complete their work efficiently, with the highest standards of excellence. The team is responsible for shielding the company’s systems from security risks, while designing technology strategies that enable AIG’s businesses to achieve their goals. Innovation in IT drives innovation across the organization.

How you will create an impact

AIG is seeking a Vice President of Application Engineering to lead our technology transformation. This is a high-impact role within the Global Insurance Technology organization, centered on bridging the gap between complex business strategy and technical execution.

You will ensure our global technology landscape is scalable, simplified, and optimized. You will act as the strategic technical architect of delivery, ensuring every technical initiative translates into measurable business value, aligned to AIG technology standards.

You will be the primary bridge between Solution Architecture, Engineering, and Business stakeholders to ensure technical feasibility and strategic alignment. Translate high-level strategic intent into actionable, high-quality engineering solutions throughout the entire delivery lifecycle. Champion engineering standards that prioritize scalability and efficiency, moving the needle on AIG’s long-term digital vision, including Gen AI. Partner with Technology and Business leadership to navigate the transformation agenda and optimize global outcomes.

  • Develop and maintain an aspirational technical architectural road map for the organization, define technology strategy and technical architecture decisions for strategic programs
  • Lead and Deliver technical architecture solutions in alignment with GI IT and business objectives
  • Leads the end-to-end  technical architecture for a region or 1-2 critical business applications or leads a core technical domain architecture areas
  • Oversees end-to-end technical architecture for a country's specific applications, or lead technical architecture for several large or mid-sized business applications, or oversee components of Functional or Technical Domain architecture
  • Partner with regional stakeholders and governing boards to enforce technical architecture standards
  • Drives IT strategy, current, transitional and target state technical architectures and roadmaps for a technical domain across lines of business that align to enterprise, technical and other functional domain standards, including Cloud and hosting, security, data, integration, frameworks, devops, automation, productivity services and tools, application lifecycle services
  • Initiate and deliver technology evaluations and recommendations
  • Gain Insurance organizational commitment for enterprise level architecture and infrastructure initiatives
  • Deploy and maintain the technical architecture repository for technology standards, best practices and tool sets
  • Ensure compliance to Enterprise and General Insurance technical architectural standards, policies and practices
  • Maintain in-depth knowledge of IT industry best practices, technologies, architectures and emerging technologies

What you'll need to succeed

 

  • 10–15+ years of experience in application engineering and technology management, preferably within large-scale global enterprises or the financial services/insurance sector.
  • A strong foundation in modern engineering practices, cloud-native architecture, and the delivery of complex, scalable software systems.
  • Proven track record of leading large-scale technology migrations or architectural shifts.
  • Exceptional ability to articulate complex technical concepts to non-technical business partners and other senior leaders.
  • A disciplined approach to working under tight deadlines and managing high-pressure delivery cycles without sacrificing quality.
  • Strong ability to partner with analysis teams to refine business requirements into technical roadmaps. Applying modern engineering standards, cloud-native architectures, and automation to drive performance, reliability, and speed to market. Help foster a culture of learning, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
  • Strong understanding of AWS, Azure, Google CLOUD services, and their use in designing secure, scalable application platforms. Working knowledge of Generative AI (preferred) from application and security perspective. Working knowledge of languages, and application Frameworks.
  • Hands on experience in open-source code and frameworks, Micro services Architecture, Angular/ React, Java/ J2EE, Relational DBs, NoSQL DBs such as MongoDB. Some development experience preferred.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or related field.
  • Certifications desired, not mandatory – TOGAF, AWS, Leeds, CISSP, CCC, SAFe for architects etc

 

Ready to make a bigger impact? We look forward to reviewing your application.

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Senior Executive Underwriter to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Job.JobTitle: Lead Business Analyst: Data Office - Actuarial Data & Tools
Job.JobDescription:
American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance in approximately 70 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets and manage risks.


At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as Lead Business Analyst – Actuarial Commercial Lines to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make Your Mark: 

General Insurance is a leading provider of insurance products and services – focused on helping to manage risk for commercial and personal customers. We offer a broad range of products through a diversified, multi-channel distribution network, including one of the world’s most far-reaching property casualty networks.  The Data Office supports the overall General Insurance product by managing Data, Data Governance, and the presentation of the data (Business Intelligence Delivery).


How you will create an impact:


AIG is looking for a driven individual to assume a critical role within the Data Office. This role will work directly with the Actuarial and Data teams to ensure a clear understanding of data and analytics needs and priorities. In addition, the individual will hold Global Data Warehouse Product Ownership responsibilities, ensuring execution aligns with the highest business priorities and Data Office strategy, and that sunset opportunities are realized.


 About the Role

The Business Analyst – Actuarial, Commercial Lines role sits within the Global Data Office at the intersection of business strategy, data, and analytics, and works closely with Commercial Lines Actuarial Groups. The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of actuarial concepts (reserving, pricing, and risk assessment), proven data and analytics capabilities, excellent communication skills, and experience as an Agile Product Owner. In this role, you will translate complex actuarial business requirements into actionable data engineering specifications by collaborating directly with data development teams. As a trusted business partner and product owner within the Global Data Warehouse, this role will help shape how AIG uses data to make better decisions, simplify its analytics landscape, and focus investments where they matter most.

 

Responsibilities


Business Requirements: Lead deep, structured requirement sessions with senior actuaries to understand workflows, data nuances, and reporting needs, creating detailed functional specifications.


  • Stakeholder Management: Facilitate alignment across actuaries and Data Office teams on project priorities, project timelines, and management of the deliverables.
  • Product Owner for Data Platform & Tool Development: Develop roadmaps for actuarial data and tool development requirements and partner with data engineers to build and deploy them in timely manner.
  • Agile Development Leadership & Product Backlog Management
    • Lead Agile Ceremonies: Act as the Business Analyst Lead within an agile team, facilitating user story refinement, sprint planning, and daily scrums.
    • Backlog Grooming: Translate actuarial requirements (reserving, pricing, modeling) into actionable user stories, epics, and acceptance criteria for developers.
  • Data Governance & Quality: Ensure compliance with data standards and maintain rigorous documentation for data lineage, testing, and production changes.

What you'll need to succeed


  • Experience: 7+ years of experience in business analysis, actuarial tool design within the insurance/financial industry.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in actuarial science, Computer Science, Data Analytics, Mathematics, or related field.
  • Actuarial Knowledge: Strong understanding of Commercial Insurance actuarial concepts (e.g., reserving methods, pricing tools)
  • Data Proficiency: Experience with data environments, ETL and visualization tools
  • Leadership: Demonstrated experience leading Agile teams and managing product backlogs.
  • Soft Skills: Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Preferred Qualifications: Actuarial Credentials, actuarial exams, or deep understanding of actuarial reserving/pricing concepts. 

Ready to make a bigger impact? We look forward to reviewing your application.

Veterans are encouraged to apply.

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance in approximately 70 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets and manage risks.

We’re also committed to making a positive difference for our colleagues and in the communities where we work and live. We encourage colleagues to give back to the causes they care most about, supporting these efforts through our Volunteer Time Off and Matching Grants Programs.

General Insurance is a leading provider of insurance products and services for commercial and personal insurance customers. It includes one of the world’s most far-reaching property casualty networks. General Insurance offers a broad range of products to customers through a diversified, multichannel distribution network.


Make your mark in Information Technology


At AIG, technology is at the heart of everything we do, from underwriting risks to processing claims. The Information Technology team equips our employees with the latest tools to complete their work efficiently and with the highest standards of excellence. The team is responsible for shielding the company’s systems from security risks, while designing technology strategies that enable AIG’s businesses to achieve their goals. AIG’s Information Technology functions include application development and management, enterprise architecture, and technology risk and compliance.


How you will create impact: 


The Senior Software Developer will provide development support regarding the design, coding, testing, documentation, and the implementation of complex changes, relating to a variety of applications that support the Western World / Lexington businesses. In addition to working on development initiatives, the Software Developer will also be expected to be engaged on end user support, maintenance activities, vulnerability management, service improvement planning and ongoing SOX / IT Control support. The Senior Software Developer will work closely with other key IT Team Contacts (i.e. DBA Teams, IT Infrastructure, IAM, etc.), the Operations Team and with project leaders to ensure that all projects and deliverables are appropriately structured, developed according to the development standards and expectations are clearly managed. The Senior Software Developer will be responsible for the coordinating resources, ensuring clear and open planning and providing a core subject management expertise.


What you'll need to succeed:


  • Design, document, develop, and implement scalable, reliable and maintainable software products that meet the requirements of the business
  • Work closely with the development team to perform hands-on review of the code, and provide guidance for the team to incorporate best coding practices and standards
  • Collaborate closely with business stakeholders and other development team members to deliver products, clarify objectives, provide reliable estimates, formulate detailed delivery plans, determine scope, drive consensus, identify problems and recommend solutions.
  • Establish strong relationships with other development team members and key business stakeholders.
  • Authoring developer friendly documentation in relation to Runbooks, deployment plans, systems architecture etc.
  • Ensure communication of technical concepts to a non-technical audience.
  • Development and support of integration capabilities with other platforms, supporting the end-to-end processing of business.
  • Enforces security best practices in all aspect of the development lifecycle.
  • Working with the wider IT group to understand direction and other in-flight initiatives, facilitating a collaborative and shared understanding.
  • Provide end user support, ongoing maintenance to ensure service levels are maintained, with a focus on customer service and platform stability.
  • Ability to manage other software development resources and assist in IT planning exercises.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or Information Systems
  • 4+ years of experience in software development within the insurance industry
  • Proven technical proficiency in .Net, SQL Server, SSIS, JS, HTML, C#, Angular, Type Script
  • Experience with Dev-Ops practices and tools
  • Clear and confident communicator, ability to challenge and influence change at a strategic level.
  • Excellent experience with the development of software using a variety of frameworks, developing and consuming API’s, building robust and scalable applications in a complex environment.
  • Team player, ability to work effectively in challenging and complex environments
  • Excellent attention to detail with the ability to understand complex concepts.
  • Customer focused with a desire to deliver excellent customer service to business stakeholders
  • Detailed level of understanding of Cloud platforms

Reinsurance Accountant

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Reinsurance Accountant to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Make your mark in Finance

Our Finance team plays an essential role in maintaining a healthy balance sheet at AIG. It delivers significant finance support for the overall enterprise, optimizing operations, controllership, funding, and capital structure to honor our stakeholder commitments. The team’s work is invaluable to informing leadership decision making, complying with regulatory requirements, and maintaining financial discipline, transparency, and controls, while providing timely and meaningful information.

How you will create an impact

Reinsurance Operations & Cash Management

  • Collection of loss recoverable: Monitor, calculate and bill reinsurance claims (loss recoverable). Actively pursue collections from reinsurers and resolve billing disputes in a timely manner.
  • Payment of ceded premium: Calculate, verify, and process premium payments due to reinsurers based on treaty and facultative contract terms.
  • Account reconciliation: Reconcile assumed and ceded premium, commission, and loss accounts against reinsurance ledgers and broker statements

Financial & Statutory Reporting

  • Monthly/Quarterly closing: Prepare journal entries, monthly financial statements inputs, and variance analysis related to reinsurance assets, liabilities, and income items.
  • Statutory Schedule F: Lead the preparation, verification, and filing of Schedule F, ensuring accurate calculation of unauthorized reinsurance penalties, provision of reinsurance, and additional requirements.
  • Puerto Rico Regulatory Reports: Compile and submit mandatory financial reports required by the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance of Puerto Rico (OCS), ensuring alignment with both US GAAP and Statutory Accounting Principles (SAP).

Audit and Compliance

  • Assists internal and external auditors during annual financial audits and OCS regulatory examinations by providing necessary schedules, reconciliations, and contract documentation of reinsurance programs in place.
  • Monitor reinsurance contract terms and conditions to ensure accounting treatments match specific treaty triggers and clauses.
  • Maintain robust internal controls over reinsurance processes in compliance with Company’s control framework.

Any other additional/related job responsibilities required by AIG to support the Department and the Company.

What you’ll need to succeed

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance or a related business field is required.
  • This role is for candidates with experience in job-related tasks and within the Property and Casualty insurance or reinsurance sector.
  • Proven experience in supporting the preparation of Schedule F and navigating Puerto Rico OCS filing requirements.
  • Advanced proficiency in MS Excel (VLOOKUPs, pivot tables, complex data manipulation) and familiarity with accounting system SAP.
  • Skills to effectively interact with all levels of staff and management.
  • Strong communication skills to effectively manage relationships with international reinsurers, brokers, and local regulatory bodies.
  • Time management, customer service and attention to details skills.
  • Fully bilingual in English and Spanish (written and verbal) is required for interacting with local regulators and global reinsurance partners.
  • Analytical and problem-solving capabilities to be able to identify trends, investigate discrepancies in broker statements, and interpret reinsurance contract wording.  
  • Ability to multitask with a variety of systems and processes.

Job.JobTitle: Underwriting Specialist, Specialty Energy Middle Market, (SEMM)
Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as an Underwriting Specialist, SEMM, Retail Casualty to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


AIG underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, Multinational Clients, and High Net Worth individuals. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model, and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.


How you will create an impact


The Underwriting Specialist will handle accounts/clients that are most complex and be responsible for underwriting an Admitted Casualty portfolio.

Develops and manages underwriting strategies for both renewals and prospects within his/her portfolio of accounts. This includes knowledge of the current market penetration of NA Casualty products and the development of specific plans to increase portfolio share. 

Develops and implements negotiation strategies.  Makes independent sales calls to market and cross-market products.  Identifies target markets, designs and implements strategies for lead development and builds prospect lists.  

  • Provides technical direction to management, less senior specialists, producers, and claims adjusting personnel. 
  • Communicate risk appetite and NA Casualty Value Proposition to brokers. 
  • Collaborate with Distribution, Territory Managers, and other line(s) of business underwriters to target desirable accounts and cross selling opportunities from brokers.  
  • Rapidly evaluate, prioritize and select submissions to be underwritten.  
  • Recognize and create cross sell opportunities for other Commercial products.  
  • Work with broker to understand the deal structure, terms, and AIG Services that best meets clients’ needs. 
  • May review, evaluate and make recommendations to underwriting guidelines. 
  • May direct or conduct internal underwriting audits. 
  • Negotiate pricing, terms & conditions, and deal structure with brokers and clients.  
  • Participate in special underwriting projects as needed. 
  • Develop strong, long-term relationships with brokers and clients to profitably grow a book of business. 
  • Will identify cross selling opportunities. 
  • Provide superior customer service to brokers and clients. 


What you’ll need to succeed


  • Minimum 5 years of Commercial Insurance Company, Agency or Brokerage experience. 
  • Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university. 
  • Proven ability to build and maintain strong professional relationships.  
  • Advanced working knowledge of the NA Casualty lines of business including product features, forms, regulatory environments and risks etc. (i.e. Environmental, Excess or Primary Casualty, NA Auto, WC, AL, GL, DBA, Foreign Casualty)

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Senior Underwriter, North America Fronting to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


AIG underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, Multinational Clients, and High Net Worth individuals. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model, and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. This position is a Senior Underwriter for North America Fronting. Main focus will be the support and servicing of complex fronting accounts. How you will create an impact


Work closely with Captive Solutions Fronting Team and liaise with Product pillars to verify program structure and reinsurer details.

Perform sanctions and screening checks

Resolve account-related questions from internal peers and/or Clients/ Brokers that are within their scope; or escalate to leadership

Make independent sales calls to market and cross-market products. Refers declined business to other AIG divisions, as appropriate.

Participate in client (internal/external) conference calls.

Prepare for and help respond to all captive audits.

3+ yrs relevant experience, preferably within the insurance industry.

Proactive, highly motivated, well-organized, self-sufficient, and able to demonstrate the ability to work productively under minimum supervision

Excellent time management skills with ability to work with deadlines and be responsive and flexible to client needs and changes in program requirements

Ability to work in dynamic, rapidly changing environment, adapting to changing requirements and collaborating with a wide range of colleagues to deliver expected results.

Highly motivated and results-oriented, proven creative problem solver.

Demonstrated ability to understand and work with analytical tools, reports and technology.
