IT - Information TechnologyAIG Employee Services, Inc.

Be part of something groundbreaking 

At AIG, we are making long-term investments in a brand-new, innovative Generative AI team, designed to explore new possibilities for how artificial intelligence can be applied in insurance and beyond, and we need your help.  

With the support and investment needed to explore new frontiers in generative AI, you’ll be working alongside talented colleagues, innovating and leading projects that will transform how we manage risk and serve our customers.  

This team is central to our vision of the future and the core of our business offering. We will incorporate best-in-class engineering and product management principles and your guidance and collaboration will be critical to its success. To rapidly advance and innovate, we need your skills and expertise to build and scale world-class products. If you’re excited by the opportunity to create meaningful impact, we’d love to hear from you. 

Who we are 

AIG is a leading global insurance organization providing a wide range of property casualty insurance and other financial services. We provide world-class products and expertise to businesses and individuals in approximately 190 countries and jurisdictions.  

At AIG, we’re reshaping how the world manages risk, and we’re inviting you to be a key part of that transformation.

How you will create impact

As a Data Scientist at AIG, you will serve a critical role in the architecture, development, and delivery of impactful enterprise-level Generative AI solutions. We are seeking a highly technical individual contributor with extensive hands-on experience, as we are an applied data science team operating in an agile and production-oriented environment. You will be focused on Large Language Models (LLMs) and Machine Learning (ML), acting as a primary technical driver for our most complex projects.

Your Responsibilities

  • End-to-End Development: Lead the development and successful delivery of data science and generative AI solutions in accordance with business requirements.

  • Production Oversight: Monitor solutions in production to ensure performance, reliability, and accuracy.

  • Technical Collaboration: Partner with cross-functional teams including product managers, engineers, and business leaders to translate requirements into technical reality.

  • Evaluation & Quality: Build robust evaluation frameworks to measure LLM efficacy, manage ground truth dataset quality, and guide the product development roadmap.

  • Architecture: Design scalable ML pipelines and RAG frameworks that integrate seamlessly with enterprise data structures.

What is Needed to be Successful

  • 8+ years of Engineering Experience in a development environment

  • 6+ years of experience in a data science role, with a strong emphasis on NLP and ML, working in an agile production-oriented environment.

  • 3+ years of practical experience with open-source Large Language Models (Llama 3, Mixtral, etc.), including prompt engineering, inference optimization, and fine-tuning.

  • 3+ years of experience building Generative AI Solutions, including designing and building RAG frameworks, validation pipelines, observability, and monitoring solutions. 

  • Proven Delivery: Experience successfully delivering multiple GenAI, analytical, or ML projects from conception through to production.

  • Python Expertise: Strong, expert-level proficiency in Python and its data science ecosystem (e.g., PyTorch, Pandas, Scikit-learn).

  •  Education: Master’s degree in data science, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field.

Added Bonus / Preferred Qualifications

  • Palantir Platform Experience: Hands-on experience or certification in the Palantir platform (Foundry/AIP).

  • Ontology Mastery: A strong understanding of Ontology—specifically how to map complex real-world data entities and relationships into a digital twin framework to power AI applications.

  • Large-scale Data Infrastructure: Strong understanding of performance optimization in big data environments, with hands-on experience using distributed data processing frameworks such as Apache Spark or PySpark.

  • Agentic Solution: Experience implementing advanced agentic architectures, such as autonomous agents capable of multi-step reasoning and decision-making or integrating agentic solutions with large-scale enterprise systems. 

Required Competencies

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.

  • A "hands-on" mindset with the desire to be a primary technical lead through code quality and architectural excellence.

Ready to set new industry standards? We would love to hear from you.

Veterans are encouraged to apply.

If you’re looking for a place to grow your career and where your contributions will shape the future, AIG is where you belong.  

How you will create impact: 

As a Senior Full Stack Software Engineer for GenAI, you will lead the design, development, and operationalization of GenAI data pipelines that enable innovative AI models and analytics. You’ll collaborate across teams to deliver data solutions that drive business insights and value, all while ensuring scalability and sustainability. This is an exciting opportunity to shape the future of data engineering at AIG, guiding teams through complex data challenges and enabling AI-powered decision-making that will fuel business growth.  

Your responsibilities include: 

  • Collaborating with stakeholders to identify and deliver innovative data solutions that meet the evolving needs of the business. 

  • Mentoring and growing junior engineering talent

  • Designing, building and maintaining GenAI data pipelines across the business

  • Partnering with data architects and senior engineers to implement best practices, ensuring sustainable and scalable technical designs. 

  • Working closely with analytics, application development, and data science teams to foster collaboration and drive innovation. 

  • Leading the onboarding of new business lines to GenAI workflows

  • Delivering on-time, high-quality results on fast-paced schedules while maintaining rigorous standards for development and code management. 

 What is needed to be successful: 

  • Minimum of 7 years of professional software development experience.

  • Strong proficiency in at least one high-level programming language (Python, Typescript, Java JavaScript/React, etc.),

  • A strong background in Typescript is a plus but not required.

  • Write clean, efficient, and well-documented code.

  • Be curious and motivated to learn new things

  • Design, develop and implement data processing pipelines in Palantir Foundry. Prior experience in Foundry is a big plus but not required.

  • Experience with testing frameworks (pytest, unittest).

  • An understanding of containerization and compute optimization

  • Build and maintain scalable and reliable APIs to expose data and functionalities to other services and applications.

  • Identify and implement performance optimization for existing code and data processing workflows, including leveraging containerization technologies for parallel execution.

  • Contribute to the design and architecture of our data platform and applications.

  • Participate in code reviews to ensure code quality and adherence to best practices.

  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines

  • Experience setting up E2E Engineering pipeline, monitoring, and troubleshooting.

  • Have prior experience leading teams of engineers

 It would be nice if: 

  • You are passionate about exploring innovative AI and Generative AI technologies, using them to drive impactful solutions within large-scale enterprise environments. 

  • You have experience working with both internal and external teams to deliver best-in-class data engineering solutions, sharing knowledge and best practices across the organization. 

  • You enjoy working within the financial services or insurance industry and understand the unique data challenges these sectors face. 

Veterans are encouraged to apply.

Job.JobTitle: Senior Account Risk Engineer - Power Generation
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Loss Control Consultant, Risk Management / Loss Control
Job.JobDescription:
Join us as an Senior Account Risk Engineer to make more of your technical expertise and loss prevention insight.

Make your mark in Risk Engineering

AIG’s worldwide network of risk engineers work with clients, brokers and underwriters to help identify and improve risk globally for various energy sectors, including but not limited to: Power Generation, Renewable Energy, Oil and Petroleum, Chemical, Pharmaceutical, Upstream and Mining.  AIG’s experience, tools, guidelines and training elevate AIG to a leader in the industry, allowing us to better understand client risk and contribute specialized knowledge to help in identifying and mitigating risks.

How you will create an impact

Energy Risk Engineers are responsible for conducting loss control surveys, managing power generation accounts as an account engineer, working with underwriters, clients, and brokers to help identify and improve risk for various energy sectors, including but not limited to: Power Generation and Renewable Energy.  The Energy Risk Engineers are integral in allowing AIG to better understand exposures and contribute specialized knowledge to help in identifying and mitigating risks. This position is home-based with fieldwork conducted at insured facilities. 

  • Perform loss control inspections, desk top reviews, and account reviews for a wide range of Energy accounts

  • Determine key loss prevention attributes at various energy facilities

  • Evaluate hazards associated with various types of turbine generators, power generations equipment and renewable technology

  • Evaluate overall Management Programs and Maintenance Programs

  • Evaluate business interruption exposures including Contingent Business Interruption (CBI) and Interdependencies Business Interruption (IBI)

  • Determine building construction and assess construction characteristics as applicable

  • Analyze water supplies and sprinkler system demands to determine water supply and sprinkler system adequacy

  • Identify occupancy hazards and assess the adequacy of their protection features

  • Identify and assess the impact of external exposures on a facility

  • Determine fire and natural catastrophe loss estimates for a facility

  • Conduct consultative visits at customer facilities

  • Conduct plan reviews

  • Document survey results in a data-driven report writing application

  • Mentor and train lesser experienced staff

What you’ll need to succeed

  • Bachelor’s degree in Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics   

  • Minimum five (5) years of industry experience in Power Generation and Renewable Energy

  • Fluent in English and Spanish

  • Knowledge of a wide range of occupancies, exposures per best business practices 

  • Strong ability to identify, analyze and solve problems as well as the ability to learn rapidly, adapt quickly to change, exercise influence, and manage and prioritize multiple concurrent projects

  • Ability to work in a dynamic, rapidly changing environment, adapting to changing requirements and collaborating with a wide range of colleagues to quickly deliver solutions

  • Superb verbal and written communication skills

  • Position is expected to travel and attend meetings at various offices, fields, plants, facilities and construction sites . Approximately 50% travel through year - predominantly in the US and Latin America countries

Strengths for the position: 

Soft Skills: 

  • Strategic orientation, managing vision and purpose, developing organizational capability.

  • Goal-oriented but flexible enough to value different methods of achievement.

  • Strong influencing and communications skills; able to work across multiple areas both internally and externally.

  • Demonstrable experience formulating initiatives that support broader organizational aims.

  • Experienced in building relationships externally and internally and managing key stakeholder relationships.

  • The individual must be able to make decisions with and without established guidelines and to provide technical support to account engineers, underwriters, and clients.    

Hard Skills: 

  • Industry experience with real world knowledge of the challenges in the Energy sectors. 

  • Ability to perform inspections of Energy and Construction facilities, both visually and with instruments. 

  • Ability to read construction drawings, diagrams, printed materials.  

  • Possess at minimum of at least one year of driving experience with a valid driver’s license.   

Additional Requirements: 

  • Ability to perform physical activities required for the position (i.e., be on feet and walking 8-10 hours a day, safely work at heights).  

  • Ability to understand and appreciate safety training specific to numerous workplace and construction hazards.  

  • Ability to safely use ladders, scaffolds, lifts and other access equipment. 

  • Ability to lift and carry materials and equipment up to 50 lbs. 

  • Ability to perform work in the outdoors. 

  • Ability to wear safety equipment required for the position (hard hat, safety shoes, safety glasses and hearing protection). 

  • Ability to safely work in a variety of occupationally hazardous locations. 

  • Ability to type at a computer for several hours a day.  

  • Ability to drive and safely operate a motor vehicle. 

  • Current Passport

  • Fluent in English and Spanish

  • Hybrid

Job.JobTitle: Auto Property Damage Adjuster (Fast Track Representative)
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Property Claims Adjuster, Claims, Claims Adjuster
Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as an Auto Property Damage Adjuster (Fast Track Representative) to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Make your mark in Claims Stewardship

Our Claims professionals support AIG policyholders through some of the most trying times. When our clients face losses large and small, we step up to help them ease the financial burdens of catastrophic events like fires and hurricanes; we help them get their businesses back up and running again or recoup the value of a lost family heirloom or a prized possession. Our Claims team is an industry leader, drawing daily on its unparalleled levels of expertise to offer our clients the highest levels of stewardship to drive total cost of claim improvement and consistent outcomes. AIG manages claims using a wealth of technical and market knowledge about risks, business practices, and the ever-evolving legal and regulatory environment.

How you will create an impact

The role of an AIG Fast Track adjuster is to investigate, evaluate and resolve first and third party auto liability claims, minor injury claims and low complexity general liability losses. This requires accurate and thorough documentation, as well as completion of resolution action plans based upon the applicable law, coverage and supporting evidence.  Provides exceptional customer service and on going communication to the appropriate stake holders through the life of the claim. Performance Objectives:

  • Maintains high standards of customer service. This includes prompt contact and follow up to complete timely and accurate investigation, damage evaluation and claim resolution in accordance to regulatory and company standards.

  • Conducts a thorough investigation of coverage, liability and damages.  Must document facts and maintain evidence to support claim resolution.

  • Comply with all statutory and regulatory requirements in all applicable jurisdictions.

  • Establish appropriate loss and expense reserves with documented rationale. On going review of reserves required through life of file.

  • Demonstrates technical efficiency through timely, consistent execution of best claim handling practices and claim handling guidelines.

  • Communicates effectively with internal and external customers on claims and account issues.

  • Maintain and manage a diary system to efficiently manage and resolve assigned claim inventory.

  • Property and Casualty licenses required.  Must be obtained within 6 months of hire.

What you'll need to succeed

  • Bachelors’ degree or equivalent work experience.

  • 2 years previous claim handling experience preferred.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

  • Excellent customer service skills.

  • Analytical with good decision making skills.

  • Strong organizational skills and detail oriented.

  • Ability to work independently, handle multiple tasks simultaneously and exercise good judgment.

Ready to accelerate your career? We would love to hear from you.

Compensation for this position includes base salary and eligibility for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. In addition, we’re proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits

  • The role will be responsible for underwriting an Excess Casualty portfolio 
  • Develops and manages underwriting strategies for both renewals and prospects within his/her portfolio of accounts. This includes knowledge of the current market penetration of NA Casualty products and the development of specific plans to increase portfolio share. 
  • Develops and implements negotiation strategies.  Makes independent sales calls to market and cross-market products.  Identifies target markets, designs and implements strategies for lead development and builds prospect lists.  
  • Provides technical direction to management, less senior specialists, producers, and claims adjusting personnel. 
  • Communicate risk appetite and NA Casualty Value Proposition to brokers. 
  • Collaborate with Distribution, Territory Managers, and other line(s) of business underwriters to target desirable accounts and cross selling opportunities from brokers.  
  • Rapidly evaluate, prioritize and select submissions to be underwritten.

  • Work with broker to understand the deal structure, terms, and AIG Services that best meets clients’ needs. 
  • May review, evaluate and make recommendations to underwriting guidelines. 
  • May direct or conduct internal underwriting audits. 
  • Negotiate pricing, terms & conditions, and deal structure with brokers and clients.  
  • Participate in special underwriting projects as needed. 
  • Develop strong, long term relationships with brokers and clients to profitably grow a book of business. 
  • Will identify cross selling opportunities. 
  • Provide superior customer service to brokers and clients. 

What you’ll need to succeed

  • Minimum 5 years of Commercial Insurance Company, Agency or Brokerage experience. 
  • Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university. 
  • Proven ability to build and maintain strong professional relationships.  
  • Advanced working knowledge of the NA Casualty lines of business including product features, forms, regulatory environments and risks etc. (i.e. Environmental, Excess or Primary Casualty, NA Auto, WC, AL, GL, DBA, Foreign Casualty) 
  • Demonstrated sales, marketing, and relationship building experience. 
  • Very strong verbal and written communication skills. 
  • Highly motivated and results-oriented. 
  • Ability to work in dynamic, rapidly changing environment, adapting to changing requirements and collaborating with a wide range of colleagues to quickly deliver solutions. 
  • Willingness to be flexible, learn on the job, and maintain a can-do attitude.  
  • Expert with underwriting analytical tools and technology.

  • Ability to work closely with brokers to communicate risk appetite and our value proposition – and to understand the deal structures, terms and conditions and products that best meets clients’ needs.

Join us as a Complex Claims Director to grow your experience in Claims.

Make your mark in Claims

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency.

How you will create an impact

Are you interested in handling some of the largest and most complex claims in the industry? Your deep technical claims expertise will be put to the test in the investigation, evaluation and disposition of new and existing 3rd party property and casualty claims.  These multimillion-dollar claims include multi-vehicle auto accidents, plant explosions, class action injury claims, catastrophic product liability claims.  You will be required to review coverage under Excess Commercial General liability and auto policies, participate in the investigation of the claim and control litigation strategy.  The adjuster will be required to direct the litigation, attend mediations and trials, assess liability and damages, and recommend reserves.  It will be necessary for the adjuster to present the large value cases to senior management.  The adjuster will need excellent customer service skills in communicating with insureds, brokers, attorneys, and claimants.  Only the most highly skilled negotiators will succeed in resolving these claims in the toughest venues against the most elite plaintiff attorneys. 

  • Determining the scope and extent of available coverage.  
  • The investigation, evaluation and disposition of new and existing 3rd party property and casualty claims.
  • Preparation and execution of investigation strategies which identify critical issues effecting liability, causation and damages and assessment of risk transfer and contribution  opportunities.
  • Clear and concise communication and contact with internal and external customers, including insureds, brokers, and underwriters, to provide guidance and manage expectations.
  • Proper documentation of exposure evaluation and resolution strategy. 
  • Presentation to senior management of claim disposition recommendations.
  • Obtain the appropriate authority to independently negotiate multimillion-dollar claims with the top plaintiff attorneys nationwide. Document evaluation, thought process, and strategy. Utilize ADR as appropriate and necessary.
  • Effectively strategize and budget litigation of each claim through discussions with counsel, vendors, and insureds.  Establish with defense and coverage counsel clear ground rules to maintain financial control of budget and expenses.

What you’ll need to succeed

  • 5+ years of Commercial/Industry claims experience preferred
  • Excellent communication skills (verbal/written) and strong negotiation skills
  • Advanced experience and capabilities in litigation claims management including ADR and mediation process
  • Experience attending and controlling cases- pre-suit, litigated and post trial- at mediations, settlement conferences, etc.
  • Property and Casualty licenses required, must be obtained within 6 months.
  • Motivated individuals who are interested in the potential for an upwardly mobile career path.

Job.JobDescription:
Regional Product Specialist, Lexington Builders Risk

Lexington has an opportunity for a Regional Production Specialist on the U.S. Builders Risk team specializing in underwriting primary, shared and layered construction risks. The Regional Production Specialist is expected to work effectively in an independent manner to successfully manage his/her book of business of new and renewal production along with executing the profitability strategy for territory’s portfolio. A Regional Production Specialist must be able to illustrate sufficient technical analysis and underwriting acumen combined with marketing and sales skills to meet underwriting goals (i.e., achieve growth targets and maintain overall profitability). In addition, the ability to coach, train and develop staff to their fullest potential is required.

Make your mark in Underwriting

We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model, and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.

How you will create an impact

  • This is a key role in our Lexington Builders Risk team in which you will take ownership for achieving goals and outcomes. You will be tasked with overseeing a range of programs and processes, in addition to handling a portfolio of Master Builders Risk program renewals and new business made up of complex risks.
  • You will thrive by successfully balancing the needs of multiple stakeholders and making sound decisions using data, analysis, experience, judgment, and a risk mindset. It will be essential to build effective relationships with brokers and to deliver a high standard of customer service as an example for the team to follow.
  • You will promote a culture of collaboration, inclusivity, and learning while mentoring and developing colleagues through effective leadership, role modeling, and training programs. You will aim to facilitate personal growth and career development, supporting succession planning.
  • You will also play a key role in new business development, including attending broker events and building new relationships across the market. Handle a portfolio of Master Builders Risk program renewals and new business made up of complex risks.

What you’ll need to succeed:

  • Proven underwriting experience in US Builders Risk, Inland Marine, Construction or Property including product features, forms, regulatory environment, and risks etc. and a successful record of selling products to clients.
  • Deep technical expertise of Builder’s Risk as well as knowledge of the market, portfolio management, acquisition, and distribution
  • Strong communication, networking, and relationship-building skills.
  • Good organizational and time management skills.
  • Customer and sales-orientated behaviors: motivated, tenacious, focused, technically skilled, proactive, and accountable.

Ready to lead by example? We would love to hear from you.

For positions based in Chicago, New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, , the base salary range is $114,500 - $143,500 and the position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. In addition, we’re proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits Overview.

Job.JobDescription:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this role is to provide analysis, guidance, and direction for the management and resolution of corporate compliance and privacy-related matters. Reporting to the Director of Corporate Compliance, this position works closely with leaders in Law and Corporate Compliance and serves as a key resource for leaders and team members throughout the organization on privacy program requirements and corporate compliance functions.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Manages the company’s privacy program (under the direction of the department director), partnering with Information Security, insurance operations, finance, purchasing and vendor management, human resources, and other departments on privacy and cybersecurity compliance.
  • Oversees data events and incident response processes to support timely and appropriate resolution.
  • Maintains up to date knowledge of applicable privacy, AI, cybersecurity, data classification, data retention, and data protection laws and regulations across the U.S.
  • Supports general corporate compliance functions, including corporate policy management, conflict of interest administration, compliance risk assessments, data management, regulatory change management, compliance training, team member awareness, and enterprise-level compliance risk management.
  • Develops compliance workflows, key risk indicators, and metrics to support compliance risk management, regulatory readiness, and program maturity.
  • Participates in the development and drafting of corporate policies and policy-related materials, without use of AI.
  • Prepares departmental and executive-level reports on compliance risk management and assigned program activities. 
  • Interprets corporate policies, frameworks, and process documents within assigned areas of responsibility.
  • Promotes responsible innovation, practical compliance risk management, and accountable data management across the organization.
  • Mentors and assists in supervising the work of less experienced members of the department.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have formal supervisory responsibilities but will assist with providing mentorship and oversight to others.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent combination of education and experience) required.  Juris Doctorate (JD) preferred.  4+ years’ related experience required in privacy, corporate compliance or closely related area. Insurance industry experience is helpful.  Leadership experience, including direct people-management experience, is preferred.


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

None required. Certified Information Privacy Professional (CIPP) a plus.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Substantial, direct experience interpreting legal requirements for privacy program management and providing practical management-level guidance on consumer privacy and cybersecurity laws and regulations.
  • Excellent computer skills, including familiarity with corporate cybersecurity practices and an interest in AI governance.  GRC systems experience is helpful.
  • Familiarity with general corporate compliance functions, such as corporate policy management, conflict of interest principles, and compliance risk assessments.
  • Superior legal research and analytical skills, with careful attention to detail and the ability to provide guidance in complex, ambiguous situations.
  • Proven ability to translate complex statutory language into plain English reports, process guidance, policy statements, and training materials.
  • Demonstrated ability to work without relying on AI to produce high caliber analyses and written work product.
  • Excellent communication skills, including experience leading cross-functional meetings and presenting reports to leadership.
  • Strong problem-resolution skills, including experience with internal investigations and balancing compliance risk management needs with corporate priorities.
  • Client-oriented perspective, with a focus on timely, actionable guidance that responds to business needs.
  • Comfortable working in a growth-oriented environment with evolving regulatory requirements, uncertain legal interpretations, and organizational change.
  • Well-developed self-management skills, with the ability to work independently with minimal guidance, take direction from management, and collaborate effectively with individuals from diverse backgrounds.
  • Proven ability to oversee the work of others, provide guidance and feedback, and recognize when issues should be escalated to department leadership.
  • Executive presence, sound judgment, and demonstrated ability to handle sensitive matters respectfully, ethically, and with discretion.
  • Good interpersonal skills, with the ability to build cross-functional relationships, set direction, and develop consensus in support of organizational goals.
  • Experience in business management, insurance operations, contract interpretation, employment law, sanctions compliance, or corporate governance is helpful.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands.  Employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear. 

 

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

Working at corporate headquarters in the San Diego area, this position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB 


The Senior Product Owner plays a pivotal role in driving the successful development and delivery of innovative products that meet the needs of our customers and aligns with the company’s strategic goals. This role acts as the bridge between business stakeholders, development teams and end-users, ensuring clear communication and effective prioritization of features and enhancements throughout the product lifecycle. 


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Maximizes the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum team. 

  • Defines and communicates product vision, overall strategy and growth opportunities to business and IT stakeholders, with minimal guidance from leadership and other Product team members. 
  • Drives the continuous refinement of the product vision, roadmap, and strategy to drive optimum business value.
  • Works closely with business stakeholders across the organization to convert product ideas into a prioritized backlog according to business value or return on investment (ROI).
  • Participates in agile ceremonies such as sprint planning, iteration reviews, and retrospectives to ensure continuous improvement and iterative development.
  • Facilitates Product Grooming Backlog sessions to align priority & strategy for better cross functional collaboration.
  • Remains accountable for each stage of the development process and the final product, evaluating progress and performance at each iteration and deciding whether the team can move on to the next steps.
  • Works closely with Technical Product Managers and Scrum master to ensure the successful execution of the product roadmap.
  • Anticipates product’s future needs by maintaining user personas and journey maps.
  • Creates annual and quarterly plans to align product groups to roadmap deliverables.
  • Independently manages and proactively identifies direction updates related to product areas.
  • Owns and drives user-centric product outcomes collaboratively with business and IT leadership.
  • Researches and analyzes market trends and user needs to develop and shape the roadmap for the product.
  • Collaborates with other Product Owners, Product Managers and shares best practices across teams to ensure alignment and consistency in ways of working within a value stream. 

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES 

This position has no supervisory responsibility.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 

  • Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university is required with a major or emphasis in Business, Finance, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field.
  • Minimum of 10 years’ related experience inclusive of leading technical teams, collecting business needs, and translating requirements to a technical audience.
  • Experience in the insurance industry highly desired.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience as a Product Owner, Product Manager, or similar role, with a track record of successfully launching and managing products or platforms.  
  • 3+ Specialty lines (Underwriting Workbench/PAS/Rater) implementations — techno-functional ownership across submission intake, quoting, binding, issuance, endorsements, renewals, cancellations, and reinstatements.
  • Good understanding of Specialty and Excess & Surplus (E&S) insurance operations
  • Experience with integrations across underwriting workbenches, PAS, billing systems, distribution/agency management, document management, and third-party data providers.
  • Experience with AI-powered or automated intake workflows (document extraction, OCR, conversational submission)
  • Data migration and reconciliation experience preferred
  • Majesco, Guidewire or comparable platform experience preferred

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS 

Certified Product Owner (CPO) required, SAFe preferred.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Knowledge of Agile processes and principles.
  • Understanding of the Insurance industry.
  • Ability to map value stream across business lines.
  • Possess technical expertise and understanding of product development practices.
  • Ability to balance technical constraints and a differentiated product that meets the needs of the marketplace.
  • Knowledge of mobile and web platform design conventions and technology limitations and opportunities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, experience working with cross-functional teams, and presenting to leadership.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications including Word, Visio, Excel, Project, and PowerPoint.
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills.
  • Advanced analytical, qualitative, quantitative, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to apply critical thinking and analytical skills to recommend creative solutions to business and technical challenges.
  • Strong attention to detail.
  • Ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment. 

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS  

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Claims Specialist position is responsible for handling complex claims with a focus on providing exceptional service for stakeholders in order to drive claims to an equitable resolution within Company standards.  The Claims Specialist works with a sense of urgency, understands insurance coverage concepts, and navigates the legal system with the support of counsel to drive strategic outcomes.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Manages complex claims inventories requiring advanced technical expertise and strategic claim handling  

  • Effectively communicates with policyholders, agents, attorneys, and witnesses to gather information and provide the highest possible level of customer service.
  • Promptly investigates claims to determine exposure, works with appropriate experts and makes strategic recommendations.
  • Utilizes appropriate resolution tactics (e.g., mediation, negotiation, denial, litigation or offer) to proactively drive outstanding results.
  • Operates within the requirements of related state and/or the governing entity rules and regulations as well as internal claims handling policies and procedures. 
  • Directs defense counsel throughout the litigation process in line with ICW litigation guidelines while monitoring legal fees and costs.

 All Claims Specialists:

  • Consistently provides exceptional customer service
  • Effectively collaborates with cross-functional Team Members for project and process discussions
  • Makes recommendations for streamlining processes and adopting the industry’s best practices
  • Ensures accuracy of data in claims system for compliance with applicable regulatory reporting
  • Provides knowledge transfer across the organization
  • Continuously seeks to improve technical skills by attending job related training and tracking current case law. 
  • As a SME (subject matter expert), serves as a technical resource and mentors/trains less experienced Team Members

Workers’ Compensation Claims (Specific Responsibilities):

  • Prepares and presents claims status reports for internal and external stakeholders.
  • Administers timely and appropriate benefits to injured workers; manages and approves payment of benefits within designated authority level.  Works within applicable state rules, regulations as well as ICW Group’s internal claims handling policies and procedures.
  • Creates and adjusts reserves in a timely manner to ensure reserving activities are consistent with company policies.
  • Resolves claims fairly and equitably, acting in the best interest of the insured while providing timely benefits to injured workers as required by law.
  • Supports specialty claim handling programs and strategic initiatives involving complex litigation, medical exposure, catastrophic injuries, fatality, PTD, or long-duration claims
  • Provides technical guidance and collaborates with leadership on complex claim resolution strategies and specialty handling initiative
  • Identifies and drives resolution opportunities on complex or long-duration claims through proactive settlement, reserving, and medical management strategies.


SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibility


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree (or equivalent combination of education and experience) required along with a minimum of 8 – 10+ years’ related claims handling experience involving complex litigation, reserving, settlement strategy, and high exposure claims. 


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Workers’ Compensation: Certification that meets the minimum standards of training, experience, and skill required. WCCA and WCCP preferred. State Workers Compensation License is required in some branches.



KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Excellent understanding of laws and jurisdictional restraints to manage claims
  • Excellent verbal communication skills, time management, attention to detail and organizational skills
  • Must be adept at learning new technology
  • Flexibility to adapt to changes in a fast-paced environment

Must have the ability to:

  • Read, analyze, and interpret technical and legal documents
  • Write reports and business correspondence
  • Respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers (insured), claimants and regulatory agencies
  • Present information at meetings, to management and clients
  • Solve practical problems and deal with a variety of variables in situations where limited standardization exists

Workers’ Compensation: Advanced knowledge of workers’ compensation claims handling, reserving, litigation management, and resolution strategies



PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear. 

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB 

The purpose of this job is to oversee the complete lifecycle recruitment process, including candidate sourcing and assessment, onboarding, and maintaining good hiring practices. This position exists to attract and place high-quality talent across the enterprise while providing exceptional candidate experiences to promote the brand and generate engagement to support Human Resources (HR) initiatives.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Participates in the execution of Corporate Talent Attraction strategies.

  • Coordinates the placement of ads utilizing online job boards, internal job postings, and school postings.
  • Recommends and participates in proactive recruitment strategies, such as college relations, job fairs, and military recruiting as warranted.
  • Creates and maintains contacts within the insurance and related industries.
  • Participates in networking groups and other business and community programs to increase skill and market knowledge.
  • Assists in the creation and execution of social media and relationship-building strategies to secure pre-employment interest and loyalty to the organization.
  • Places and maintains internal and external job postings for all positions, including technical roles, through schools, professional organizations, technical communities, and other sources in alignment with the Recruiting Plan.

Manages the candidate selection and onboarding process.

  • Sources qualified candidates for assigned and other positions using the most effective means, including internal and external job boards such as LinkedIn, Indeed, communities, professional associations, schools, or other target sources to minimize the use of agencies and provide high-caliber candidates.
  • Uses the most efficient and effective method of recruiting based on the position's requirements.
  • Works closely with Hiring Managers and HR Business Partners to determine staffing needs, role requirements, and timeliness of the recruitment process.
  • Maintains regular contact with possible future candidates and develops pipelines for recurring and hard-to-fill roles.
  • Pre-screens and recommends candidates to hiring managers, assessing relevant technical experience and competencies.
  • Works with the Talent Coordinator to schedule interviews and arrange travel as needed.
  • Notifies leadership of any concerns related to candidate experience, hiring practices, or the recruitment process.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB


The Senior Claims Examiner position handles moderate to complex claims with a focus on providing the highest level of service for policyholders and ICW Group to independently bring claims to an equitable conclusion within Company standards and best practice guidelines. The Senior Claims Examiner works with a sense of urgency, understands insurance coverage concepts, and navigates the legal system with the support of counsel to drive strategic outcomes.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Manages all aspects of  a moderate to highly complex  claims inventory.

  • Effectively communicates with policyholders, agents, attorneys, and witnesses to gather information and provide the highest possible level of customer service.
  • Promptly investigates claims to determine exposure, works with appropriate experts and makes strategic recommendations.
  • Utilizes appropriate resolution tactics (e.g., mediation, negotiation, denial, litigation or offer) to proactively drive outstanding results.
  • Operates within the requirements of related state and/or the governing entity rules and regulations as well as internal claims handling policies and procedures. 
  • Directs defense counsel throughout the litigation process in line with ICW litigation guidelines while monitoring legal fees and costs.

All Claims Examiners:

  • Consistently provides exceptional customer service.
  • Effectively collaborates with team members from various departments for project and process discussions.
  • Makes recommendations for streamlining processes and adopting the industry’s best practices.
  • Ensures accuracy of data in claims system for compliance with applicable regulatory reporting.
  • Provides knowledge transfer across the organization.
  • Continuously seeks to improve technical skills by attending job related training and tracking current case law. 
  • Acts as a mentor and provides training for less experienced team members.
  • Serves as a technical resource and mentors less experienced Team Members

Workers’ Compensation Claims (Specific Responsibilities):

  • Prepares and presents claims status reports for internal and external stakeholders.
  • Administers timely and appropriate benefits to injured workers; manages and approves payment of benefits within designated authority level.  Works within applicable state rules, regulations as well as ICW Group’s internal claims handling policies and procedures.
  • Creates and adjusts reserves in a timely manner to ensure reserving activities are consistent with company policies.
  • Resolves claims fairly and equitably, acting in the best interest of the insured while providing timely benefits to injured workers as required by law.
  • Provides technical guidance and collaborates with leadership on complex claim resolution strategies and specialty handling initiative
  • Handles specialized claim inventories involving complex medical exposure, litigation, fatality, PTD, life pension, or long-term resolution strategies.
  • Identifies and drives resolution opportunities on complex or long-duration claims through proactive settlement, reserving, and medical management strategies.


SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibility


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree (or equivalent combination of education and experience) required along with a minimum of 5+ years’  related claims handling experience required; complex litigated claims experience is highly preferred.   


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Workers’ Compensation: Certification that meets the minimum standards of training, experience, and skill required. WCCA and WCCP preferred. State Workers Compensation License is required in some branches.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Good understanding of laws and jurisdictional restraints to manage claims
  • Excellent verbal communication skills, time management, attention to detail and organizational skills
  • Must be adept at learning new technology
  • Flexibility to adapt to changes in a fast-paced environment

Must have the ability to:

  • Read, analyze, and interpret technical and legal documents
  • Write reports and business correspondence
  • Respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers (insured), claimants and regulatory agencies
  • Present information at meetings, to management and clients
  • Solve practical problems and deal with a variety of variables in situations where limited standardization exists

Workers’ Compensation: Advanced knowledge of workers’ compensation claims handling, reserving, litigation management, and resolution strategies

PURPOSE OF THE JOB 

The purpose of this job is to prepare and analyze financial information to provide accurate and useful information to management for review and provide insight to management to help in overall decision making. This position exists to ensure accounting processes and financial statements are completed thoroughly and accurately, while aligning with Company standards. 


The Reinsurance Accountant supports the accurate and timely accounting for the Company’s assumed reinsurance portfolio. This role processes and reviews broker bordereaux and statements, records premium, loss, commission and cash activity in accordance with the underlying treaties, prepares and reconciles reinsurance general ledger accounts, and supports month-end, quarter-end and year-end close. This position combines accounting skills with an operational mindset: it manages a steady flow of high-volume, deadline-driven work, tracks items from receipt through to resolution, and keeps handoffs between teams clean. The Reinsurance Accountant works closely with brokers, Operations, Underwriting, Actuarial and Internal Audit, and contributes to the controls and process improvements that keep reinsurance financial information accurate, complete and aligned with Company standards.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Reinsurance Process and Analysis

  • Enters and reviews broker bordereaux (BDX) and statements, including premium, losses, commission and brokerage, and completes the review checklist for each item. 
  • Records initial premium booking with allocation of premiums to annual statement lines (ASL), along with premium adjustments and endorsements; calculates premium earnings. 
  • Records claims and loss activity reported on bordereaux and statements, including allocation of losses to ASL, and confirms that cash is cleared only after the related claim is recorded. 
  • Ensures all recorded transactions are in line with the reinsurance contract. 
  • Monitors contractual reporting timing and payment terms and applies and settles cash to and from various brokers. 
  • Follows up with broker accounting departments on delayed or large payments, exception payments and complex premium or claim bordereaux; sets up trust accounts and collateral as required; and flags reporting or accounting anomalies. 
  • Monitors the shared intake folder and mailbox for incoming broker bordereaux, statements and correspondence daily, and logs and tracks each item from receipt through to completion. 
  • Manages a workload of high-volume transactions against processing deadlines and service targets, prioritizing items by due date, size, and complexity. 
  • Coordinates handoffs with Operations and Underwriting (for example, claims and cash calls) so that no item is left unentered or unowned between teams. 
  • Builds and maintains relationships with the accounting departments of brokers and clients as needed. 

 

Accounting Operations and Reconciliations 

  • Prepares income statement, balance sheet, consolidated and other accounting statements and reports. 
  • Reviews general ledger accounts, prepares journal entries, and reconciles reinsurance accounts between the reinsurance administration system and the general ledger. 
  • Identifies, researches, resolves and follows up on reconciling items, including any inefficiency in department policies and procedures. 
  • Analyzes financial reports and records, and makes recommendations relative to the accounting of reserves, assets, and expenditures. 
  • Maintains and manages an assigned section of the statutory financial statements. 

Process Improvement and Governance 

  • Follows internal controls, including segregation of duties, and does not review or approve their own entries. 
  • Reviews and verifies the accuracy of journal entries, bordereaux entries and accounting classifications entered by others, and documents and escalates errors or omissions found. 
  • Assembles, creates and reconciles month-end accounting entries, resolving discrepancies. 
  • Prepares asset, liability and capital account entries by compiling and analyzing account information. 
  • Maintains desk procedures, checklists and tracking logs, and follows up on aged or outstanding items (such as unreconciled cash or outstanding premium) until they are resolved. 
  • Supports internal and external audits by preparing documentation and responding to requests. 
  • Demonstrates effective communication and problem-solving skills, and contributes ideas and tools that improve department processes, including checklists, automation and review procedures. 
  • Accurately passes internal information to state agencies and works with them to make sure requirements are completed. 

Financial Reporting & Analysis 

  • Prepares ad-hoc reinsurance reports and memos as required by management. 
  • Assists in the preparation of the Quarterly and Annual Statement Schedule F. 
  • Updates and reconciles all reinsurance-related general ledger accounts. 
  • Calculates and records quarterly adjustments, such as commuted treaty reserve adjustments and reinsurance reserves, and uploads changes in ceded reinsurance reserves to the general ledger. 

 

 SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES  

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities. 

 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE  

  • Bachelor's degree from four-year college or university preferred, with a major or emphasis in Accounting, Finance, or related field.  
  • Minimum 2 years of related experience in Accounting; or equivalent combination of education and experience required.  
  • Experience in insurance or reinsurance accounting or operations preferred. 

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS  

None required.  

 

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS 

  • Working knowledge of General Accounting, Accounts Payable (A/P), Accounts Receivable (A/R) and/or in an entry-level accountant role, required.   
  • Understanding of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) regulations.  
  • Operational orientation, with experience in process-driven, high-volume, or workflow-based work and comfort managing queues, deadlines and handoffs between teams. 
  • Strong attention to detail, with the ability to review work for accuracy and identify errors and omissions. 
  • Proficiency in Excel for tracking, reconciling and analyzing data. 
  • Proven ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, and to interact effectively with management, employees, brokers and auditors. 
  • Ability to work independently and meet stringent deadlines. 
  • Willingness to adopt new tools and automation to improve review and reconciliation processes.  
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite applications. 

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS   

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.   

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT   

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this job is to produce complex analyses and provide expert actuarial advice to the Actuarial team. This position exists to support and execute Company strategy as directed by the Chief Actuary, while establishing and upholding a department direction and vision. This position will also manage an entire line of business or other area similar in scope or complexity, including owning one or more domain areas of responsibility, as well as increased breadth of ownership managing enterprise actuarial requests and solutions across all lines of business.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 

Establishes and upholds a department direction and vision.

  • Contributes to discussions around establishing vision and direction for the actuarial department.
  • Represents the company in business settings and potentially with external parties.
  • Responsible for developing new business processes or comprehensive analytic efforts.
  • Ensures that the work product supports business growth and profitability.
  • Takes responsibility to extensively modify processes in order to improve accuracy and efficiency.
  • Invokes critical thought process to solve complex problems and identify dependencies in processes to enable direction of staff.
  • Ensures soundness of actuarial analyses and consistency with Standards of Practice. 

Partners with business leaders to provide expertise on business efforts.

  • Partners with business leaders in administering an entire line of business or other area of responsibility similar in scope and complexity.
  • Organizes and coordinates actuarial efforts with business leaders to develop and implement new products and expand into new markets.
  • Fosters positive, collaborative working relationships with higher level experts across the organization.
  • Acts as the Subject Matter Expert (SME) for actuarial matters.
  • Prepares and communicates actuarial findings to business leaders. 

Develops and manages a team of Credentialed Actuaries and Actuarial Analysts

  • Provides direction to team.  Communicates Mission, Values and other organization operating principles to the team.
  • Establishes high standards for the delivery of services and products rendered, resulting in an excellent customer experience.  Ensures that the entire team is engaged and that leadership practices encourage development, recognition and retention.
  • Establishes and adheres to hiring criteria, on-boarding and training requirements for incoming staff.
  • Oversees the performance management and development process for the team and performs performance management duties, development planning and coaching for direct reports. 
  • Acts as a resource for team members to answer questions and solve complex problems.
  • Manages budget, technology and other resources, workload and customer requests for services.  Ensures adherence to all Company policies and procedures and Compliance responsibilities.
  • Ensures data quality, adherence to IT security guidelines, profitability and other risk-related metrics for self and members of the team. 

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position directly supervises employees within the Actuarial department and carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws. These responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; conducting performance and salary reviews; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems; coaching, mentoring, and developing team members to further their skills and knowledge; creating and monitoring development plans; setting performance expectations/goals; forecasting staffing needs and planning for peak times and absences; enforcing department policies and procedures.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree from four-year college or university required in Applied Mathematics, Computer Science or related field preferred.  Minimum 7 years of related experience and/or training; or, equivalent combination of education and experience. 


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Associate of the Casualty Actuary Society (ACAS) or Fellow of the Casualty Actuary Society (FCAS) designation required.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

Strong interpersonal skills and proven leadership ability. Thorough knowledge of actuarial models and ability to assess results. Experience managing complex projects, resources and staff. Broad company and industry experience and expertise, with the ability to work collaboratively with other business leaders to solve complex business problems. Ability to mentor and train actuarial staff. Ability to take actuarial ownership of significant segments of responsibility, including multiple lines of business. Ability to influence the strategic vision of the actuarial department.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this job is to create deliverables that help develop target-state guidance (standards, guidelines, reference implementations) for evolving the data infrastructure across the enterprise in order to enable business strategy, knowledge worker productivity, improve customer experience and business decision-making, and deliver targeted business outcomes. This position exists to provide the leadership, facilitation, analysis and design tasks required for the development of an enterprise's data architecture.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 

Leads efforts to develop and maintain the architectural assets for the data domain including current and target state data architectures.

  • Sets an architecture direction for the data domain that is aligned with business goals. Leads presentations for the organization.
  • Maintains a holistic view of data assets by creating and maintaining blueprints that illustrate how data is stored, processed, and accessed.
  • Ensures data solutions are in alignment with data architecture principles and target state.
  • Oversees end-to-end data asset lifecycle management activities. Drives collaboration efforts and capitalizes on the talents of others to achieve established goals.
  • Facilitates and orchestrates the delivery of targeted business outcomes through architectural decisions. Leads the creation of models, architecture design work products, and new technology innovation initiatives within area(s) of responsibility and for the enterprise.
  • Leads the design, documentation, and analysis of the business architecture in their area and provides recommendations to ensure the delivery of an integrated, holistic solution.   

Collaborates with enterprise, solution, and domain architects to understand the implications of respective architectures on data architecture and maximize the value of information across the organization.

  • Works with senior stakeholders and subject matter experts in driving effective data management standards and policies across the organization.
  • Provides recommendations on business information that will need to be available and shared consistently across the organization through the identification, definition, and analysis of how information assets aid strategies and business outcomes.
  • Assists data and analytics leaders, and business and IT leadership in developing data strategy, and governance processes and structures.
  • Leads the creation of models, technical standards, and architecture design work products within area(s) of responsibility. Leads technology portfolio prioritization efforts and owns the management of technology portfolio within area(s) of responsibility.
  • Expands the use and successful delivery of information across the enterprise, resulting in improved decision making. 

Provides strategic recommendations to maximize the value of enterprise data assets, including the external data ecosystem through data exploitation, envisioning data-enabled strategies and enabling business outcomes through analytics, data and analytics governance, and enterprise information policy.

  • Evaluates and recommends emerging technologies for data management, storage, and analytics.
  • Provides insight into the relationship of data to business objectives, applications, technology, principles, and standards.
  • Represents enterprise architecture by advocating and sharing knowledge. Builds credibility for an initiative by presenting evidence and ensuring that individuals affected are included in the process at the outset.
  • Participates as a member of one or more architectural review boards (ARB) that ensure architecture quality and compliance.
  • Leads short and long-term initiatives and road mapping efforts that drive change and gains support for proposed solutions. Sets goals, strategic vision, and leads others work. Questions current assumptions and seeks out-of-the-box solutions to challenges.  

Contributes to the design, documentation, and analysis of the data architecture in area(s) of responsibility to ensure the data portfolio operates more simply and reliably.

  • Works with Head of Architecture and acts as a leader to influence enterprise direction/approach and the strategic planning process. Coaches and mentors others and assists with problem resolution.
  • Acts as an expert and sets the current and future state information architecture(s). Seeks out a wide range of views on the topic to refine options, which they communicate to key stakeholders.
  • Educates business and IT partners on information architecture. Contributes ideas and makes recommendations to improve the process followed for work product by making it more efficient and effective.
  • Researches, proposes, and champions new technology innovation initiatives in the organization. Creates and advances the data architecture vision and strategy.
  • Leads the design, documentation, and analysis of the technical and integration architecture practice to ensure the infrastructure runs efficiently and effectively.
  • Leads project-level architectural reviews and ensures alignment with architectural deliverables, principles, strategies, and standards.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibility.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's Degree from four-year college or university required with a major or emphasis in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, Economics, Sociology, or related field.  Master’s Degree preferred.  Minimum 12 years of experience in IT or data management and analytics experience required. Minimum 8 years of architecture experience in multiple architectural domains such as business, information, application, integration, technology, and security required. Experience working in the insurance or financial services industry required.


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

TOGAF, IASA or any other architecture-related certification required. Insurance or financial services-related certification is strongly desired.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

Ability to establish credibility through visualizations and tell a compelling story to a broad audience. Working knowledge of IT and/or business services and participates in information gathering to support at least one service. Ability to present clearly and effectively to diverse audiences orally and in writing. Ability to identify and communicate the implications and impacts of tactical and strategic architecture decisions on the larger enterprise. Ability to make decisions and recommendations on technology strategies while considering various options and business needs. Awareness of insurance or financial services industries. Working knowledge of infrastructure technologies and participates in information gathering to support their area’s technical architecture. Working knowledge of integration techniques and technologies and participates in information gathering to support their area’s integration architecture. Working knowledge of business architecture and participates in information gathering to support the practice.  Ability to persuade peers within area(s) of responsibility by leveraging existing relationships of peers/manager.   Excellent written and verbal communication skills, experience working with cross-functional teams, and presenting to leadership. Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications including Word, Visio, Excel, Project, and PowerPoint. Ability to apply principles of logic to a wide range of intellectual and practical problems.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Security Architect II is a senior individual contributor within the Enterprise Architecture team who develops and influences enterprise security architecture direction and establishes frameworks and reusable guidance within assigned areas of responsibility to support the operationalization of security across the enterprise. The role translates business objectives, risk priorities, and regulatory obligations into practical security capabilities, standards, reference architectures, and implementation patterns. Working across business, technology, security, infrastructure, data, and delivery teams, the Security Architect II promotes consistent risk-based decisions and ensures security is designed into enterprise platforms, cloud environments, applications, integrations, data solutions, and emerging AI capabilities.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Develops and influences enterprise security architecture and strategic direction.

·   Develops, maintains, and communicates enterprise security architecture frameworks, principles, target-state architectures, reference architectures, roadmaps, and reusable security patterns.

·   Maps business goals, risk appetite, regulatory obligations, and enterprise strategy to security capabilities and technical implementation direction.

·   Partners with enterprise, solution, cloud, data, integration, infrastructure, and AI architects to embed security into technology strategies and solution designs.

·   Defines current-state and target-state security capabilities, identifies gaps and dependencies, and recommends sequenced initiatives to improve enterprise security maturity.

·   Provides architecture guidance for identity and access management, zero trust, network and cloud security, application security, data protection, cryptography, secrets management, logging and monitoring, resilience, vulnerability management, and third-party technology risk.

·   Creates decision records and clearly documents security trade-offs, assumptions, risks, compensating controls, and required follow-up actions.


Defines and maintains security standards, guidelines, and procedures.

·   Develops and maintains enterprise security standards, guidelines, control patterns, and procedures within assigned areas of responsibility and contributes to broader enterprise security direction, ensuring the resulting guidance is actionable, internally consistent, and aligned with enterprise policy.

·   Uses recognized frameworks and principles such as NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST SP 800-53, NIST Zero Trust Architecture, ISO/IEC 27001 and 27002, CIS Controls, and secure-by-design practices as appropriate to the organization.

·   Develops and maintains minimum security requirements and approved patterns within assigned areas of responsibility for AWS services, cloud accounts, networking, identity, encryption, key management, secrets, workload protection, observability, and incident readiness.

·   Contributes to exception and risk-acceptance criteria and partners with Security, Risk, Compliance, and technology owners to ensure deviations are explicit, time-bound, and appropriately approved.

·   Maintains traceability among business objectives, security risks, policies, standards, architecture decisions, technical controls, and implementation evidence.


Provides security architecture governance and solution guidance.

·   Performs and documents security architecture reviews for strategic initiatives, platforms, products, vendor solutions, integrations, and material technology changes.

·   Presents security-significant decisions and recommendations to the Architecture Review Board and other governance forums.

·   Engages early in initiative planning and solution design to identify threats, misuse cases, trust boundaries, attack paths, security requirements, and control responsibilities.

·   Advises teams on secure architecture patterns without displacing accountable engineering, cybersecurity operations, risk, privacy, legal, or business owners.

·   Evaluates vendor products and services, including security capabilities, architectural fit, data handling, integration requirements, operational dependencies, and concentration risk.

·   Mentors architects and technical teams, builds security architecture competency, and serves as a trusted advisor on complex or high-impact decisions.


Advances AI security architecture.

·   Defines security architecture guidance for AI and generative AI solutions, including data protection, identity and authorization, model and supply-chain risk, prompt injection, tool misuse, and unintended data disclosure.

·   Develops risk-based security patterns for AI applications and agentic workflows within assigned areas of responsibility, including adversarial testing, monitoring, human oversight, and controls that constrain autonomous actions.

·   Collaborates with data, privacy, legal, risk, and AI governance stakeholders to align AI security controls with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the NIST Generative AI Profile, OWASP guidance, business impact, and acceptable risk.


SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. The role provides technical leadership, architecture mentorship, and influence across teams and initiatives.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

·   Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field required. Equivalent relevant experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.

·   Minimum 8 years of progressively responsible IT or cybersecurity experience required.

·   Minimum 4 years of experience in security architecture, cloud security architecture, enterprise architecture, or solution architecture with substantial security responsibility required.

·   Demonstrated experience defining security standards, reference architectures, technical controls, and architecture roadmaps in a complex enterprise environment required.

·   Hands-on or architecture-level experience with AWS security services, identity and access management, network security, application security, data protection, security monitoring, and secure cloud adoption required.

·   Experience supporting regulated industries, financial services, or property and casualty insurance is preferred.

·   Experience with AI, machine learning, generative AI, or agentic-system security and governance is preferred.


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, AND REGISTRATIONS


One senior-level security or security architecture certification is required. CISSP is preferred as the baseline credential. Relevant alternatives or advanced credentials may include:

·   ISC2 Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Information Systems Security Architecture Professional (ISSAP), or Certified Cloud Security Professional (CCSP).

·   AWS Certified Security - Specialty or AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional.

·   GIAC Defensible Security Architecture (GDSA), GIAC Cloud Security Architecture and Design (GCSA), or another relevant GIAC certification aligned to the role.

·   ISACA Certified Information Security Manager (CISM) or Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC).

·   AI security training or certification, such as GIAC AI Security Automation Engineer (GASAE), is desirable when supported by relevant practical experience.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

·   Advanced knowledge of security architecture principles, threat modeling, zero trust, defense in depth, least privilege, secure-by-design, privacy-by-design, and risk-based control selection.

·   Strong working knowledge of NIST, ISO, CIS, cloud security, and enterprise architecture practices; ability to tailor frameworks rather than apply them mechanically.

·   Advanced knowledge of AWS security architecture and cloud-native control patterns.

·   Knowledge of application and API security, identity federation, privileged access, network segmentation, encryption, key management, secrets management, logging, monitoring, incident readiness, vulnerability management, and software supply-chain security.

·   Working knowledge of AI security risks and controls across data, models, prompts, retrieval, tools, agents, infrastructure, monitoring, and human oversight.

·   Ability to translate business goals, regulatory obligations, and risk scenarios into clear architecture requirements, technical standards, roadmaps, and solution options.

·   Ability to communicate strategic and tactical perspectives and explain complex security topics to executives, business leaders, architects, engineers, and control functions.

·   Strong facilitation, negotiation, written communication, presentation, and stakeholder-management skills.

·   Ability to operate as a self-directed senior individual contributor while collaborating effectively across architecture, cybersecurity, engineering, operations, risk, compliance, legal, privacy, and audit teams.

·   Ability to balance risk reduction, delivery speed, user experience, cost, resilience, and operational supportability.

This job operates in a professional office environment. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear and frequently will sit, stand, walk, and bend during working hours. The role requires manual and finger dexterity, eye-hand coordination, and normal or corrected vision and hearing. The employee may be required to lift light objects.
