ABOUT ICW GROUP 

ICW Group is a national, multi-line insurance carrier with an AM Best rating of 'A', approximately 1,300 employees, and headquarters in San Diego, California. ICW Group is executing an enterprise AI strategy that treats AI as core infrastructure: built on a single enterprise platform, governed by a single framework, and deployed under regulatory oversight from day one. As AI moves into underwriting, claims, and operational decisions, disciplined governance is what allows ICW to adopt AI quickly and defensibly. 

ABOUT THE AI GOVERNANCE OFFICE 

The AI Governance Management Office is ICW's standing execution and coordination function for artificial intelligence, sponsored by the SVP and Chief Digital and AI Officer. It serves the AI Governance Executive Committee (AIGEC) as its operational arm, turning AIGEC's policy, risk, and approval decisions into coordinated, well-governed delivery. The Office is the single operational home for AI intake, prioritization, coordination, enablement, and transparency.  

The Office is also ICW's single coordination point for NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool response preparation. California, ICW's domiciliary state, is participating in the 2026 NAIC pilot, which creates an active compliance window for the organization's higher-risk AI systems in underwriting and claims. 

PURPOSE OF THE JOB   

The AI Governance Manager is an advanced professional individual contributor within the AI Governance Management Office, reporting to the Director of Cloud, AI, ML, and Enablement Platforms. This dedicated position works independently with limited oversight to administer, facilitate, and execute AI governance day to day: coordinating the governance committees, operating the intake-to-decision workflow, owning the AI Hub, and maintaining the governance artifacts and evidence that keep ICW audit-ready and regulator-ready.  

Working closely with leadership and management at all levels, control functions, business owners, and external stakeholders, the AI Governance Manager makes governance practical and efficient so that teams move through it rather than around it. AIGEC and its subcommittees set policy, risk tolerance, and approvals; this role translates those decisions into consistent, well-documented execution, leads governance projects and processes, and provides guidance, coaching, and review of work products contributed by lower-level professionals and cross-functional partners. 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 

Governance Operations and Lifecycle Management 

  • Coordinate and administer AIGEC and its AI Risk & Compliance and Third-Party AI Governance subcommittees: run the cadence (intake triage, risk review, forums), prepare review packs, and document decisions and action items to closure. 

  • Operate the intake-to-decision workflow -- apply the risk taxonomy (Tier 0 through Tier 4), move each use case through the lifecycle gates with required signoffs and triggered control-function reviews, resolve intake or escalation issues, and maintain the decision log, exception register, and escalation paths. 
     

Policy, Standards, Controls, and Inventory 

  • Maintain the AI policy, standard, procedure, and control library with clear owners and review cadence, coordinate rollout of the policy suite (including the prohibited-use list), keep governance templates current, support control sufficiency testing for Tier 1 and Tier 2 systems, and recommend process and control enhancements that improve governance performance across the function. 

  • Administer the AI Systems Registry as the single audit-ready inventory of AI use cases, models, agents, and vendor AI, enforce the registry gate before build or deploy, guide business and technical owners through registry requirements, and coordinate model and system cards with lineage and classification for higher-risk systems. 

AI Hub Ownership 

  • Own and operate the AI Hub on SharePoint as the enterprise's single front door for AI serving approximately 1,300 employees -- intake, approved tools, responsible-use guidance, governance materials, learning, and metrics -- managing the content lifecycle and running it as the interface between AIGEC and the workforce. 

NAIC Regulatory Compliance Coordination 

  • Serve as the NAIC Response Coordinator, or lead significant portions of the response, for California DOI AI Systems Evaluation Tool inquiries, coordinate cross-functional evidence collection, maintain the artifacts serving Exhibits A through D (AI Systems Registry, model cards, AI Data Element Registry with Data Services, and the risk classification methodology), and track readiness and related policy updates as the pilot evolves. 

Monitoring, Audit Readiness, and Reporting 

  • Operate the governance KPI and KRI dashboard and produce reporting for AIGEC and executive leadership, assemble audit-ready evidence packs for Tier 1 systems, run regulatory scanning (NIST AI RMF, NAIC, ISO/IEC 42001, state AI laws), and route material changes into policy and control updates with operational recommendations. 

Training, Awareness, and Change Management 

  • Coordinate role-based AI governance training, attestation, and change-triggered learning, support the governance champion network and cultural-change activities, and provide guidance, coaching, and review of governance work products to reinforce clear ownership and consistent governance behavior. 
     

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES 

This role does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Information Technology, Risk Management, or related field, or equivalent experience.  

  • Minimum of ten years of experience in program or project management, governance, risk, or compliance operations within a technology, IT, or regulated environment. 

  • Demonstrated experience independently operating a governance, risk, or compliance program, including committee coordination, decision logging, evidence management, escalation management, and cross-functional process improvement. 

  • Experience with AI/ML programs, digital transformation, or technology transformation initiatives, or a strong record of ramping quickly on new governance domains. 

  • Advanced facilitation, stakeholder-management, and influencing skills, with the ability to navigate technical and business audiences at all levels of the organization, and influence practices, procedures, and policies at an operational level 

  • Proficiency with collaboration and tracking tools such as Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet, or equivalent, and experience with SharePoint content management. 

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to produce executive-level packs, dashboards, regulatory response materials, and reporting. 

  • Extensive working understanding of governance frameworks and compliance requirements in regulated industries, including the impact of governance decisions on business, technology, risk, and control functions 

  • Experience in the insurance or financial services industry preferred. 

  • Familiarity with AI governance frameworks: NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, the NAIC AI Model Bulletin, and the NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool (Exhibits A through D) preferred. 

  • Experience with NAIC regulatory requirements or Department of Insurance examination processes preferred. 

  • Familiarity with the AI and ML platforms in use at ICW (AWS Bedrock, Snowflake Cortex) and enterprise AI tools (Claude Enterprise, Microsoft 365 Copilot) preferred. 

  • Experience with SharePoint site design and enterprise portal management. 

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS  

  • Risk, audit, or governance certification such as CRISC or CGEIT, or a project and program management certification such as PMP or PgMP, or SAFe / Lean Portfolio Management preferred. 

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS 

  • Governance Discipline: Advanced ability to operate and improve governance processes, cadence, controls, and evidence, so decisions are defensible, repeatable, and scalable across the enterprise. 

  • Facilitation: Ability to run committees, reviews, and cross-functional decisions across diverse technical and business teams, and to influence operational practices, procedures, and policies within and outside the immediate job function. 

  • Detail Orientation: Meticulous attention to governance artifacts, compliance documentation, and registry data integrity. 

  • Communication: Ability to synthesize technical, business, and regulatory information into clear, actionable materials for business owners, control functions, vendors, and executive leadership. 

  • Ownership and Project Leadership: Self-directed execution across multiple concurrent governance workstreams in a fast-paced environment. 

  • Adaptability: Comfort with ambiguity and the ability to establish structure and process where none exists. 

  • Regulatory Awareness: Genuine interest in AI regulation and responsible AI, and in keeping ICW's posture current as expectations evolve. 

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS   

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk and hear.  

WORK ENVIRONMENT   

This position is based at ICW Group's Innovation Point campus in San Diego, CA. Occasional collaboration with remote team members and external partners via Microsoft Teams may be required. This position observes standard business hours with flexibility to support cross-time-zone engagements as needed. 
 

This description is a general statement of essential job functions and responsibilities. 

The position may include other duties as assigned.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this role is to develop, manage, and grow a profitable book of business within assigned line(s) of business, while serving as a senior-level underwriting and distribution partner to agents and internal stakeholders.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Quality Engineer II is an established, technical professional who serves as the Quality Engineering lead for their assigned delivery team. This role takes complete ownership of the test strategy, planning, and quality outcomes for the team, ensuring that quality is engineered into every stage of the software delivery lifecycle. Working independently with limited supervision, the QE II drives shift-left practices within the team, builds and maintains automated test solutions, and sets quality objectives that directly impact department results. The role requires practical depth in test engineering, the ability to solve difficult and moderately complex problems by drawing from prior experience, and the capacity to coordinate quality activities, delegate tasks, and coach junior team members.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the complete test strategy and test planning for the assigned Projects – defining scope, approach, risk assessment, entry/exit criteria, and test coverage targets for each release and sprint.

  • Act as the QE lead within the team and drive quality discussions during grooming, sprint planning, and design reviews; set quality objectives; and ensure the team delivers against them.

  • Develop, execute, and maintain comprehensive test plans, test cases, and test scripts for functional, regression, integration, API, and exploratory testing.

  • Build, maintain, and extend automated test suites using frameworks such as Playwright for UI, Postman/Newman for API, following clean code practice.

  • Execute API-level testing including payload validation, error handling, and contract verification for in-house and third-party service integrations.

  • Contribute automated tests to CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions), supporting continuous testing across regression, smoke, and feature validation stages.

  • Validate data integrity across integrated systems including ETL pipelines, data transformations, and end-to-end data reconciliation.

  • Identify, record, and thoroughly document defects; perform root cause analysis by reviewing logs, stack traces, and database states to diagnose systemic issues.

  • Participate in code reviews to provide quality-focused feedback on testability, error handling, and edge-case coverage.

  • Recommend enhancements to testing processes, tools, and standards to improve efficiency and effectiveness within the POD and broader team.

  • Own test data management, mock services, and QA environment configurations for reliable, repeatable test execution.

  • Leverage AI tools to assist in test case generation, coverage analysis, and failure triage.

  • Track and report quality metrics including defect density, escape rate, test coverage, and automation progress. Uses data to influence quality decisions.

  • Coordinate quality activities with distributed teams and offshore/nearshore vendor partners on test assignments, status calls, and triage.

  • Coach, guide, and review the work of junior team members; provide training on quality engineering practices and tools.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct reports but may mentor and/or train less experienced members.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, or related field (or equivalent experience); 3+ years in quality engineering or software testing with 2+ years in test automation.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

N/A

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Practical, hands-on proficiency in at least one programming language (Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript) with the ability to read, understand, and debug production code.

  • Demonstrated experience designing test strategies and owning end-to-end test planning for a product, team, or release.

  • Hands-on experience building and maintaining automated tests using Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, REST Assured, or Postman/Newman.

  • Solid understanding of API testing concepts: request/response validation, status codes, error handling, and RESTful service patterns.

  • Working knowledge of SQL and database concepts – ability to write queries for data validation, verify data transformations, and support ETL testing.

  • Experience contributing automated tests to CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions) and understanding of continuous testing principles.

  • Familiarity with version control (Git), branching strategies, and pull request workflows.

  • Understanding of the test automation pyramid and strategic allocation of coverage across unit, API, UI, and data layers.

  • Exposure to performance testing concepts and tools (JMeter, k6, or equivalent).

  • Awareness of AI-assisted testing tools and willingness to adopt AI workflows for test generation and defect analysis.

  • Solid understanding of Agile/Scrum practices, shift-left testing, and the software development lifecycle.

  • Ability to work independently on moderately complex assignments with limited supervision; strong problem-solving skills drawing from prior experience and analysis.

  • Good communication skills; able to influence within the team and communicate with contacts within and occasionally outside the department.

  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate quality tasks, delegate work, and review the output of junior team members.

  • Preferred skills include strong Insurance domain background, specifically in Claims Management and/or Insurance Billing business workflows.

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.  Employees are required to reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.  Employees must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds.  Employees are required to have visual acuity and be capable of operating and viewing computers and other electronic devices for extended periods of time.

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

Job.JobDescription:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

Head of Media Liability – North America

New York, Los Angeles, Alpharetta  

Job Description


Axis Capital’s Cyber, Technology, and Media Practice is expanding its Media vertical within the North American market. We are seeking a Head of Media Liability for North America to drive the strategic growth of this segment across Small Business, Middle Market, and Risk Management portfolio.

Reporting to the Head of Cyber, North America, this role will have responsibility for the U.S. Media portfolio, including P&L performance, technical underwriting, portfolio strategy, distribution, product development, and talent.

We are seeking an accomplished Media underwriting leader with deep technical expertise, strong commercial acumen, and the market relationships to build and grow a profitable specialty business.

Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate will be a highly accomplished, hands-on Media Liability underwriting leader with deep expertise across Media E&O, Cyber, and Technology E&O. They will bring a strong track record of underwriting and growing profitable portfolios across traditional media, film and television, advertising, and specialized production risks.

The successful candidate will combine technical underwriting expertise with strong commercial leadership, including P&L and portfolio management, business planning, product development, and experience across Small Business, Middle Market, and Large Account segments.

They will bring established wholesale and retail broker relationships, strong executive presence, and market credibility, with the ability to influence across a complex organization. This leader will help shape and execute the Media Liability growth strategy while remaining close to key underwriting decisions, distribution partners, and the development of underwriting talent.

Work Profile


This role offers a 3-day hybrid work environment based in New York Metro, Alpharetta, or Los Angeles. This position also requires regular travel to meet with brokers and clients face-to-face and attend industry and company events.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:


  • Own the strategy, P&L, and overall performance of the U.S. Media portfolio
  • Provide technical underwriting leadership across complex and strategic Media risks
  • Develop and deepen relationships with key wholesale and retail brokers and clients
  • Lead portfolio strategy across pricing, appetite, capacity, coverage, and risk selection
  • Drive product development and innovation in partnership with Product, Actuarial, Claims, and other key stakeholders
  • Monitor emerging exposures, loss trends, competitive dynamics, and regulatory developments to inform underwriting and growth strategy
  • Lead, coach, and develop underwriting talent while expanding Media expertise across the broader Cyber organization
  • Represent Axis in the marketplace and strengthen the visibility and positioning of the Media franchise

Candidate Profile

  • Deep Media Liability underwriting expertise with a strong understanding of Cyber and Technology E&O exposures
  • Deep expertise across the Media E&O landscape, including traditional media, film and television production, and specialized advertising and production wrap solutions
  • Demonstrated experience underwriting across Small Business, Middle Market, and Risk Management/Large Account segments
  • Proven P&L, portfolio management, and business planning capabilities
  • Established relationships across wholesale and retail distribution
  • Strong business acumen, technical underwriting judgment, and negotiation skills
  • Demonstrated leadership capabilities and the ability to influence within a complex, matrixed organization
  • Strong executive presence and credibility with brokers, clients, and senior stakeholders

Qualifications


  • Bachelor’s degree
  • Minimum of five years of Media Liability underwriting experience with demonstrated leadership responsibilities
  • Working knowledge of Cyber and Technology E&O insurance
  • CPCU, CISSP, or other relevant professional designation preferred, but not required
  • Ability to travel domestically in support of business objectives

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of USD $200,000 to USD $238,500. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of various factors. In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.  Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes.

Job Description: Account Manager

How does this role contribute to our collective success?


The Account Manager is responsible for delivering high-quality and efficient service to both internal and external clients, serving as a critical partner to the underwriting teams and placing brokers. Working closely with the Senior Account Manager (Sr.AM) and underwriting teams, the AM focuses on maintaining service excellence, managing the book of business, and achieving key metrics in retention, profitability, and growth.

Leveraging expertise in Property & Casualty (P & C) commercial insurance, the AM contributes to the company's overall success by building and maintaining relationships with underwriters and brokers, ensuring exceptional customer service, and facilitating new account marketing and renewal retention efforts.

What will you do in this role?

Policy Administration and Processing:


  • Perform advanced administrative tasks related to new and renewal business, including policy binding, issuance, and endorsements.
  • Review policy documents for accuracy and compliance with regulatory standards.
  • Identify opportunities for process improvement and efficiency enhancement within service delivery and underwriting operations.

Relationship Building, Client Engagement and Communication:


  • Acts as a key point of contact for brokers and clients, addressing inquiries, providing updates, and ensuring exceptional customer service.
  • Cultivate and nurture relationships with key broker contacts and decision-makers through regular communication and engagement.
  • Provide guidance and mentorship to junior team members, fostering a collaborative and supportive work environment.

Data Management and Documentation:


  • Maintain accurate records of policy and underwriting data, ensuring timely input and retrieval as needed.
  • Utilize diary systems to track and manage information flow and deadlines effectively.
  • Review underwriting documents and policies for accuracy and compliance with company guidelines and regulatory requirements.
  • Review underlying policies and endorse changes as needed.
  • Adhere to compliance standards and maintain accurate account files and underwriting documentation.

You may also be required to take on additional duties, responsibilities and activities appropriate to the nature of this role.

About You:

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table, so while there are some qualifications and experiences, we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge might lend itself to fulfilling this role and help us achieve our goals.

What you need to have:

 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Undergraduate degree in business, finance, or related field preferred, but not required.
  • Minimum of 2+ years’ experience in the commercial insurance industry as an Underwriter Assistant or equivalent insurance experience is required.
  • Solid understanding of Property and Casualty insurance coverage is necessary.
  • Proficient in written and verbal communication, capable of independently interacting with internal and external business partners such as brokers on behalf of Operations and Underwriting.
  • Experience with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, and Outlook), or similar software is necessary.
  • Strong aptitude for learning new computer/software programs is required.
  • Strong customer service skills and professional attitude are required.

Job.JobTitle: Head of Applied Science and AI Delivery
Job.JobDescription:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

How does this role contribute to our collective success?
Data, analytics and AI are critical to AXIS’s ability to make confident decisions, identify opportunities, improve efficiency and create sustainable competitive advantage. The Head of Applied Science & AI Delivery leads the development, management and evolution of AXIS’s portfolio of reusable applied science and AI capabilities.
Rather than owning delivery for individual business initiatives, this role provides the shared services, models, frameworks, engineering patterns and specialist expertise that enable and support delivery of high-quality business solutions rapidly, safely and consistently. The role is accountable for creating scalable, governed capabilities that can be adopted across multiple value streams, reducing duplication and accelerating value from analytics and AI.

What will you do in this role?

  • Set the platform vision and roadmap: Define and communicate the strategy, architecture and investment roadmap for reusable data science and AI capabilities, aligned with AXIS’s business priorities, enterprise technology strategy and Data & Analytics operating model.
  • Build reusable capabilities: Lead the design and development of shared AI services, analytical models, accelerators, agent frameworks, evaluation frameworks, experimentation environments and common solution components that can be adopted across multiple business-aligned solutions.
  • Enable business-aligned delivery: Partner closely with the Head of Insights & Analytics and value-stream teams to understand recurring needs, translate them into platform priorities and ensure capabilities are practical, discoverable, well documented and easy to adopt.
  • Lead experimentation and innovation: Create a controlled environment for exploration of emerging analytics, machine learning, generative AI and agentic capabilities. Convert successful experimentation into supported, repeatable enterprise components where there is clear value.
  • Establish product and platform management: Manage analytics and AI capabilities as products through their full lifecycle, with clear ownership, roadmaps, service expectations, adoption measures, technical health indicators and plans for continuous improvement or retirement.
  • Lead technical standards and engineering excellence: Establish consistent patterns for development, testing, deployment, integration, monitoring, observability, version control, documentation and reuse. Ensure capabilities are robust, maintainable and designed for enterprise scale.
  • Drive responsible and governed AI: Partner with Data & AI Governance, Information Risk Management, Legal, Compliance and Technology teams to embed responsible AI, model risk management, security, privacy and regulatory requirements into platform capabilities by design.
  • Own evaluation and monitoring frameworks: Ensure reusable approaches are in place to evaluate model and agent quality, performance, reliability, safety and value, and to monitor deployed capabilities throughout their lifecycle.
  • Advance the technology ecosystem: Work closely with Data Platforms & Engineering and Business Technology Solutions to shape and implement the analytics and AI technology stack, integration patterns and deployment pathways across Azure and Databricks.
  • Build and lead a high-performing specialist team: Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team of data scientists, applied scientists and AI engineers. Set a high bar for technical and academic rigour while fostering collaboration, inclusion, curiosity and pragmatic delivery.
  • Manage demand, capacity and investment: Prioritise the platform backlog based on enterprise value, reuse potential, risk reduction and strategic fit. Manage resources, budgets, suppliers and delivery commitments transparently.
  • Champion adoption and reuse: Promote awareness and effective use of shared capabilities, provide technical enablement to delivery teams and actively identify opportunities to consolidate duplicated solutions or patterns

How this role works with Insights & Analytics

The Insights & Analytics teams are aligned to business value streams and are accountable for identifying opportunities, defining priorities, designing solutions for each business need, delivering business-aligned solutions and driving adoption and measurable value. The Analytics & AI Platforms team is accountable for the reusable technical capabilities, frameworks, standards and specialist expertise that enable those teams to deliver at greater speed, quality and scale.

Both teams share accountability for successful end-to-end outcomes. The platform team does not become a central delivery queue for every use case, and business-aligned teams should reuse enterprise capabilities wherever practical rather than creating parallel solutions.

Success Measures / Key Outcomes

  • Reuse and adoption: Shared analytics and AI capabilities are adopted across multiple value streams, with evidence that reuse is reducing duplicated effort and accelerating delivery.
  • Speed and scalability: Business-aligned teams can move from opportunity to production more quickly because common services, patterns and deployment pathways are available and reliable.
  • Quality and reliability: Platform capabilities meet agreed standards for performance, availability, maintainability, documentation, monitoring and support.
  • Responsible delivery: Analytics and AI capabilities operate within AXIS governance, security, privacy, model risk and responsible AI requirements, with effective controls embedded by design.
  • Business enablement: Capability investments are demonstrably connected to priority business outcomes and enable solutions that are adopted and deliver measurable value.
  • Technology modernisation: The portfolio evolves in a controlled way to take advantage of relevant advances in data science, machine learning, generative AI and agentic technology.
  • Team performance: A highly engaged, inclusive and technically strong team with clear accountabilities, effective development pathways and a culture of collaboration and continuous improvement.
  • Cost and portfolio discipline: Investment is focused on capabilities with enterprise value and reuse potential, with transparent management of cost, technical debt, suppliers and lifecycle decisions.

About You
We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While there are qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge may help you fulfil this role and contribute to our goals.

What you need to have

  • Platform and product leadership: Significant experience defining and delivering a platform, product or reusable capability strategy in a complex organisation, with accountability for roadmaps, prioritisation, adoption and lifecycle management.
  • Technical leadership: Deep experience in data science, machine learning and AI, including generative AI, with the credibility to set technical direction, challenge design decisions and lead senior specialists.
  • Insurance or financial services experience: Understanding of the data, analytical, regulatory and risk context of insurance or another highly regulated industry.
  • Enterprise AI engineering: Strong understanding of how analytical models and AI services are developed, evaluated, deployed, monitored and operated at scale, including modern software engineering and MLOps or LLMOps practices.
  • Cloud and data platforms: Strong knowledge of Azure AI services and Azure Databricks, together with practical understanding of enterprise data architectures, APIs, deployment pipelines and integration patterns.
  • Responsible AI and risk: Experience embedding governance, security, privacy, controls and responsible AI practices into the design and operation of analytics and AI capabilities.
  • Strategic and commercial judgement: Ability to balance innovation, speed, enterprise value, cost, risk and technical sustainability when making platform investment and prioritisation decisions.
  • Collaborative operating style: Demonstrated success working across business-aligned analytics teams, engineering, architecture, technology, governance and senior stakeholders to deliver shared outcomes without relying solely on direct authority.
  • People leadership: Proven ability to build, lead and develop multidisciplinary technical teams and create a high-performance, inclusive and learning-oriented culture.
  • Communication and influence: Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical concepts, choices and risks clearly to executives, business leaders and delivery teams.
  • Delivery leadership: Ability to operate in a fast-paced environment, manage multiple priorities and provide clear direction, resource planning, cost oversight and delivery transparency.

What we prefer you to have

  • Relevant technical background: Advanced technical education or equivalent professional experience in data science, computer science, statistics, engineering or a related field.
  • Enterprise implementation experience: A track record of building reusable analytics or AI platforms and taking generative AI or agentic capabilities from experimentation into governed enterprise use.
  • Technical depth: Strong working knowledge of Python, Databricks, foundational models, evaluation techniques, retrieval patterns, agent architectures, deployment pipelines and monitoring approaches.

Role Factors

  • Attend your local office in line with AXIS expectations to build relationships with colleagues and the wider business.
  • Engage in company activities to grow your network and build a strong team culture.
  • Travel internationally on occasion, as required by the role.

What we offer
You will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid annual leave, and much more.

 

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $280,000.00 to $325,000.00. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. 

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.  

Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is [Exempt/Non-Exempt] for FLSA purposes.

Senior Underwriter – Ocean Marine Cargo
New York or Chicago


The Senior Underwriter, Ocean Marine Cargo will act within established guidelines to analyze, evaluate, price, and manage new and renewal business in support of the growth of the U.S. Ocean Marine Cargo portfolio. The initial focus will include Small and Middle Market, Large Complex Transit, Stock Throughput, and Excess Stock Exposure risks


The role will also support AXIS’s broader Marine Logistics capabilities, which complement traditional Cargo coverage by addressing liability exposures throughout the movement, handling, and storage of goods. Relevant experience may include Cargo Legal Liability, Warehouse Legal Liability, Errors & Omissions, Shipper’s Interest, and packaged logistics solutions.


Candidate Profile

The Senior Underwriter, Ocean Marine Cargo will be a hands-on technical underwriting professional with a demonstrated history of success within a leading commercial insurance carrier, building and managing a complex Ocean Marine Cargo portfolio.


Candidates should have strong relationships across Ocean Marine Cargo wholesale and retail broker channels and full lifecycle underwriting experience, including solicitation and evaluation of submissions, risk analysis, structuring terms and conditions, pricing, preparing and issuing indications, quotations and binders, and portfolio management.


Candidates with Marine Logistics or related supply-chain liability underwriting experience are especially attractive, including exposure to freight forwarders, logistics providers, warehouse operators, and transportation intermediaries. Experience with Cargo Legal Liability, Warehouse Legal Liability, Errors & Omissions, Shipper’s Interest, or packaged Marine Logistics solutions is highly desirable.


The successful candidate should understand how traditional Cargo exposures interact with transportation, warehousing, contractual liability, and logistics-related risks across the broader supply chain, allowing them to evaluate opportunities from both a cargo/property and logistics liability perspective

Key Duties and Responsibilities

  • Underwrite and manage complex Ocean Marine Cargo business, including Small and Middle Market, Large Complex Transit, Stock Throughput, and Excess Stock Exposure risks.
  • Evaluate Marine Logistics opportunities that complement the Ocean Cargo portfolio, including Cargo Legal Liability, Warehouse Legal Liability, Errors & Omissions, Shipper’s Interest, and packaged logistics solutions.
  • Assess supply-chain exposures involving freight forwarders, logistics providers, warehouse operators, transportation intermediaries, and other businesses involved in the movement, handling, and storage of goods.
  • Review contractual and operational exposures to determine appropriate coverage structure, limits, retentions, pricing, terms, conditions, and endorsements.
  • Work with brokers to identify cross-sell opportunities across Ocean Cargo and Logistics, and develop broader solutions for clients with complex supply-chain exposures.
  • Prospect for new business and develop strategies targeting Small to Middle Market and Large Complex Corporate risks.
  • Develop and maintain strong wholesale and retail broker relationships, using those relationships to generate submissions and expand the portfolio.

Required Experience

  • 5+ years of direct Ocean Marine Cargo underwriting experience.
  • Demonstrated experience building and managing complex Ocean Cargo business.
  • Experience with Logistics, Cargo Legal Liability, Warehouse Legal Liability, Errors & Omissions, Shipper’s Interest, or related transportation/logistics liability products strongly preferred.
  • Understanding of supply-chain exposures and the contractual relationships among cargo owners, freight forwarders, logistics providers, warehouse operators, and transportation intermediaries.
  • Ability to build and expand retail and wholesale broker relationships.
  • Strong technical underwriting, portfolio management, negotiation, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a collaborative underwriting environment with strong attention to detail.

We currently expect to offer a base salary of $150,000 -210,000K for this position. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of various factors, including your specific years experience and work location. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package that includes medical plans.

Underwriting Trainee - Environmental

Position Summary

AXIS is seeking an ambitious and analytical Underwriting Trainee to join our Environmental team. This is an excellent opportunity for a recent graduate or early-career professional interested in developing a long-term career in specialty insurance underwriting.

The Environmental business provides innovative insurance solutions for environmental contractors, environmental consultants, engineers, construction-related risks, and other professional service firms with complex environmental exposures.

As an Underwriting Trainee, you will receive hands-on training and mentorship from experienced underwriters while developing technical underwriting, risk assessment, broker relationship management, and portfolio management skills.

This position is designed to provide a structured career path toward promotion into an Underwriter role within the DP&E organization.

What You Will Do

Under the guidance of senior underwriters, you will:

  • Learn the fundamentals of specialty commercial insurance underwriting, pricing, and risk selection.
  • Assist in evaluating new and renewal submissions by reviewing loss history, financial information, exposure data, operational details, and account characteristics.
  • Analyze environmental, professional liability, and contractor-related risks to support underwriting decisions.
  • Conduct research on insureds, industries, market trends, and emerging environmental exposures.
  • Prepare underwriting analyses and recommendations for peer review and underwriting discussions.
  • Support the quoting, binding, and policy issuance process.
  • Learn AXIS underwriting guidelines, coverage forms, endorsements, and risk appetite.
  • Assist with renewal reviews, policy changes, endorsements, and premium adjustments.
  • Participate in broker meetings, training sessions, and marketing initiatives alongside experienced underwriters.
  • Develop a foundational understanding of environmental liability, professional liability, and specialty package products.
  • Build strong working relationships with brokers, clients, internal partners, and distribution teams.
  • Gain exposure to portfolio management and profitability analysis while learning how disciplined underwriting drives sustainable growth.

You will build proficiency in:

Core Underwriting Skills

  • Risk assessment and exposure analysis
  • Coverage review and interpretation
  • Underwriting processes, workflows, and systems
  • Pricing methods and rating fundamentals
  • Loss ratio and profitability analysis

Product Knowledge

  • Contractors Pollution Liability
  • Professional Liability
  • Pollution Legal Liability
  • Combined environmental package products
  • Related environmental and specialty casualty coverages

Business Development

  • Broker relationship building
  • Marketing and distribution basics
  • Clear presentation and communication skills
  • Industry networking and professional growth

Qualifications Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Risk Management, Insurance, Economics, Environmental Science, Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field.
  • 0-1 years of professional experience.
  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
  • Ability to learn technical concepts and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Demonstrated curiosity, initiative, and desire to build a career in underwriting.

Preferred

  • Internship experience in insurance, engineering, construction, environmental services, or related industries.
  • Coursework or academic background in environmental science, engineering, risk management, or finance.
  • Interest in specialty insurance and environmental risk management.
  • Experience analyzing data and making recommendations based on findings.

Job Description:

Job Description
AXIS is seeking a Senior Claim Director, Specialty Complex Claims to join our North America Claims team and will report the Head of Specialty Complex Claims.

As a direct report to the Head of Specialty Complex Claims, the candidate will be part of a sophisticated team of claims professionals handling and managing a wide variety of claims with coverage issues as well as coverage litigation involving Casualty (Primary & Excess), Commercial Property, Financial Lines, EPL, Cyber, various Professional Lines Specialties and Design Professionals and Environmental claims), Program Claims (all lines of business), Canada Claims (all lines of business) and A&H Claims.

This role will also be responsible for delivering the AXIS North America Claims value proposition engaging with stakeholders, brokers, and insureds to ensure constant communication and service engagement distinguishes AXIS claims every day.

The successful candidate will: Direct handle claims involving complex coverage issues as defined by the Head of North America Claims, including the investigation, analysis and evaluation of coverage liability and damages, within best practices.

Direct handle coverage disputes, including litigation and arbitration matters initiated by AXIS issuing companies and when AXIS issuing companies are parties to such litigation.

Formulate claims and litigation strategies, assigning, directing, and managing outside counsel in coverage litigation or arbitration

Manage coverage counsel and litigation costs as well as collaborate and work with the Litigation Management and Vendor Management teams ensuring cost management and the development and enhancement of the coverage counsel panel.

Manage discovery issues and responses, including opportunities to ensure consistency as well as identifying relevant and responsive information and ensure proper and adequate preparation of company witnesses for deposition and trial testimony

Provide guidance to the North America Claims teams regarding coverage issues, coverage disputes and claim handling issues, time limited demands, emerging issues, including strategic direction as well as recommend and approve outside coverage counsel assignments

Review Coverage positions for matters pending in states required as per the Specialty Complex Claims Referral Guidelines Collaborate across disciplines and business units, including: the general counsel team overseeing errors and omissions issues arising from claims handling

Manage selection of and requests to hire coverage counsel related to any claims pending in North America Identify liability and coverage trends and issues with both individual and portfolio impact and formulate the processes and strategies for handling such claims as well as the related coverage issues ensuring accurate and consistent claims management across impacted underwriting segments and lines of business.

Support response to underwriting inquiries and information requests regarding policy construction and drafting, reporting claim trends, data analysis, and risk assessments

Actively coach and mentor the North America claim teams on coverage issues and guidance Build and maintain key relationships with internal stakeholders (e.g., peers, Underwriting, Actuarial, various executive management leaders) and external stakeholders (e.g., brokers, insureds, attorneys, auditors, reinsurers, and vendors)

Extensive communication with senior executives, brokers, reinsurers, actuaries, insureds, and auditors (both external and internal)

Axis Culture and Values – everyday demonstrate the Axis behaviors that support and align with AXIS values: People, Decisiveness, Excellence and Stronger Together

KEY SKILLS & ABILITIES: 7-10+ years of claims management experience handling a wide variety of coverage issues and coverage litigation involving the various claims disciplines summarized previously, as well as:
Demonstrated leadership, organizational, and management skills Experience practicing law as well as claims management (both directly managed and TPA managed claims)

Demonstrated ability to influence and collaborate at all organizational levels, both internally and externally as well as the ability to identify and resolve complex, disputed claims

Analytical thinker that can drive results using all facets of the legal and claims processes

Understanding of and ability to balance both the immediate claim issues as well as the broader portfolio impact and customer service impact of coverage disputes and issues

Excellent oral and written communication skills with the ability to deal effectively with people with conflicting expectations, differing opinions, and multiple viewpoints

Demonstrated ability and experience handling coverage issues involving a wide variety of loss scenarios as well as reporting and presenting about same to senior management

In-depth knowledge of claims, litigation, arbitration, and trial processes as well as excellent analytical, investigative, and negotiating skills

Law Degree and admission in good standing to one of the fifty state bars

Adjuster Licenses in all states required by AXIS

Travel is associated with this role (e.g., team management, court proceedings, mediations, and settlement)

New York, Chicago, Alpharetta, San Francisco, Los Angeles

Hybrid

Position Description

AXIS’ US Construction team is seeking an experienced Senior Underwriter to support the continued growth of our Builders Risk portfolio, with a focus on both Project and Master Builders Risk solutions. This role will be responsible for developing strong broker and client relationships, identifying profitable new business opportunities, and building a quality book of business that supports the long-term success of the US Construction unit.

The Senior Underwriter will play an important role in strengthening AXIS’ market presence, applying sound underwriting judgment, and delivering thoughtful solutions for complex construction risks. The ideal candidate will bring strong technical expertise, established broker relationships, and the ability to drive responsible growth through disciplined underwriting, effective portfolio management, and consistent market engagement.

Candidate Profile

The Sr Underwriter Builders Risk position requires a skilled professional who has excelled in a prominent Commercial Insurance Carrier and specializes in Project and Master Builder Risk Solutions. This role focuses on accounts engaged in large construction risks with varying sizes and complexity. The ideal candidate will possess extensive knowledge in all aspects of underwriting, including portfolio management, submission solicitation, underwriting analysis, and the creation and issuance of indications, quotations, and binders.

In addition to their technical expertise, the Underwriter should have excellent networking abilities and the capacity to establish relationships with retail brokers. The ability to effectively promote insurance products is also a crucial skill. Moreover, the candidate should possess a solid executive presence and excel in communication and influence. They must cultivate strong relationships that benefit AXIS and contribute to long-term strategic goals. 

Work Profile 

Based in one of our offices, this position provides a hybrid work environment three days a week. Roughly 25% of travel is necessary to meet with brokers and clients and participate in industry and company events.

What will you do in this role?

  • Establish themselves as a “go-to” person for builder’s risk with brokers and customers through demonstrating expertise in the field.
  • Analyze and qualify opportunities based on the organization’s appetite and be able to communicate such effectively.
  • Underwrite within the underwriting governance framework.
  • Negotiate pricing, terms and conditions, and participation on risks that meet appetite and sound underwriting judgment.
  • Develop relationships with our broker partners to support desired business retention. Work with our customers and brokers to identify their insurance needs and provide recommendations and possible solutions.
  • Proactively be in the market to seek out new business opportunities.
  • Manage their portfolio (both new and renewal) in support of the organizational goals.
  • Attend industry functions and professional events as a respected member of the AXIS team.
  • Conduct partnership or relationship meetings with our brokers and customers to identify areas of success and improvement.
  • Work collaboratively with colleagues across the organization to meet our customers' needs.
  • May be asked to participate in training or support for lower-level underwriters or underwriting assistants.

About You:

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While we need you to have some qualifications and experiences, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge might lend itself to fulfilling this role and helping us achieve our goals.

What you need to have:

  • 5+ years of builder’s risk underwriting experience focused on accounts with TIV greater than $200 million
  • Proven track record delivering profitable results.
  • In-depth knowledge of builder’s risk, including coverage, pricing, and marketplace dynamics.
  • Able to analyze risks and communicate underwriting concepts or position well to audiences of varying experience.
  • Able to work autonomously as well as in a team setting.
  • Capable of handling time constraints for quoting new and renewal business.

What we prefer you to have:

  • Understanding of both admitted and non-admitted / Excess & Surplus underwriting framework.
  • Underwriting expertise in large and complex risks.
  • Established retail broker relationships in their relative market/territory.
  • Creative problem-solving skills.

You will also be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package that includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.

Senior Director, Executive Recruitment, Talent Intelligence & Advisory

Job Family Grouping:

Human Resources


Job Family:

Talent Acquisition / Executive Recruitment


How does this role contribute to our collective success?

The Senior Director, Executive Recruitment, Talent Intelligence & Advisory serves as AXIS' lead advisor on executive talent acquisition, external succession intelligence, and strategic leadership hiring. Reporting to the Global Head of Talent Acquisition, this individual partners directly with the CEO, Executive Committee (EXCO), senior business leaders, and Human Resources leadership to identify, assess, attract, and advise on executive talent decisions that support the organization's long-term business strategy and leadership objectives.

This role combines the disciplines of executive search, talent intelligence, market mapping, competitive talent research, leadership assessment, and executive advisory. The successful candidate will lead highly visible executive and mission-critical searches while building and maintaining external succession pipelines for critical leadership positions across the enterprise.

The Senior Director will provide an external market perspective to senior leadership, helping inform executive hiring decisions, succession planning discussions, organizational design considerations, and future leadership capability needs. The role requires exceptional judgment, executive presence, intellectual curiosity, discretion, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders through data, insight, and market intelligence.


What will you do in this role?

  • Lead end-to-end executive and senior leadership searches globally across all business functions.
  • Partner with the CEO, EXCO, Board-facing executives, and senior Group/P&L leaders to define leadership requirements and develop search strategies.
  • Design and execute search plans including market mapping, target company identification, candidate engagement, assessment methodology, stakeholder alignment, and offer strategy.
  • Personally identify, engage, assess, and recruit senior executive talent, including highly passive candidates.
  • Develop and present executive candidate slates supported by market intelligence and candidate assessment insights.
  • Facilitate executive interview processes, stakeholder calibration discussions, and finalist evaluations.
  • Partner with Total Rewards, Legal, HR, and business leaders on executive offer development, negotiation, and closing strategies.
  • Deliver a differentiated executive candidate experience reflective of AXIS's leadership brand and culture.
  • Develop and maintain executive talent maps and external succession pipelines for enterprise-critical leadership roles.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership regarding executive talent strategy, market intelligence, organizational capability, and succession planning.
  • Manage executive assessment processes, external search firms, and strategic talent intelligence partnerships.
  • Drive operational excellence, governance, compliance, reporting, and continuous improvement across executive recruitment activities.

You may also be required to take on additional duties, responsibilities, and activities appropriate to the nature of this role.


About You

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table, so while there are some qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge might lend itself to fulfilling this role and helping us achieve our goals.


What you need to have:

  • Bachelor's Degree or equivalent combination of education and professional experience.
  • Minimum of 10+ years of progressive experience in executive search, executive recruitment, talent intelligence, talent advisory, or related talent acquisition disciplines.
  • Minimum of 7 years leading executive or senior leadership searches with direct responsibility for search strategy, market mapping, executive assessment, candidate engagement, stakeholder management, and offer completion.
  • Demonstrated experience partnering directly with C-suite executives, Executive Committee members, or equivalent senior business leaders.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting executive market mapping, talent intelligence, competitive talent analysis, or succession-related research initiatives.
  • Experience developing executive candidate assessments, market intelligence reports, leadership profiles, and executive presentations.
  • Experience identifying and recruiting passive executive talent.
  • Experience managing retained executive search firms and external talent partners.
  • Demonstrated experience leading multiple concurrent executive searches and confidential talent initiatives.
  • Experience advising senior business leaders on executive talent decisions.
  • Working knowledge of executive recruiting technologies, applicant tracking systems, talent intelligence platforms, CRM systems, LinkedIn Recruiter, and executive research tools.
  • Ability to travel globally as business needs require.

What we prefer you to have:

  • Experience working within insurance, reinsurance, financial services, professional services, consulting, or similarly complex global organizations.
  • Experience supporting CEO, Board, Executive Committee, or enterprise-critical recruitment initiatives.
  • Experience conducting external succession planning and executive talent benchmarking projects.
  • Experience advising senior executives regarding organizational design, leadership capability, and executive talent strategy.
  • Experience recruiting leaders with significant P&L responsibility and enterprise-wide accountability.
  • Experience conducting executive recruiting and talent intelligence activities across multiple geographies and international markets.
  • Experience managing highly confidential leadership, succession, or organizational-change initiatives.
  • Experience utilizing AI-enabled recruiting, talent intelligence, or market research tools.
  • Advanced degree or professional certification related to executive search, leadership assessment, human resources, talent acquisition, or organizational effectiveness.

Role Factors

In this role, you will typically be required to:

  • Travel globally as business needs require.

The Pricing team has responsibility for developing consistent pricing practices across the AXIS Insurance segment and is primarily responsible for pricing, product and portfolio monitoring and construction, profitability studies, new business / product development, price adequacy metric development and monitoring, and business planning. Job Description: Head of Enterprise Portfolio & Delivery


Role purpose

The Head of Enterprise Portfolio & Delivery is accountable for ensuring AXIS deploys its technology and AI investments against the highest-value enterprise priorities and delivers those investments predictably with measurable business outcomes. The role leads enterprise portfolio planning, prioritization, investment governance and delivery-performance oversight, providing leadership with clear insight and recommendations on value, capacity, risk and execution. The role will also continue to mature AXIS’ Agile business-technology delivery model, strengthening accountabilities, decision rights, ways of working and delivery discipline.

The role leads the divisional Portfolio Leads across North America, Reinsurance & CUO, Global Markets, Claims and Corporate, and reports to the Head of Technology & AI Strategy.

The role goes well beyond portfolio reporting. Building on the foundations AXIS put in place over the past year, the focus now is pace and value: running the portfolio engine behind our enterprise planning and governance cadence, proactively finding and fixing root causes in troubled programs, and coaching Portfolio Leads and delivery teams to build that same capability across the organization.

Job Responsibilities

Strategic Portfolio Governance & Planning

  • Planning & Prioritization: Bring a strategic, enterprise lens to the planning cycle, working with Transformation Leads and Value Stream Leads to set the right level of ambition for each division, so that demand is prioritized by business value, capacity is committed to each division’s value stream, and every investment is tied to OKRs and business case benefits.
  • Executive Decision Framing: Shape the agenda and recommendations for enterprise portfolio and investment forums. Rather than collating submissions, pressure-test the evidence on value, financials, capacity and dependencies with teams, refine proposals until they are decision-ready, frame the trade-offs leadership needs to make, and follow decisions through to closure.
  • Stage Gating & Readiness: Own project readiness and stage gating, proportionate to size and risk, as a real challenge rather than a compliance check. Probe whether the problem, scope, plan, business case and delivery approach are credible, send back proposals that are not ready, and confirm key partners (e.g., vendor management, security, data compliance, finance, architecture, AI governance) have reviewed and signed off before work starts.
  • Governance Framework: Set lean, proportionate portfolio governance with clear mandates and decision rights, focused on outcomes over process, and evolve it as the delivery model matures.

Funding, Value & Performance


  • Capacity-Based Funding: With FP&A, shape annual capacity allocation across divisions and value streams, and drive quarterly start/scale/pause/stop decisions and in-year moves based on value and delivery evidence.
  • Investment Evaluation: Challenge business cases before funding, testing assumptions, alternatives and fully loaded costs and benefits, and hold divisions to one consistent benefit-tracking approach so committed benefits are tracked through to realization.
  • AI Investment Portfolio: Manage the portfolio of AI use cases from idea to scaled value, working with AI governance, so that AI investments are prioritized, scaled or stopped based on evidence; and use AI within portfolio management to predict delivery risk and automate portfolio insight.
  • OKRs & Reporting: Run the enterprise approach for cascading and tracking OKRs and KPIs, and provide leadership with one view of value and delivery predictability (e.g., features delivered in-quarter, idea-to-release cycle time), automated from ADO and supported by AI where possible.

Problem Projects & Root-Cause Resolution


  • Proactive Intervention: Use portfolio data and early-warning signals (e.g., slipping milestones, benefits at risk, rising cost, unresolved dependencies) to identify projects in trouble, and lead the deep-dive on the most critical ones.
  • Diagnosis & Resolution: Get beyond symptoms to root causes (e.g., unclear ownership, unrealistic plans, capacity or skills gaps, vendor performance, dependent-team delays). Bring business and technology teams together to agree recovery options (re-plan, re-scope, re-sequence, add capacity, pause or stop) and follow through to resolution.
  • Learning Loop: Turn recurring causes into fixes in standards, readiness criteria, planning practices and vendor management so problems do not repeat.

Portfolio Lead Leadership

  • Lead & Coach: Lead, coach and develop the divisional Portfolio Leads to one consistent standard. Coach them to act as operating partners to the Transformation Lead and Value Stream Lead rather than reporters: challenging and shaping portfolio direction, diagnosing root causes on troubled projects and influencing course corrections.
  • Delivery-Health View: Ensure each Portfolio Lead gives their division a consolidated view of budget, scope, resourcing, risk and schedule, built from the teams’ own tools (e.g., Azure DevOps (ADO)) rather than manual reporting.
  • Capability: Run a Portfolio Lead community of practice, deliver role-based training and build a bench of portfolio talent.

Business-Technology Delivery Model

  • Delivery Model Maturity: Continue to mature AXIS’ agile business-technology delivery model across structure, governance, ways of working, culture & talent, and tooling & technology, so that delivery becomes faster, more predictable and more clearly tied to business value.
  • Ways of Working & Coaching: Own the business-technology delivery playbook and standards, and coach delivery teams hands-on to adopt them, working alongside teams on live work rather than issuing guidance.
  • Maturity Measurement: Set leading and lagging metrics against a baseline to track the maturity of the delivery model, and refine the model based on evidence.

What Success Looks Like (18–24 Months)

  • Technology and AI spend tied to quantifiable OKRs, with evidence ready for every quarterly review
  • Measurable maturity gains in the Agile business-technology delivery model against baseline
  • Delivery predictability against annual aspirations; benefits delivered vs. plan
  • Troubled projects identified early and recovered, with fewer repeat issues
  • A strong, engaged Portfolio Lead team, and positive teammate sentiment on the changes

Qualifications


  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, computer science, finance, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Proven experience in portfolio and project management, strategic planning, or a related field, including leading an enterprise portfolio function and a team of portfolio leads.
  • Track record of leading an enterprise agile delivery or product operating model transformation, including value stream funding and OKRs, and of turning around troubled programs.
  • Experience presenting investment trade-offs and recommendations to an Executive Committee.
  • Preferred: Insurance or financial services experience.

Skills & Attributes

  • Problem Solving: Structures ambiguous problems, gets to root causes quickly and drives practical solutions through to resolution.
  • Influence Without Authority: Builds alignment and drives action across business, technology and vendor leaders outside direct authority, and coaches rather than commands.
  • Communication: Clear, concise and compelling, able to turn complex portfolio data into decision-ready insight for the Executive Committee and to have candid conversations when projects are off track.
  • Financial & Delivery Acumen: Builds and challenges business cases, understands capex/opex and capacity-based funding, and uses delivery metrics (e.g., predictability, cycle time, benefits realization) to drive decisions.

Job Description: Chief of Staff to the Group COO


Position Summary


The Chief of Staff to the Group COO serves as the strategic execution partner to the Group COO, ensuring alignment, execution discipline, and measurable value delivery across AXIS's Operations, Data & Analytics, Technology, AI, Transformation, Architecture, and Information Security portfolios. Based on the current AXIS role profile, the Chief of Staff acts as the strategic extension of the Group COO and the primary integration point across these functions.

This role converts strategy into action by driving portfolio governance, operating cadence, value realization, cross-functional execution, and executive decision support. The Chief of Staff enables the Group COO to focus on the highest-value strategic, operating, talent, and investment decisions while ensuring accountability for execution and outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & COO Agenda

  • Shape and manage the Group COO's enterprise agenda and strategic priorities.
  • Integrate Operations, Technology, Data & Analytics, AI, and Transformation into a unified operating model and execution roadmap.
  • Surface key trade-offs, dependencies, risks, and recommendations for decision-making

Portfolio Management & Value Realization

  • Maintain oversight of the COO portfolio, including investment priorities, benefits realization, execution health, and resource allocation.
  • Ensure major initiatives have clear business outcomes, ownership, success metrics, and accountability.
  • Challenge initiatives that are not delivering measurable business value.

Enterprise Execution & Transformation

  • Drive coordination across complex cross-functional initiatives.
  • Resolve interdependencies, delivery obstacles, and organizational barriers.
  • Ensure transformation efforts produce sustainable business outcomes rather than activity-based progress.

Data, Technology & AI Leadership

  • Act as the COO's integration point across Data & Analytics, Technology, AI, Architecture, and Operations.
  • Ensure investments are aligned to underwriting advantage, operational effectiveness, scalability, and business growth.
  • Support responsible AI adoption, governance, workforce readiness, and value realization.

Operations & Underwriting Support Effectiveness

  • Partner with Operations and Underwriting leadership to improve capacity, efficiency, resilience, service quality, and scalability.
  • Drive process modernization, workflow redesign, automation, and AI-enabled operating model improvements.
  • Support AXIS's objective of increasing underwriting capacity without proportionate increases in operational cost or headcount.

Governance, Risk & Resilience

  • Operate the management cadence for the COO organization, including strategic reviews, investment governance, risk reviews, and performance management.
  • Maintain visibility of operational, technology, cyber, AI, third-party, and execution risks.
  • Track and coordinate significant audit, regulatory, control, and remediation commitments.

Executive & Board Support

  • Prepare the Group COO for ExCo, Board, and executive leadership discussions.
  • Develop concise, decision-oriented materials, recommendations, and executive-level analyses.
  • Ensure consistent messaging across the COO portfolio.

Experience & Qualifications

  • Senior leadership experience in Operations, Strategy, Transformation, Technology, Data & Analytics, AI, or Enterprise Program Leadership.
  • Experience operating within a complex, regulated financial services or insurance environment.
  • Proven ability to lead large-scale cross-functional initiatives and influence senior executives without direct authority.
  • Strong commercial, financial, operational, and strategic acumen.
  • Working knowledge of technology, data, AI, governance, risk, and organizational design.

Leadership Capabilities

  • Enterprise thinker with strong business judgment.
  • Strategic, outcome-oriented, and execution-focused.
  • Excellent executive communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Strong financial and value-realization mindset.
  • Ability to challenge constructively and drive accountability.
  • Trusted advisor capable of operating effectively with senior leadership and the Board.

Success Measures

The Chief of Staff will be successful when:

  • The Group COO agenda is clear, focused, and effectively executed.
  • Strategic investments deliver measurable business value.
  • Cross-functional execution is coordinated and predictable.
  • Technology, AI, and data initiatives improve underwriting and operational performance.
  • Risks, dependencies, and remediation activities are proactively managed.
  • Executive and Board discussions are concise, fact-based, and decision-oriented.
