Senior Manager, Quality Assurance and Compliance | North America Claims, Claims Shared Services-

AXIS is seeking a Senior Manager, Quality Assurance and Audit, North America Claims to join the Claims Shared Services team. Reporting to the Head of Quality Assurance and Compliance, Claims Shared Services, this role will lead, oversee, enhance and optimize the North America claim direct handle, manager quality review and TPA oversight audit program. The role will also coordinate, oversee, and enhance the North America Claims SIU and Fraud program.

The successful candidate will plan, coordinate, monitor, and report on audits and quality file reviews across North America Claims, including specialty claim handler audits across multiple lines of business, TPA oversight audits, and leadership quality control file reviews. Incumbent may be responsible for technical file reviews. The role will manage audit execution through internal stakeholders and external audit partners, track findings through closure, report results to leadership, and use audit insights to strengthen claim handling quality, compliance, consistency, and operational performance.

This role is ideal for a claims, audit, quality assurance, or compliance professional with strong technical claims judgment, experience assessing specialty claim handler performance, working knowledge of TPA or outsourced claims partner oversight, and the ability to translate audit and file review results into practical actions that improve claim outcomes.

The successful Candidate will be responsible for:

Claims Audit Program Management
• Lead and report on the North America claim handler audit program, TPA oversight audit program, and leadership quality control file review program across multiple lines of business.
• Manage end-to-end audit execution, including planning, scope, scheduling, sample selection, file collection, stakeholder communications, and audit readiness.
• Coordinate with claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPAs, audit vendors, Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, and Operations to ensure consistent, timely audit delivery.
• Enhance audit standards, questionnaires, scorecards, and methodologies in line with claim best practices, regulatory expectations, and technical excellence standards.
• Review audit observations across coverage, liability, damages, reserving, litigation management, settlement strategy, documentation quality, compliance, and claim handling controls.
• Track findings, action plans, remediation activities, owner accountability, due dates, and closure evidence.

Audit Results, Analytics, and Reporting
• Gather, validate, and analyze audit results, quality assurance data, compliance findings, and technical claim handling trends.
• Develop dashboards, scorecards, and management reports covering quality review results, technical audit outcomes, recurring themes, risk areas, trends, and improvement opportunities.
• Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting for Claims leadership and governance forums, covering claim handler audit results, TPA oversight audit results, and leadership quality control file review outcomes.
• Measure audit effectiveness, remediation progress, transparency, accountability, and control discipline.

Compliance, Controls, and Remediation
• Partner with Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, Claims Operations, and Claims Leadership to align audit activity with regulatory, governance, and operational risk priorities.
• Monitor findings related to Medicare, regulatory obligations, documentation standards, claim handling controls, and other compliance requirements.
• Maintain action plans that address findings, strengthen controls, and promote consistent claim handling across North America specialty claim teams, TPA claim programs, and leadership quality control file reviews.
• Escalate material issues, recurring trends, control gaps, and remediation delays to appropriate leaders and governance forums.

SIU and Fraud Audit Program
• Enhance, measure, and report on the SIU and fraud deliverable program as part of the North America claims audit program.
• Assess whether SIU and fraud deliverables are timely, complete, consistent, and aligned with claim handling expectations, regulatory obligations, and technical audit standards.
• Identify themes, control gaps, escalation issues, documentation weaknesses, and opportunities to improve fraud identification, referral quality, and SIU oversight.
• Partner with SIU, Compliance, Claims leadership, TPAs, and audit vendors to strengthen execution, reporting, accountability, and remediation follow-through.

Technical Excellence and Continuous Improvement
• Use audit and quality control file review insights to improve technical claim quality, consistency, reserving discipline, litigation management, settlement practices, and compliance execution.
• Support updates to claims guidelines, audit protocols, procedures, workflows, controls, and training materials based on audit trends and root-cause analysis.
• Provide practical recommendations to claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPAs, and business partners to improve claim outcomes and audit performance.
• Participate in governance meetings, working groups, and initiatives related to claims quality, audit readiness, and technical excellence.

Stakeholder Management
• Build effective relationships across North America Claims, specialty claim teams, TPAs, Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, Actuarial, Finance, Operations, and Shared Services.
• Manage day-to-day coordination with external audit vendors, including schedules, deliverables, issue tracking, reporting inputs, and performance expectations.
• Provide audit and quality assurance subject matter support to claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPA managers, and governance stakeholders.
• Communicate findings, themes, risks, and recommendations clearly to management and senior leadership.

Skills
• 6–10 years of experience in commercial P&C insurance, reinsurance, specialty claims, claims audit, quality assurance, compliance, operational risk, or a related discipline.

Technical skills or claims management adjusting experience preferred.
• Minimum 3 years of experience supporting or managing claims audits, quality assurance reviews, compliance monitoring, operational controls, or remediation tracking.

We are seeking an Enterprise Test & Quality Lead to provide end-to-end ownership of testing across development, QA, UAT, and release activities. This role is accountable for defining and governing the test strategy, coordinating testing across multiple concurrent delivery teams, improving environment and test data readiness, and ensuring that releases meet agreed quality and business acceptance criteria. The role is particularly important in a delivery context where shared environments, constrained non-production data, and cross-team dependencies require disciplined planning, strong stakeholder management, and clear operational control.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the end-to-end test management lifecycle across Unit Testing, System Integration Testing, QA, UAT, regression testing, and release readiness.

  • Define and drive a Quality Engineering strategy embedding automated testing across the SDLC including “shift-left” and “shift-right” practices.

  • Define and maintain the overall test strategy, test plans, phase entry and exit criteria, acceptance thresholds, and defect management approach. Work and align with incumbent vendor to align QA to this overall strategy.

  • Define and enforce automated quality gates within CI/CD pipelines.

  • Coordinate testing across multiple concurrent scrum teams, ensuring alignment of delivery schedules, dependencies, and release milestones.

  • Define an environment strategy that enables parallel team execution, minimizes contention, and supports continuous testing.

  • Ownership of Test Data Governance Framework

  • o Ensure adherence and support from DPO / IRM / Privacy

  • Own the approach to Test Data Management, including data readiness, lineage, masking or obfuscation controls, and interim solutions required to support testing safely and effectively.

  • Partner with QA leads to define test scenarios, test cases, regression coverage, and the appropriate level of automation, including use of tools such as Tosca to deliver ROI driven automation, decisions on what to automate and coverage targets. 

  • KPI Management of QA vendor

  • SLA tracking

  • Capability and skill matrix optimization.

  • Trend analysis of defect origin (code, data, environment, design) leading to systemic issue elimination

  • Work with Product Owners and business stakeholders to secure UAT participation, define UAT scripts and acceptance criteria, and manage UAT execution to completion.

  • The Test Manager should be a critical input into the release management go / no go stage gate decisions.

  • Manage defect triage, retest cycles, and regression planning to ensure efficient resolution and minimal disruption to completed testing.

  • Provide decision grade insights on test progress, risks, defect trends, environment readiness, and overall release confidence to project and executive stakeholders.

  • Drive continuous improvement in test practices, with a focus on moving from reactive or waterfall-like testing toward a more agile, disciplined, and scalable operating model.

  • Define and oversee post release validation strategies, including observability, monitoring, and production quality feedback loops.

  • Skills and Experience

  • Proven experience in Test Management, QA leadership, or quality engineering leadership within complex technology delivery environments.

  • Strong understanding of end-to-end software testing practices across unit, integration, system, regression, data lineage and user acceptance testing.

  • Experience managing testing in agile delivery environments with multiple concurrent teams and shared environments.

  • Practical knowledge of test automation and engineering led strategy and tooling, ideally including Tosca or comparable platforms, especially AI driven technologies and processes.

  • Strong understanding of environment management and test data management, including handling of sensitive data in non-production environments.

  • Ability to define quality gates, release readiness criteria, and structured defect management processes.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work across engineering, QA, product, operations, and business teams.

  • Excellent planning, coordination, and communication skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and delivery risk.

  • Experience in regulated or control-conscious environments is highly desirable.

  • Experience of integrating testing into DevOps pipelines and familiarity with release orchestration and production validation techniques.

  • Experience of operating in SAFe (scaled agile) frameworks


Success Measures

  • Improved coordination and predictability across QA and UAT cycles including continuous validation and early user involvement.

  • Reduction in defects caused by environment or data issues rather than true functional failures.

  • Clear and consistently applied phase entry, exit, and acceptance criteria.

  • Increased confidence in release readiness and reduced rework or defect recycling.

  • Greater use of automation and regression coverage to support faster retest cycles.

  • Stronger governance, visibility, and accountability for end-to-end testing outcomes.


Key Interfaces
This role will work closely with Development Leads, QA Leads, Product Owners, Business UAT representatives, Environment and Release Management teams, Data and Privacy stakeholders, and senior programme or technology leadership.
Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • Relevant testing or quality certifications such as ISTQB Advanced Test Manager or equivalent are desirable.

  • Experience in insurance, financial services, or other highly regulated delivery environments would be advantageous.

North America Casualty Treaty Reinsurance Underwriter


Job Family Grouping

AXIS Re - Underwriting

Job Family

AXIS Re - Underwriting | Underwriters

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

Reporting to the Head of North America General Casualty and Workers Compensation, AXIS Re, the successful candidate will underwrite and manage a portfolio of North American General Casualty and Workers Compensation Treaty Reinsurance business. The role will contribute to Business Unit profit goals, portfolio strategy, client and broker engagement, and disciplined cycle management across General Liability, Workers Compensation, Commercial Auto Liability, Umbrella/Excess Liability, and other casualty classes within the team's appetite.

What will you do in this role?

·   Originate, analyze, price, structure, negotiate, and underwrite North America general casualty and workers compensation treaty business in accordance with underwriting guidelines, portfolio appetite, allocated authority, and established best practices.

·   Manage assigned renewals and new-business opportunities across proportional and non-proportional treaty structures, including quota share, surplus share, working excess, and catastrophe or clash protections, as applicable.

·   Assess cedent strategy, management, underwriting controls, distribution, claims practices, reserving, rate adequacy, exposure trends, and historical performance to develop a clear underwriting view.

·   Partner with actuarial, claims, contract wording, finance, and legal colleagues to evaluate treaty economics, key assumptions, terms and conditions, and potential volatility.

·   Build and maintain strong relationships with reinsurance intermediaries and cedent clients to support profitable business origination, retention, and long-term strategic partnerships.

·   Contribute to casualty strategy and portfolio management, including appetite, guidelines, aggregate and limit management, concentration monitoring, and deployment of capacity.

·   Monitor market conditions and casualty loss drivers, including social inflation, litigation trends, legal and regulatory developments, medical inflation, loss-cost trends, and changes in underlying policy terms.

·   Prepare clear underwriting referrals, portfolio updates, and recommendations for senior leadership and governance forums.

·   Participate in cedent underwriting audits, claims reviews, stewardship meetings, and ongoing monitoring of account performance.

·   Maintain accurate and timely underwriting documentation, pricing records, exposure data, and internal system entries.

·   Travel to service clients, meet brokers, conduct audits, and attend industry conferences and market events.

You may also be required to take on additional duties, responsibilities, and activities appropriate to the nature of this role.

About You

You are a hands-on casualty treaty underwriting professional with strong technical judgment and a record of building and managing a complex book of reinsurance business. You understand the treaty underwriting lifecycle, from submission review and portfolio analysis through pricing, structuring, negotiation, authorization, documentation, and post-bind monitoring. You bring professional presence, commercial judgment, and the ability to communicate, influence, and build relationships that add value to the AXIS Re portfolio and support longer-term strategic initiatives.

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While there are qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge may help you succeed in this role and contribute to our goals.

What you need to have

·   Demonstrated casualty underwriting, reinsurance underwriting, broking, actuarial, or related experience with a strong understanding of North American casualty business.

·   Knowledge of General Casualty and Workers Compensation, with familiarity across Commercial Auto Liability, Umbrella/Excess Liability, General Liability and related casualty classes.

·   Working knowledge of actuarial and pricing concepts, including experience partnering with actuarial teams to evaluate and price reinsurance treaties.

·   Ability to assess exposure and experience data, loss development, rate and exposure change, limits, retentions, attachment points, and treaty economics.

·   Strong grasp of underlying policy forms, reinsurance contract wording, exclusions, claims issues, and the roles of claims, actuarial, legal, accounting, and finance in the underwriting process.

·   Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to audiences at all levels, including executive leadership.

·   Strong analytical, negotiation, marketing, and influencing skills, with sound judgment when faced with ambiguity or changing priorities.

·   Client-focused approach and flexibility in developing solutions that meet client needs while maintaining underwriting discipline.

·   Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple submissions, renewals, and peak-period workflows.

·   Highly collaborative and versatile, with the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a cross-functional team.

·   Ability to initiate and independently lead defined projects and portfolio initiatives.

·   Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline or equivalent industry experience.

What we prefer you to have

·   CPCU, ARe, ACAS, FCAS, ARM, or other relevant industry designation.

·   A minimum of five years of casualty insurance, reinsurance underwriting, actuarial, claims, or broking experience.

·   Experience underwriting or analyzing both proportional and non-proportional casualty treaty structures.

·   Established relationships with reinsurance brokers and North American casualty insurers.

·   Effective strategic relationship management and portfolio management skills.

·   Advanced Excel capability, including lookup functions, PivotTables, and analysis across multiple data sets.

·   Experience building dashboards or data models using Power BI.

·   Experience with AI Assistants a plus. 

·   Based in the New York City area or another approved AXIS office location.

Role Factors

·   Travel to visit clients and brokers, conduct underwriting audits, and attend industry conferences. 

·   Be in the office, or visiting brokers or clients, three days per week.

·   Attend broker and client events as required, including evenings and some weekend travel. 

What we offer

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $185,000 - $250,000. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors, including your specific experience and work location.

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate performance and your individual performance. You will also be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package that includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and more.

Job Description: Technology and AI Strategy Lead


How does this role contribute to our collective success?

AXIS is undertaking a multi-year transformation to strengthen how we operate,

serve customers, and create competitive advantage. Technology and AI are important enablers of this transformation, creating opportunities to improve operational effectiveness, support business growth, and enhance customer outcomes.


The Technology & AI Strategy Lead is responsible for shaping, maintaining, and driving execution of the enterprise technology and AI agenda in partnership with business, technology, data, risk, and functional leaders. The role owns the integrated strategic agenda, enterprise-level recommendations, strategic coherence, value framework, and executive decision support. It does not own delivery of individual products or programs; delivery remains with the relevant business and technology owners, and business leaders remain accountable for outcomes, adoption, and benefit realization.


The role provides independent analysis, subject matter expertise, and strategic recommendations that help leadership evaluate technology and AI opportunities, risks, and trade-offs. Success requires strong business acumen, strategic thinking, stakeholder engagement, and the ability to translate complex technology concepts into practical business implications and measurable outcomes.
________________________________________

Key Responsibilities

Director, Talent Management & Workforce Readiness

Job Family Grouping: Human Resources

Job Family: Talent Development

Grade: F

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

This role designs and drives AXIS's talent management and workforce readiness agenda in partnership with HR and business leaders, ensuring the organization has the leadership, skills, capabilities, and talent required to deliver business priorities today and in the future. You will establish and continuously improve the frameworks, processes, and insights that support performance, talent, succession, and workforce decisions across the organization. This is a talent management role with a workforce readiness component; learning and development experience alone will not meet the requirements. Success will be measured through stronger leadership pipelines, improved workforce readiness, effective talent decisions, and the organization's ability to build the capabilities needed for future growth.


What will you do in this role?

·       You will design, drive, and continuously improve AXIS's core talent management processes, including goal setting, performance management, talent reviews, assessments, succession planning, and development planning. You will establish clear frameworks and governance that support high-quality talent decisions and stronger leadership pipelines.

·       You will drive workforce readiness efforts by helping the business understand the leadership, skills, capabilities, and talent needed to deliver future priorities. You will assess workforce gaps, use internal and external talent intelligence, and identify actions to build, buy, borrow, reskill, redeploy, or automate capabilities.

·       You will identify development needs and priorities through performance, talent, succession, assessment, and workforce planning insights. You will partner with the Head of Learning to ensure development programs and investments address the organization's most important leadership, skill, and capability gaps; this role does not own learning program design or delivery.

·       You will partner with business leaders, HR Business Partners, the COO organization, and transformation teams to assess the workforce impact of changes in business strategy, technology, AI, and how work gets done. You will translate those changes into clear recommendations for skills, roles, workforce planning, mobility, succession, and talent investments.

·       You will use talent data, workforce intelligence, assessments, and external market insights to identify risks and opportunities and provide practical recommendations to senior leaders. You will monitor the health and effectiveness of talent and workforce practices and use insights to improve them over time.

·       You will lead and develop the Talent Operations & HR Business Analyst, manage key external partners, and work across HR and the business to deliver priorities, strengthen manager capability, and drive adoption of talent management and workforce readiness practices.

You may also be required to take on additional duties, responsibilities and activities appropriate to the nature of this role.


About You:

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While there are some qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge could help you fulfil this role and contribute to our goals.


What you need to have:

·       10+ years of progressive HR experience, including at least 5 years of direct responsibility for designing, leading, or significantly evolving core talent management processes such as performance management, talent reviews, assessments, succession planning, and development planning at an enterprise or business-unit level.

·       2+ years of experience translating business strategy into future workforce, skills, or capability requirements through strategic workforce planning, skills strategy, organization transformation, workforce analytics, or a closely related discipline.

·       Demonstrated experience designing and implementing talent frameworks, governance, and processes across multiple businesses, functions, or geographies.

·       Demonstrated experience influencing senior leaders and using talent data, workforce intelligence, and business insights to support decisions.

·       Experience assessing complex talent and workforce issues, identifying risks and opportunities, and translating findings into clear recommendations and actions.

·       Experience leading enterprise-wide change, managing competing priorities, and driving adoption through HR Business Partners and people managers.

·       Experience leading and developing a team member, managing external partners, and collaborating effectively across HR and the business.

·       Demonstrated ability to handle sensitive talent, assessment, succession, and workforce information with discretion and sound judgment.


What we prefer you to have:

·       Direct experience with strategic workforce planning, skills-based workforce strategies, talent intelligence, or workforce transformation. Candidates are not expected to have equal depth in talent management and workforce planning, but must demonstrate credible experience across both.

·       Experience assessing how AI, automation, and evolving ways of working affect roles, skills, capacity, and talent needs.

·       Experience using Workday or similar technology to support talent and workforce processes.

·       Experience selecting, implementing, or governing assessment solutions that support talent and leadership decisions.

·       Experience in insurance, financial services, or another highly regulated global industry.

Be in the office 3 days per week

Travel domestically and internationally as business needs require

Claims Lead – Grade I

Job Family Grouping: Claims Group

Job Family: Claims Specialist

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

The Claims Specialist plays an important role in protecting AXIS Re's balance sheet, reputation, and client relationships through the timely, accurate, and consistent handling of reinsurance claims. The role supports effective claim resolution, sound reserving practices, and high-quality service to internal and external stakeholders while ensuring compliance with contractual obligations and regulatory requirements.

By working closely with underwriting, actuarial, finance, brokers, cedents, and fellow claims professionals, the Claims Specialist contributes to loss analysis, reserve monitoring, and portfolio understanding. Through disciplined claim management and effective communication, the role helps deliver reliable claims outcomes and supports informed business decision-making. Through effective communication and knowledge sharing, the Claims Specialist helps bridge the gap between claims activity, business strategy, and operational decision-making. The role transforms complex claims information, loss data, and emerging risk developments into practical insights that support underwriting, actuarial, finance, and management stakeholders.

Ultimately, the Claims Specialist helps AXIS Re maintain strong claims governance, operational excellence, and trusted client service while supporting the broader objectives of the Reinsurance Claims team.

What will you do in this role?


  • Handle assigned reinsurance claims and claim portfolios in accordance with AXIS Re claims guidelines, delegated authorities, contractual obligations, and regulatory requirements.
  • Ensure claims are promptly and accurately documented, evaluated, reserved, and processed throughout the claim lifecycle.
  • Analyze claim submissions, loss notices, and supporting documentation to assess coverage, liability, financial exposure, and reporting requirements.
  • Identify and escalate coverage issues, large losses, accumulation concerns, and other material developments in a timely manner.
  • Maintain case reserves and monitor claim activity and loss development on assigned accounts.
  • Partner with underwriting, actuarial, finance, and legal teams to support effective claim management and informed business decision making.
  • Communicate directly with brokers, cedants, and other stakeholders regarding claim developments, information requests, coverage matters, and reporting requirements.
  • Participate in claims audits, including audit planning, file selection, audit attendance, preparation of audit reports, and communication of findings and recommendations.
  • Monitor legal, regulatory, and market developments that may impact claims handling, reserving practices, or portfolio performance.
  • Maintain high-quality claim files and ensure accurate, complete, and reliable claims data within company systems.
  • Contribute to management reporting, portfolio reviews, and other initiatives that support effective oversight of the claims portfolio.
  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including underwriting, actuarial, finance, brokers, cedants, auditors, and service providers.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives that enhance claims handling practices, operational efficiency, reporting capabilities, and data quality.
  • Assist in the development and maintenance of training materials, desk guides, reference tools, and process documentation to promote consistency and operational effectiveness across the Claims team.
  • Translate complex claims, coverage, legal, and reserving concepts into clear and concise communications tailored to a variety of business audiences.
  • Support the effective use of data, reporting tools, automation, and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence solutions, to improve workflows and business processes.
  • Collaborate across global teams and functions to improve the quality, consistency, accessibility, and usability of claims information.
  • Contribute to a culture of learning, collaboration, and continuous professional development by sharing knowledge, best practices, and lessons learned.

You may also be required to take on additional duties, responsibilities and activities appropriate to the nature of this role.

  • Minimum 3 years of experience in insurance and/or reinsurance claims handling.
  • Good understanding of insurance and reinsurance principles, coverage analysis, and claims handling practices.
  • Working knowledge of legal processes and laws applicable to insurance claims.
  • Familiarity with reinsurance customs and practices and laws applicable to reinsurance.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work collaboratively in a team environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Experience using claims management systems; knowledge of SICS is beneficial.

  • Experience handling casualty, professional liability, cyber, specialty, or other complex insurance and reinsurance claims.
  • Experience participating in claims audits, portfolio reviews, or file quality assurance initiatives.
  • Experience working directly with brokers, cedants, reinsurers, underwriters, or other external stakeholders.
  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Excel and familiarity with data visualization, reporting, or analytics tools such as Power BI.
  • Experience working in data-intensive environments and leveraging information to support business, operational, or claims-related decision making.
  • Familiarity with B2B operational processes and stakeholder engagement.
  • Interest in or experience supporting the use of automation, data solutions, artificial intelligence, or other emerging technologies within insurance or financial services environments.
  • Experience developing training materials, process documentation, job aids, or knowledge-sharing resources.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical, legal, financial, or operational concepts to a variety of audiences.
  • Experience supporting onboarding, mentoring, coaching, or training initiatives within a professional environment.
  • Knowledge of emerging issues, market developments, and trends affecting the insurance and reinsurance industry.
  • Juris Doctor (JD) designation preferred but not required.

  • Build and maintain effective working relationships with internal stakeholders including Underwriting, Actuarial, Finance, and Legal, as well as external partners such as cedants, brokers, auditors, and service providers.

The specific salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors, including the experience of the successful candidate and work location. In addition, all employees are eligible for competitive incentive opportunities based on overall corporate and individual performance.

You will also be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package, including medical plans for employees and their families, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid annual leave, and much more.

The Finance function at AXIS plays a central role in enabling enterprise strategy, capital stewardship, regulatory integrity, and performance insight. As AXIS continues to evolve, Finance is undertaking significant transformation to modernize its operating model, strengthen scalability and controls, and enhance its strategic contribution to the business.


This role sits within the CFO organization and operates as a senior Finance transformation leader, working alongside the CFO and Finance Leadership Team to modernize Finance processes, capabilities, systems and ways of working across a multi-year horizon.


How does this role contribute to our collective success?
 

The Head of Finance Transformation is accountable for shaping and delivering the Finance transformation strategy and roadmap in line with Finance priorities and AXIS business objectives. Acting as the CFO’s senior adviser on Finance transformation, the role ensures Finance has the operating model, capabilities, technology and ways of working needed to support AXIS’s strategic objectives over a multi-year horizon.


The role exists to improve Finance’s scalability, decision support, control maturity and adoption of modernized ways of working, helping Finance operate as a more integrated and insight-driven partner to the business.


Scope
 

Transformation is delivered through functional leadership, not around it. The role develops and recommends Finance transformation standards, target-state designs, and prioritization approaches, while execution accountability remains with Finance functional leaders.


The role partners across Finance (e.g., FP&A, Controllership, Finance Operations, Treasury, Investor Relations, Tax, and other Finance teams) and with enterprise partners (BTS, Data, Operations, Underwriting, Actuarial, Risk, and others) to drive integrated solutions and consistent adoption of the future state.
The role owns the Finance transformation strategy, roadmap, governance and benefits framework. The Chief of Staff integrates transformation progress, dependencies and decisions into the broader CFO agenda and executive operating cadence.


What will you do in this role?
 

  • Define and maintain the Finance Transformation strategy, roadmap, and target operating model aligned to Finance priorities and approved investment plans.
  • Serve as the senior Finance transformation adviser to the CFO, providing recommendations on transformation investment, capability development, modernization priorities and key decisions requiring CFO or Finance Leadership Team direction.
  • Shape and coordinate the Finance technology, data and analytics roadmap in partnership with BTS, Data and Risk, embedding advanced analytics and AI-enabled capabilities into Finance workflows such as forecasting, variance analysis, controls monitoring and management reporting.
  • Establish and lead governance for the Finance transformation portfolio, including recommendations on investment trade-offs, sequencing, prioritization and resource allocation to ensure initiatives are value-driven, risk-managed and controlled.
  • Build alignment across the Finance Leadership Team and key stakeholders on the Finance target operating model, transformation roadmap, design standards and adoption of future-state processes and ways of working, reinforcing accountability and addressing resistance as needed.
  • Provide oversight of major Finance transformation programs, ensuring delivery aligns to strategic intent, regulatory requirements, and enterprise risk appetite—while monitoring benefits and outcomes (efficiency, effectiveness, control strength, analytic maturity, and business value).
  • Partner with the CFO and Finance Leadership Team to evaluate Finance operating structures, resource deployment, and capability requirements needed to support future business priorities.
  • Contribute to the development and enhancement of Finance policies, operating standards, governance frameworks, and transformation practices that improve effectiveness, scalability, and organizational performance.
  • Represent Finance transformation in senior leadership forums, contributing to broader enterprise strategy and change discussions.
     

Outcomes and how success is measured
 

  • Measurable reductions in Finance cost-to-serve and improvements in cycle times (e.g., close, forecast, management reporting).
  • Finance transformation roadmap delivered against agreed milestones, with clear governance, active risk management, documented decisions, and tracked benefits realization.
  • Sustained improvement in control effectiveness, audit outcomes, and quality of regulatory engagement.
  • Improved quality, timeliness, and actionability of management and board reporting; materially better analytics supporting decision-making.
  • Increased adoption of standardized tools, processes, and data across Finance; reduced fragmentation and manual effort.
  • Clear evidence of Finance operating as a strategic business partner to underwriting, investments, and operations, with documented decision support impact.

Authority
 

To accelerate delivery and avoid transformation drift, the role is empowered—through the CFO and Finance Leadership Team—to:

  • Recommend transformation standards, target-state design principles and governance requirements for CFO and Finance Leadership Team approval.
  • Recommend prioritization, sequencing, acceleration, pausing, or redirection of initiatives to ensure focus on the highest-value outcomes.
  • Establish the governance, reporting and review cadence specifically required to oversee Finance transformation delivery, adoption and benefits realization.
  • Convene and chair cross-functional decision forums as needed to remove barriers and drive resolution.

About You – What we’re looking for
 

  • In-depth expertise in Finance transformation, including operating model design, technology enablement, analytics modernization, governance, and strategic execution.
  • Proven ability to advise executive and senior Finance leaders, influencing decisions with long-term and enterprise implications.
  • Extensive experience leading large-scale, complex transformation initiatives in highly regulated, global environments.
  • Strong enterprise judgement, balancing strategic ambition with governance, risk, and control considerations.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead through other leaders—aligning and influencing senior stakeholders without relying on direct execution ownership.
  • Strong strategic, systems, and data perspective—integrating Finance, technology, data, and operational considerations.
  • Ability to communicate complex strategic topics clearly and persuasively to Executive Leadership and senior stakeholders.

Role Factors
 

  • Significant and regular interaction with Executive Leadership and senior management across AXIS.
  • Accountability for Finance transformation outcomes, including sustained adoption, capability uplift and measurable business impact.
  • High degree of autonomy in shaping objectives, frameworks, and approaches.
  • Periodic travel will be required.
  • Hybrid or in-office presence aligned with senior leadership expectations.

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $250 - 310,000 (NY), $210 - 285,000 (IL), $220 - 295,000 (NJ), $200 - 275,000 (GA). Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. 

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.  

Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is [Exempt/Non-Exempt] for FLSA purposes.

Senior Analyst, Operational Readiness - Claims Shared Services, Axis Global Claims

AXIS is seeking a Senior Analyst, Operational Readiness, to join the Global Claims Shared Services (GCSS) team. Reporting to the Head of Optimization, Claims Shared Services, this role ensures approved technology, process, vendor and operating model changes are ready for implementation, adopted by AXIS Global Claims, and stabilized into business-as-usual operations.

The role is responsible for business readiness, cutover, adoption, operational handoff, hypercare and BAU transition, but does not own requirements, solution design, product roadmaps, project delivery or portfolio prioritization.

Working with Product Owners, business sponsors, project managers, technology teams, vendors and operational leaders, the role confirms Claims is prepared to receive, use and sustain new processes and technology.

The Successful Candidate Will Be Responsible For:

Operational Readiness & Cutover

  • Operational readiness assessments and readiness sign-off processes for approved technology, process, vendor and operating model changes, ensuring assessments are completed on time and aligned to defined go-live criteria.
  • Develop and maintain readiness frameworks, checklists and go-live criteria that establish clear expectations for operational capability, resource readiness and support model readiness.
  • Lead business cutover planning and execution activities against approved readiness, handoff and service acceptance plans.
  • Coordinate business operational handoffs and service acceptance activities, with clear ownership, success criteria and support model handoff.
  • Identify, document and escalate readiness gaps to accountable owners before implementation.
  • Establish transition-to-BAU plans, stabilization criteria and measurable success indicators for each implementation.

Training & Business Adoption

  • Implementation communications and stakeholder readiness plans, ensuring impacted users understand what is changing, when it is changing and what action is required.
  • Coordinate business training delivery and completion tracking, with the goal of meeting training completion and stakeholder preparedness targets before go-live.
  • Measure user adoption, operational utilization and preparedness to adopt new capabilities before and after implementation.
  • Identify adoption and readiness gaps before implementation and coordinate remediation with accountable owners.
  • Support post-deployment adoption reviews and feedback loops to improve future readiness execution.

Process Documentation & Knowledge Management

  • Support development of functional process maps, SOPs, workflow documentation and operational playbooks required for successful go-live and BAU transition.
  • Ensure functional process documentation remains current following operational or system changes.
  • Support establishment of centralized knowledge repositories and documentation standards that enable consistent sustainment after implementation.
  • Coordinate documentation, SOP, job aid and knowledge repository updates as part of implementation closure.

Hypercare & Stabilization

  • Lead business hypercare activities following go-live, with clear issue intake, escalation and closure disciplines.
  • Monitor adoption, operational performance and issue trends during stabilization, with focus on reducing unresolved issues and supporting faster stabilization.
  • Coordinate business inputs to issue triage, escalation and closure during the transition period.
  • Track vendor and service readiness issues, knowledge transfer actions and adherence to agreed operating procedures.
  • Coordinate lessons learned and transition closure activities, ensuring insights are captured and applied to improve future readiness, cutover and stabilization execution.

Reporting & Value Realization

  • Partner with Global MI & Insights to support adoption, utilization and benefits reporting.
  • Track readiness, stabilization, adoption and implementation outcome metrics to confirm approved changes are landing effectively.
  • Support development of implementation scorecards and executive reporting materials that highlight readiness status, adoption trends, stabilization issues and transition-to-BAU progress.
  • Assist with post-implementation reviews and outcome measurement, including lessons learned, realized benefits and continuous improvement actions.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner with Claims Operations, Claims Optimization, Compliance & QA, Third Party Management, Product Owners, Technology, Data & Analytics and Claims Business Leadership to support successful readiness outcomes.
  • Clarify readiness, cutovers, adoption and BAU handoff ownership across impacted teams.
  • Provide visibility to readiness gaps, operational dependencies and transition risks for accountable business owners to resolve.
  • Foster strong working relationships across GCSS and partner teams to ensure change lands effectively and is sustained in BAU.

Skills, Experience & Qualifications

  • 3-5 years of experience in business operations, operational readiness, project coordination, business analysis, change management, claims operations or process improvement; claims project or optimization experience preferred.
  • Experience supporting implementation, technology deployment, operational change, business transformation, vendor transition or BAU handoff activities.
  • Strong organization, communication, analytical, problem-solving and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to develop and maintain documentation, SOPs, job aids, training materials and knowledge resources.
  • Experience with claims systems, operational workflows, insurance operations, AI, automation or systems modernization preferred.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Copilot, SharePoint, Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Teams.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience required; familiarity with project management, change management or process improvement methodologies preferred.
  • Some Travel is associated with this role.

Locations

  • New Jersey
  • New York

The position is primarily focused on Employer Stop Loss, HMO/Managed Care, Medical Excess, and Provider Excess products, while also supporting the broader Specialty Accident & Health portfolio.

What You'll Do

Serve as a senior claims resource for complex, high-severity, and escalated matters, including appeals and authority referrals.

• Conduct claims and operational audits of TPAs and MGUs, report findings, and monitor corrective actions.

• Support due diligence reviews and onboarding of delegated claims partners.

• Monitor compliance with delegated authority, service standards, and claims handling guidelines.

• Coordinate responses to complaints, regulatory inquiries, attorney correspondence, carrier reviews, and benefit interpretation requests.

• Analyze claims and operational data to identify trends, emerging risks, and improvement opportunities.

• Partner across functions to support product performance, business initiatives, and process improvements.

What You'll Bring

• 4–6 years of relevant Accident & Health claims experience.

• Strong expertise in Employer Stop Loss, HMO/Managed Care, Medical Excess, and Provider Excess products.

• Experience overseeing TPAs, MGUs, delegated claims operations, and claims audits.

• Knowledge of medical claims, provider reimbursement, cost containment, exposure evaluation, and reserving.

• Knowledge of ERISA and applicable state claims handling requirements.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and relationship-management skills.

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent industry experience; insurance designation preferred.

The ideal candidate will possess deep expertise in Employer Stop Loss, HMO/Managed Care, Medical Excess, and Provider Excess products, along with working knowledge of Specialty Accident & Health lines, including Leisure Travel, Excess Accident, Pet, Firefighter Line of Duty, Limited Medical Benefits, and Voluntary Benefits.

Work Environment • Hybrid schedule with an expectation of three days per week in the office. • Periodic travel within the U.S. and Canada to support audits and business initiatives.

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range is $95,000–$130,000, based on experience and location. AXIS also offers incentive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage; health and wellness programs; retirement plans; tuition reimbursement; and paid time off. Accident & Health Senior Claims Specialist

Why AXIS?

Join a growing Accident & Health organization where you can influence claims quality, strengthen delegated partner oversight, and contribute across a broad portfolio of products. This role offers meaningful collaboration with experienced business partners and the opportunity to help shape claims practices and operational improvements.

Job Description: Strategic Sourcing Operations Lead

About the Team
 

The Strategic Sourcing & Procurement team helps AXIS make informed supplier, sourcing, contracting, and purchasing decisions. The team partners with business stakeholders to manage supplier value, improve procurement discipline, support contract governance, and identify opportunities to reduce cost, risk, and complexity across the organization.


How does this role contribute to our collective success?
 

The Strategic Sourcing Operations Lead supports effective procurement decision-making by providing analysis, sourcing coordination, supplier research, contract administration, and stakeholder support across assigned spend categories. The role helps AXIS improve savings visibility, contract discipline, supplier performance, and procurement governance while building future capability within the Strategic Sourcing & Procurement function.
 

What will you do in this role?

  • Supporting Category Managers with category plans, sourcing pipelines, savings trackers, supplier documentation, and leadership-ready updates.

  • Coordinating sourcing activities by managing documentation, supplier communications, timelines, bid analysis, stakeholder meetings, and recommendation materials.

  • Analyzing spend, supplier, contract, and pricing information to identify savings, consolidation, risk reduction, and process improvement opportunities.

  • Managing contract administration activities by tracking renewals, expiration dates, notice periods, pricing obligations, service commitments, and key contractual requirements.

  • Preparing contract summaries, renewal options, supplier comparison materials, total cost summaries, dashboards, reports, and other decision-support materials.

  • Conducting supplier research and market scans to identify potential vendors, alternative supply options, emerging providers, market trends, and supplier risks.

  • Supporting supplier onboarding, due diligence, performance tracking, issue follow-up, supplier business reviews, and compliance documentation.

  • Serving as a day-to-day procurement operations contact for assigned internal stakeholders and helping them navigate sourcing, contracting, onboarding, and procurement processes.

  • Maintaining accurate procurement records, templates, process documentation, trackers, systems data, and audit-ready supporting materials.

  • Escalating complex commercial, contractual, supplier performance, governance, or risk-related matters to Category Managers or senior procurement professionals when appropriate.

  • You may also be asked to perform other reasonable duties, as required, to support the needs of the business.


About You
 

What we’re looking for:
 

  • Possess a bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Finance, Economics, Data Analytics, Operations, or a related field, or demonstrate equivalent relevant experience.

  • Demonstrate experience supporting procurement, sourcing, supplier management, contract administration, finance, consulting, operations, data analytics, or a related business support function.

  • Able to analyze data, prepare reports, identify trends, and translate findings into practical business insights and recommendations.

  • Able to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, records, and stakeholder requests with accuracy and consistent follow-through.

  • Demonstrate experience working with contracts, suppliers, purchasing processes, business stakeholders, or highly transactional operational work.

  • Able to communicate clearly with internal stakeholders and suppliers, including summarizing information, documenting requirements, and preparing concise materials for review.

  • Able to work independently on routine and lower-risk matters while recognizing when to escalate complex commercial, contractual, supplier, or risk-related issues.

  • Demonstrate a service-oriented, collaborative, curious, and proactive approach to supporting stakeholders and building procurement capability.

  • Possess working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, including the ability to organize, compare, and analyze data; experience with pivot tables, lookup formulas, or dashboards is preferred.

  • Experience with procurement, sourcing, contract lifecycle, spend analytics, reporting, or supplier management platforms is preferred.

Role Factors
 

  • This is a hybrid role with onsite office attendance required at least 3 days a week minimum.

  • This role may require participation in supplier or stakeholder meetings across different time zones, depending on business needs.

  • Travel is not expected to be a regular requirement, but occasional travel may be required for business meetings or supplier-related activity.

What we offer
 

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary of $76k to $95k in Alpharetta, Georgia. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location.
 

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate performance and your individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.
 

Where this role is based in the United States of America, the FLSA exemption status should be reviewed and confirmed by HR before posting.

How does this role contribute to our collective success?
AI solutions are becoming increasingly important to AXIS' ability to drive efficiency, improve decision making, and enhance customer and employee experiences. As AI capabilities mature and move into production, maintaining their effectiveness, reliability, fairness, and business value becomes critical.

The AI Solutions Support Lead is responsible for the ongoing support, maintenance, monitoring, and enhancement of AI solutions that have been deployed into production. Once an AI solution has been delivered and transitioned from the Data Science & AI Delivery team, ownership of day-to-day operational support and continuous improvement will transfer to this role.

Leading a team of AI engineers provided through our strategic delivery partners, the AI Solutions Support Lead will ensure production AI solutions remain stable, performant, compliant, and aligned to evolving business needs. This role acts as the central coordination point between AI engineering, Data Science & AI Delivery, Data Engineering, BTS, business stakeholders, and governance teams to ensure AI solutions continue to deliver measurable value throughout their lifecycle.

The role combines technical leadership, operational excellence, stakeholder management, and people leadership, requiring an individual who is equally comfortable discussing model performance, coordinating incident response activities, managing enhancement roadmaps, and engaging senior business stakeholders.


What will you do in this role?

Own Production AI Solutions

  • Assume operational ownership of AI solutions following successful deployment and handover from delivery teams.

  • Establish and maintain support processes, documentation, runbooks, monitoring dashboards, escalation paths, defect management and operational procedures. once a solution has met agreed production acceptance criteria, including runbooks(those will need to be created and handed over to support team), monitoring dashboards, support ownership, escalation paths, defect management, and release evidence

  • Ensure clear ownership, accountability, and service management practices are in place for all production AI solutions.

  • Maintain an accurate inventory of supported solutions, dependencies, business owners, and support requirements.


Lead AI Support & Incident Management

  • Coordinate investigation and resolution of production issues affecting AI solutions.

  • Manage defect remediation activities and oversee the delivery of code fixes through internal and partner engineering teams.

  • Act as the primary point of coordination during major incidents impacting AI services.

  • Ensure issues are identified, triaged, prioritised, communicated, and resolved effectively.

  • Support post-incident reviews and implementation of preventative actions.


Monitor Solution Performance & Effectiveness

  • Own monitoring frameworks to assess solution performance, reliability, usage, accuracy, cost, and value realization.

  • Monitor AI outputs for signs of performance degradation, model drift, bias, fairness concerns, or changing business effectiveness.

  • Ensure solutions continue to meet business objectives, operational requirements, and governance standards.

  • Identify optimisation opportunities and drive continuous improvement activities.


Drive Continuous Improvement & Enhancements

  • Own and manage enhancement backlogs for production AI solutions.

  • Coordinate development and deployment of approved enhancements.

  • Ensure solutions evolve in line with changing business processes, regulatory expectations, and technology capabilities.

  • Support release planning and production deployments.


Collaborate Across Technology & Data Teams

  • Work closely with the broader Data Science & AI Delivery team to ensure effective transition of solutions into support.

  • Partner with Data Engineering teams to maintain data pipelines, integrations, and platform dependencies.

  • Collaborate with BTS teams to align with enterprise support processes, infrastructure standards, change management, and operational controls.

  • Coordinate activities across internal and external delivery teams to ensure service excellence.


Governance, Risk & Compliance

  • Ensure AI solutions operate in accordance with AXIS AI governance policies and standards.

  • Support periodic reviews of AI solutions to confirm continued appropriateness, effectiveness, transparency, and risk management.

  • Maintain appropriate operational documentation, support evidence, and audit artefacts.

  • Contribute to governance forums, operational reviews, and risk assessments where required.


What success looks like

  • Success in this role will be measured through:

  • High availability and reliability of production AI solutions.

  • Timely resolution of incidents and defects.

  • Strong stakeholder satisfaction with AI services and support.

  • Evidence that AI solutions continue to deliver expected business outcomes.

  • Effective monitoring and management of performance, fairness, bias, drift, and operational risk.

  • Delivery of enhancements and continuous improvements aligned to business priorities.

  • Smooth transition of solutions from delivery into operational support.

  • Well-managed support teams and partner resources.



About You
You are an organised, technically strong leader who enjoys operating at the intersection of technology, operations, and business value. You have experience supporting complex production systems and can confidently coordinate multidisciplinary teams to resolve issues and drive continuous improvement.

You combine strong technical understanding with excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, enabling you to translate business priorities into practical operational outcomes.

Skills & Experience

Essential

  • Significant experience supporting, operating, or maintaining production AI, machine learning, analytics, or data-driven solutions.

  • Strong understanding of AI solution lifecycles, including deployment, monitoring, maintenance, and enhancement.

  • Experience leading technical teams and coordinating third-party delivery partners.

  • Strong incident management and problem-solving capabilities.

  • Experience managing application support, service management, or operational delivery functions.

  • Strong understanding of data platforms, APIs, cloud environments, and software delivery practices.

  • Experience working with Agile delivery methodologies and DevOps practices.

  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.

  • Ability to prioritise effectively and manage multiple initiatives simultaneously.

  • Strong organisational and leadership capabilities.


Desirable

  • Experience supporting Generative AI, machine learning, large language model (LLM), or agentic AI solutions.

  • Experience with Azure AI, Databricks, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure OpenAI, Foundry, or similar AI technologies.

  • Understanding of Responsible AI principles, model monitoring, bias management, and AI governance requirements.

  • Experience within insurance, financial services, or other highly regulated industries.

  • Familiarity with ITIL, Service Management, or Site Reliability Engineering practices.



Working Arrangements

This role forms part of the operational backbone of AXIS' AI capability.

Given the critical nature of production support responsibilities, occasional out-of-hours work, including evenings and weekends, may be required to support incident resolution, production deployments, testing activities, or other business-critical operational events.

Role Factors:
In this role, you will typically be required to:

Attend your local office at least three (3) days per week to meet and build relationships with colleagues and the wider business.

Engage in company activities to grow your network and build a strong team culture.

What we offer:

Job Description: Ceded Finance Analyst - Reporting

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

AXIS is a global insurer and reinsurer focused on specialty lines and treaty reinsurance.  AXIS is headquartered in Bermuda and operates in North America, EMEA, Asia, and Global Markets (including Lloyd’s). 

The Ceded Reinsurance Finance and Operations function is responsible for delivering a strategic and forward-looking organization that will:

  • Advance the Company’s growth and profitability goals through the enablement of the Ceded Reinsurance Strategy;

  • Provide clear accountability for outward reinsurance contract administration, outwards reinsurance controls and outward reinsurance reporting; and

  • Drive process excellence and better data and analytics through technological enablement and our partnership with Genpact.

The Ceded Finance Analyst – Reporting (CRM) will report to the Ceded Re Lead who reports to the Global Head of Ceded Re Finance and Operations.  The CRM will lead the global ceded reinsurance reporting and collateral function and ensure timely and accurate reporting per regulatory and corporate requirements.

Role Summary
The Reinsurance Technical Accountant will be responsible for supporting assumed reinsurance technical accounting activities across global portfolios, based on business need. This role requires strong technical accounting knowledge, attention to detail, analytical judgment, and the ability to work across multiple regions, systems, and stakeholders to ensure timely and accurate processing, reporting, and resolution of reinsurance accounting activity.

The role will support close and reporting deliverables, review and process reinsurance statements of account, analyze premiums, losses, commissions, and related balances, and help ensure accounting activity is recorded accurately in accordance with contract terms and internal procedures. The position will also support issue resolution, aged balance review, account analysis, and coordination with internal stakeholders including Underwriting, Claims, Finance, Cash Accounting, offshore processing teams, and Reporting.

This role is critical to maintaining continuity, control integrity, and service quality across the global assumed reinsurance portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform assumed reinsurance technical accounting activities across global portfolios, regions, and business needs.
  • Review, analyze, and process reinsurance statements of account, ensuring activity is complete, accurate, and aligned with contract terms and internal procedures.
  • Analyze and record reinsurance activity, including premiums, losses, commissions, fees, adjustments, and other contract-related balances.
  • Support monthly and quarterly close processes, ensuring assigned deliverables are completed timely and accurately.
  • Monitor, research, and resolve open items, exceptions, and aged balances related to assigned accounts and portfolios.
  • Work closely with Cash Accounting to support timely clearing of aged balances, investigate receipt or payment-related questions, and resolve cash application or statement of account processing inquiries.
  • Partner with offshore processing teams to provide guidance, answer questions, review outputs, and support quality and consistency of processing.
  • Coordinate with Underwriting, Claims, Finance, Reporting, Cash Accounting, and other internal stakeholders to resolve account questions and ensure accurate financial reporting.
  • Support account reconciliations, variance analysis, and investigation of unusual or unexpected movements.
  • Identify and escalate complex issues, control concerns, processing delays, or aged balance risks in a timely manner.
  • Maintain clear documentation of accounting conclusions, open items, follow-ups, and resolution steps.
  • Support audit, internal control, and compliance-related requests, including preparation of supporting documentation and explanations.
  • Contribute to process improvements, reporting enhancements, automation readiness, and opportunities to improve efficiency, visibility, and control across the Technical Accounting function.
  • Assist with training, knowledge transfer, and documentation of account-specific or region-specific procedures as needed.
  • Provide flexible support across regions, portfolios, and deliverables as priorities shift within the global Technical Accounting function.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience in reinsurance accounting, insurance accounting, technical accounting, finance, or a related field.
  • Strong understanding of assumed reinsurance concepts, including premiums, losses, commissions, statements of account, treaty activity, and related accounting flows.
  • Ability to interpret reinsurance activity, identify exceptions, and apply judgment when reviewing account activity.
  • Strong analytical, reconciliation, and problem-solving skills.
  • High attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple deliverables, stakeholders, and deadlines.
  • Strong communication skills and ability to work effectively with onshore, offshore, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Ability to escalate issues appropriately and support timely resolution of complex accounting matters.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and ability to work with accounting systems, reporting tools, and large data sets.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience with assumed reinsurance technical accounting.
  • Experience supporting global, multi-region, or complex reinsurance portfolios.
  • Familiarity with reinsurance administration systems and reporting platforms.
  • Experience working with offshore processing teams or shared service models.
  • Experience supporting month-end or quarter-end close, audit requests, and control documentation.
  • Experience with aged balance analysis, account reconciliations, and statement of account review.


Key Skills and Competencies

  • Technical accounting knowledge
  • Assumed reinsurance accounting
  • Statement of account processing
  • Analytical judgment
  • Account reconciliation
  • Aged balance review and resolution
  • Issue identification and escalation
  • Stakeholder management
  • Control awareness
  • Documentation and follow-through
  • Cross-functional collaboration
  • Ability to work in a complex, deadline-driven, global environment

How This Role Contributes to Our Collective Success?

This is an opportunity to use data and analytics to make a meaningful difference to one of the most important decision-making areas at AXIS: Reserving. In this role, you will help the Reserving team turn complex data into clear, trusted insight so they can better understand trends, explain movements, and make confident decisions.

In this role, you will help us:

  • Make reserving decisions easier to understand by improving access to consistent, timely, and well-defined data.

  • Bring important trends to the surface, helping the team understand what is changing, why it matters, and where more analysis may be needed.

  • Reduce manual effort and improve the way reserving analysis is produced, shared, and used across the business.


You will help shape how reserving analytics evolves at AXIS, building practical insight capabilities that make it easier to understand portfolio movements, compare views across business areas, monitor key indicators, and support high-quality discussions with senior stakeholders.
 

You will work closely with colleagues across Reserving, Finance, Actuarial, Claims, Underwriting, and Data & Analytics to understand what the Reserving team needs and turn those needs into useful dashboards, datasets, self-service tools, and repeatable insight products. You will also partner with technical teams to make sure reserving data is trusted, accessible, clearly defined, and fit for decision-making.

Key Responsibilities
 

Be a Trusted Partner to the Reserving Team

  • Build strong relationships with the Reserving team and the wider teams that use reserving information, taking time to understand their processes, challenges, priorities, and decision-making needs.

  • Help define the reserving analytics roadmap, making sure the work we prioritise delivers clear value for the Reserving team and the business.


Create Better Data Products and Insight Tools

  • Design and deliver dashboards, datasets, and self-service tools that give the Reserving team clearer views of loss development, claims experience, exposure changes, prior-year development, and other important indicators.

  • Replace static, manual reporting with more interactive insight solutions that help users explore trends, compare results, test assumptions, and identify areas for deeper review.

  • Help identify, explain and monitor reserve signals, including AvE, PYD, claims emergence, large loss activity, exposure/mix changes and reserve diagnostics.


Explore Modern Analytics and AI

  • Work with actuarial, data science, and AI colleagues to explore where modern analytics can support reserving analysis, scenario exploration, anomaly detection, and clearer explanation of key drivers.

  • Promote practical and responsible use of AI and analytics, with a focus on improving speed, transparency, and confidence while maintaining strong governance and actuarial judgement.


Inspire Through Insight

  • Create clear, intuitive visualizations that help colleagues understand reserving movements, emerging trends, portfolio changes, and areas of uncertainty.

  • Help improve how reserving insights are communicated so they are concise, consistent, and useful for actuarial, finance, management, and business discussions.


Set Standards for Excellence

  • Help define clear standards for reserving metrics, data definitions, reporting, reconciliation, and interpretation of key indicators.

  • Support high-quality, governed outputs that align with enterprise data standards, actuarial controls, and financial reporting needs.


Collaborate Across D&A

  • Collaborate with architecture, engineering, governance, finance, actuarial, claims, and underwriting colleagues so reserving needs are considered from the data foundation through to the final insight experience.

  • Look for opportunities to simplify processes, reduce manual data wrangling, and build reusable insight capabilities that teams can rely on over time.

You may also be asked to take on additional responsibilities aligned with the nature and scope of this role.


About You
 

Required Experience & Skills

  • Experience in data, analytics, actuarial, finance, or a related insurance or reinsurance role.

  • Experience helping to design, improve, or deliver data and analytics solutions for business users.

  • A deep understanding of insurance or reinsurance data, including how claims, policy, exposure, premium, underwriting, finance, and actuarial information can be used to support analysis.

  • The ability to lead through influence, work with technical teams, and bring people together around a shared outcome.

  • Strong communication skills, including the ability to make complex data and analysis clear, practical, and actionable.

  • Experience creating dashboards, datasets, visualizations, or self-service tools that help business users understand performance, trends, and drivers.

  • Curiosity about AI and emerging technologies, and an interest in applying them to real business problems in a practical and responsible way.

  • Familiarity with data visualization tools such as Power BI, or similar platforms.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working with reserving, actuarial, finance, claims, underwriting, or performance reporting teams.

  • Some knowledge of reserving processes, actuarial triangles, loss development, claims trends, or financial close reporting.

  • Hands-on experience with Power BI and other visualization platforms.


What Really Sets You Apart

  • You enjoy turning complex data into insight that people can trust, understand, and use.

  • You are naturally curious and like asking how analysis could be faster, clearer, more consistent, and more useful.

  • You are excited by the chance to help modernize reserving analytics at AXIS and build tools that improve confidence, transparency, and business understanding.
