Job.JobTitle: Senior Actuarial Analyst, Standard Lines Pricing
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Pricing Actuary, Actuary / Modeling, Actuarial Analyst
Job.JobDescription:
Job Summary

The Senior Actuarial Analyst in Standard Lines Pricing, working with limited supervision, conducts complex analyses, provides recommendations, and leads special actuarial projects. The role applies highly technical actuarial acumen and skill set in completing assignments and works to improve processes in the actuarial department. The role researches and develops best practices pricing techniques to be implemented across the business, serves as a mentor to less experienced professionals, provides general expertise on market trends and product performance and adheres to internal and external compliance requirements/standards.

Job Responsibilities

  • Directs actuarial projects while applying actuarial skills and knowledge of the Company's insurance products and operations.
  • Completes research, ensures accuracy of calculations and analyses, and meets project deadlines.
  • Completes all complex actuarial assignments by following standard processes in area of Standard Lines Pricing
  • Provides input on the pricing of new and existing products, collaborates with the Underwriting, IT, and Product teams.
  • Assists in developing management reports that are used to monitor performance, behavior, and results of company goals and objectives.
  • Develops and maintains adequate knowledge and awareness of industry activities through attendance at seminars, reading trade journals and magazines, and through personal contact with other insurance companies, state regulatory bodies, and professional affiliations.
  • Gathers information, prepares reports, and creates datasets following already documented processes in support of the Actuarial Department.
  • Prepares supporting exhibits for defending state filing materials, and partners with the IT team to implement rate and rule changes in rating.
  • Provides ongoing review and improvements of pricing and processes for greater automation, accuracy, and rate adequacy.
  • Supports peers and less experienced professionals, analysts, and associates in their respective activities on pricing.

Job Qualifications

  • 5+ years of insurance and/or business experience.
  • 4+ years of actuarial experience.
  • Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Actuarial Science, Statistics, or a related field and/or commensurate work experience.
  • Credit for completion of the following Casualty Actuarial Society work: passing the "Basic techniques for rate making and estimating claims liability" exam and completion all CAS preliminary requirements (e.g. exams, VEEs, online courses) prior to this exam.

Location 

Hybrid – defined as working three or more days per week in the office if the employee’s residence is within 50 miles of Westfield Center, OH; or Remote – if the employee resides more than 50 miles from Westfield Center, OH.

Behavioral Competencies

  • Collaborates
  • Customer focus
  • Communicates effectively
  • Decision quality
  • Nimble learning

Technical Skills

  • Financial Acumen
  • Knowledge of Programming Languages
  • Statistical Modelling Software
  • Pricing Modeling
  • Statistical Analysis
  • Predictive Analytics
  • Corporate Reserving
  • Data Analysis and Reporting
  • Actuarial Analytics
  • Insurance Industry Knowledge

The Westfield Specialty Intern Program is a paid, ten-week program that offers students the opportunity to obtain firsthand insight into the insurance business.  Every day you'll learn and develop your skills but you'll also have a clear and supportive path ahead of you. You'll gain the confidence to take on real projects, build your network and learn from senior leaders across our business.  The 2027 Summer Intern Program will run from June 7th to August 13th. 

We are seeking Intern candidates to work with our Actuary team in our Chicago, IL office.   

Program Elements Include:

  • Classroom and On The Job Training 
  • Weekly Lunch and Learn Series with Senior Leaders
  • Formal Mentor Program 
  • Presentations from Major Brokerage Partners 
  • Teambuilding and Social Activities; including Community Service Event
  • Industry based Group Project 

Participants in the Westfield Specialty Summer Intern Program are immersed in the day-to-day operations of a fast-moving, growing insurance company. You will gain valuable, hands-on experience and insurance industry knowledge during the 10-week program. As a summer intern you will work side-by-side with industry leaders on dynamic projects that provide ample opportunity for challenges, learning and achievement.  At Westfield Specialty, we are proud to emphasize the education and development for the future leaders of the insurance industry. 

2027 Summer Intern Program Openings:

  • Alpharetta, GA: Underwriting
  • Berkeley Heights, NJ: Claims, IT, Operations 
  • Chicago, IL:, IT, Underwriting, Actuary
  • New York, NY: Actuary, Marketing, Underwriting

For those who excel in the program, we would welcome the opportunity to discuss full-time employment opportunities at Westfield Specialty after graduation as part of our Trainee Program. 

As part of our internship program you will receive: 

  • Targeted business training designed to help you refine your professional skills and acumen critical to the success of Westfield professionals; 
  • Technical training to deepen your skill level within your chosen discipline; and an understanding of the broader insurance industry; 
  • Access to additional training to compliment your professional development. 
  • Opportunity to expand your professional network with talented insurance professionals 

Responsibilities 

An Actuary Intern at Westfield Specialty works on a variety of projects to gain hands-on experience in the insurance industry and develop technical skills.  Including: 

  • Assist with actuarial analyses supporting pricing initiatives.

  • Gather, validate, and analyze large data sets using actuarial and statistical techniques.

  • Support the development and maintenance of actuarial models, reports, and dashboards.

  • Prepare summaries, presentations, and recommendations based on analytical findings.

  • Assist in evaluating trends related to claims, premium, exposure, and profitability.

  • Participate in data quality reviews and process improvement initiatives.

  • Collaborate with underwriting, finance, claims, and other business partners to support strategic decision-making.

  • Conduct research on industry trends, market conditions, and emerging risks.

  • Complete special projects and ad hoc analyses as assigned.

Desired Qualifications 

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Data Analytics, or a related quantitative field.

  • At minimum must be sitting for Actuarial Exam; successful completion of one or more actuarial exams highly preferred 

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel; experience with SQL, R, Python, Power BI, or other analytical tools is a plus.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication abilities.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

  • Demonstrated attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

  • Ability to be onsite in office 4 days a week

This is a paid internship.  Intern will be paid on an hourly basis at the rate of $25/hour.

Participants in the Westfield Specialty Summer Intern Program are immersed in the day-to-day operations of a fast-moving, growing insurance company. You will gain valuable, hands-on experience and insurance industry knowledge during the 10-week program. As a summer intern you will work side-by-side with industry leaders on dynamic projects that provide ample opportunity for challenges, learning and achievement.  At Westfield Specialty, we are proud to emphasize the education and development for the future leaders of the insurance industry. 

2027 Summer Intern Program Openings:

  • Alpharetta, GA: Underwriting
  • Berkeley Heights, NJ: Claims, IT, Operations 
  • Chicago, IL:, IT, Underwriting
  • New York, NY: Actuary, Marketing, Underwriting

For those who excel in the program, we would welcome the opportunity to discuss full-time employment opportunities at Westfield Specialty after graduation as part of our Trainee Program.

  • Targeted business training designed to help you refine your professional skills and acumen critical to the success of Westfield professionals; 
  • Technical training to deepen your skill level within your chosen discipline; and an understanding of the broader insurance industry; 
  • Access to additional training to compliment your professional development. 
  • Opportunity to expand your professional network with talented insurance professionals 

Overview:

Underwriting Interns will support Westfield Specialty’s underwriting teams while gaining hands-on experience in the insurance industry and developing foundational technical and analytical skills. This role provides direct exposure to underwriting operations, products, and decision-making processes through meaningful project work and day-to-day team collaboration. Interns will be embedded within a specific underwriting team to gain a comprehensive understanding of the business and contribute to ongoing departmental initiatives.

Responsibilities include:

  • Supporting underwriting teams with research, data analysis, and risk assessment activities.
  • Assist underwriters in evaluating complex or non-standard insurance applications (e.g., Cyber, D&O, E&O, Property, Casualty, insurance, etc).
  • Research and analyze industry-specific risks, emerging trends, and exposures unique to specialty lines.
  • Help prepare underwriting files, including summaries of risk factors, coverage recommendations, and pricing justifications.
  • Organize supporting documentation such as loss runs, financial statements, and supplemental forms.
  • Conduct competitor analysis and benchmark coverage options or pricing.
  • Compile data to support the development of underwriting strategies and guidelines.
  • Attend underwriting meetings and shadow underwriters on client calls or risk reviews.
  • Participate in training sessions on specialty insurance products, underwriting systems, and risk modeling tools.
  • Stay updated on niche markets, policy forms, and regulatory requirements in specialty insurance.

Desired Qualifications 

  • Currently matriculated students enrolled at a 4 year college or university pursuing either a Bachelors or Masters degree (required)
  • Strong GPA preferred (Minimum GPA of 3.2 required) 
  • Strong oral and written communication skills 
  • Leadership experience through work or involvement in community service, athletics, clubs, or other activities preferred 
  • Technically adept/digitally savvy
  • Ability to be onsite in office 4 days a week

Job Summary

The Actuarial Consultant utilizes advanced actuarial skills, work experience, and insurance products knowledge and serves as a technical expert and thought leader on Loss Reserving, Actuarial Reporting, and Research and Development, with a particular focus on optimizing reserving processes and conducting competitor and industry benchmarking. The role works with internal business partners in Claims, Financial Reporting, Investments, Finance Committee, etc. in support of the Company’s operations, objectives, and goals. The role leads discussion on the pricing of new and existing products, delivers management reporting, collaborates with analysts on complex analytical projects, provides support to Finance Reporting, and partners with the IT team to implement rating rule changes.

Job Responsibilities

  • Leads the preparation and analysis of loss and loss adjustment expense reserves across assigned lines of business, applying actuarial methods (e.g., loss development, Bornhuetter-Ferguson, frequency/severity) to estimate ultimate losses and reserve adequacy.
  • Performs quarterly and annual reserve reviews, documents key assumptions and judgments, and communicates reserve indications and drivers of change to management and Financial Reporting.
  • Identifies opportunities to streamline and automate the reserving process, improving turnaround time, consistency, and data quality across reserving cycles.
  • Develops and maintains reserving tools, models, and templates, partnering with IT and Data teams to enhance efficiency and reduce manual effort in reserve calculations and reporting.
  • Conducts competitor and industry benchmarking studies, comparing the Company’s reserve levels, loss development patterns, and reserving assumptions against peer and industry data to identify emerging trends and potential areas of exposure.
  • Monitors external actuarial research, regulatory developments, and industry reserve adequacy studies, incorporating relevant findings into internal reserving practices.
  • Analyzes emerging loss trends, claim frequency/severity shifts, and portfolio mix changes, assessing their impact on reserve estimates and flagging areas of concern.
  • Provides technical guidance and support to other members, mentors Actuarial Analysts, and less experienced Actuarial Consultants. Empowers team members and project groups to build reserving methodologies, pricing oversight, and related monitoring techniques consistent with best practice standards.
  • May supervise 1-2 employees, support employee selection, performance management, coaching, and development. Manages priorities and workload distribution and removes barriers that impede project progress.

Job Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in Actuarial or a related field.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Actuarial Sciences, Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, Economics or related field and/or commensurate work experience.

Location 

Hybrid – defined as working three or more days per week in the office if the employee’s residence is within 50 miles of Westfield Center, OH; or Remote – if the employee resides more than 50 miles from Westfield Center, OH.

Licenses and Certifications

  • Associate of the Casualty Actuarial Society – ACAS; required
  • Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society – FCAS; preferred
     

Behavioral Competencies

  • Collaborates
  • Communicates Effectively
  • Customer Focus
  • Decision Quality
  • Nimble Learning

Technical Skills

  • Statistical Modeling Software 

  • Data Analysis and Reporting

  • Competitor Benchmarking 

  • Corporate Reserving 
  • Reserving Process Optimization
  • Business Process Improvement
  • Financial Acumen
  • Insurance Industry Knowledge   

This job description describes the general nature and level of work performed in this role. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, skills, responsibilities, knowledge, etc. These may be subject to change and additional functions may be assigned as needed by management.

Job.JobTitle: Middle Market Underwriting and Sales Region Leader
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Commercial Lines Underwriter, Underwriting, Insurance Sales Representative
Job.JobDescription:
Job Summary:
The Middle Market Underwriting and Sales Region Leader is accountable for developing and executing the underwriting and sales strategy for an assigned region to achieve profitable growth and targeted financial results. The role leads regional business development, underwriting execution, and portfolio management while partnering with Distribution, Product Management, Marketing, and Underwriting Operations to achieve territory objectives.

The Region Leader provides leadership and direction to the regional team, using market insight, portfolio analytics, and sound underwriting judgment to identify opportunities, address performance issues, and make effective business decisions. The role builds strong agency and broker relationships, drives consistent sales and underwriting practices, and promotes collaboration across field and virtual teams. The Region Leader is also responsible for coaching and developing team members, strengthening underwriting and business development capabilities, and building a high-performing team positioned for sustained success.
 

Job Responsibilities:
·  Leads the Middle Market underwriting and sales organization for the region, establishing business priorities, monitoring performance, and ensuring execution of regional new business, renewal, pricing, and profitability objectives.

·  Leads underwriting managers and underwriting teams to achieve appropriate productivity, service, and portfolio results while maintaining sound underwriting discipline and effective partnership across Underwriting, Underwriting Practices, and Underwriting Operations.

·  Builds a strong culture of collaboration across field, home office, and virtual teams and models effective teamwork, communication, and shared accountability for results.

·  Ensures adherence to underwriting guidelines, authority, policies, procedures, regulatory requirements, and quality assurance standards, including timely implementation of corrective actions and QA recommendations.

·  Leads and develops other leaders, establishing clear expectations for performance, coaching, and accountability while strengthening the team's underwriting expertise and ability to manage larger and more complex accounts.

·  Uses portfolio analytics, market intelligence, and business judgment to identify trends, prioritize opportunities, address performance gaps, allocate resources, and support effective underwriting and business decisions.

·  Establishes and maintains a disciplined, objective process for granting and managing underwriting authority based on demonstrated technical capability, experience, judgment, and performance.

·  Supports significant new business and renewal opportunities through agency and broker engagement, sales presentations, account strategy, and negotiation of coverage, pricing, financial terms, and service solutions.

·  Monitors performance against regional financial and operating objectives, identifies emerging issues and opportunities, and develops action plans to improve new business production, retention, pricing, profitability, and overall portfolio performance.

·  Owns talent management for the region, including hiring and selection, succession planning, performance and compensation management, employee development, career coaching, workload management, and resolution of employee issues that may affect team effectiveness.

·  Manages regional expenses within established plans, monitors spending throughout the year, and provides forecasts and variance explanations as required.

·  Maintains a strong understanding of commercial insurance market conditions, competitor activity, industry trends, and jurisdictional developments through agency engagement, industry participation, and other sources, and translates those insights into regional underwriting and sales strategies.

Job Summary

The National Partner Manager serves as Westfield's primary relationship leader for our largest and most strategically important national distribution partners, including agency networks, aggregators, financial institutions, and private equity-backed organizations with complex agency structures. This highly visible role is responsible for developing executive-level partnerships, aligning enterprise and partner strategies, and driving profitable growth across Westfield's Standard Lines business segments. 

Working closely with senior leaders across Distribution Management, Underwriting, Product, Operations, and other enabling functions, the National Partner Manager influences strategic direction, identifies emerging market opportunities, and provides leadership across some of Westfield's most significant distribution relationships. The role serves as the strategic owner of the partner lifecycle, providing executive engagement, growth planning, governance oversight, performance stewardship, and issue resolution across corporate, regional, and local stakeholder groups. 

Through business development, market intelligence, and cross-functional leadership, the National Partner Manager helps ensure alignment between Westfield's business strategies and partner objectives while creating long-term value for both organizations. This role plays a critical part in shaping how Westfield competes, grows, and strengthens relationships with some of the most influential organizations in the insurance distribution marketplace.

Job Responsibilities

  • Lead and strengthen executive-level relationships with a portfolio of Westfield's most strategic national distribution partners, including agency networks, aggregators, financial institutions, and private equity-backed organizations.  
  • Develop and execute partner growth strategies that align partner objectives with Westfield's business priorities and profitable growth goals. 
  • Serve as the strategic owner of assigned partnerships, providing leadership across executive engagement, performance stewardship, governance, and relationship lifecycle management. 
  • Identify, influence, and capitalize on opportunities to expand business, increase market presence, and strengthen long-term partner value. 
  • Lead strategic business planning and performance reviews, utilizing data and market insights to drive results across business segments and optimize partner performance. 
  • Collaborate with leaders across Distribution Management, Underwriting, Product, Operations, and other business functions to ensure enterprise alignment and a coordinated partner experience. 
  • Provide market intelligence and strategic insights regarding distribution trends, agency consolidation, private equity activity, and emerging opportunities within the insurance marketplace. 
  • Facilitate governance and accountability processes that support effective partnership management, risk oversight, and compliance with company standards. 
  • Represent Westfield as a trusted advisor, influencing strategic decisions and strengthening relationships with senior leaders across partner organizations. 
  • Manage budgets and partnership investments responsibly while ensuring alignment with business objectives.

Job Responsibilities

  • 10+ years of experience in Sales, Distribution Management, or a related field.
  • Bachelor's degree in business, Sales or a related field and/or commensurate work experience.
  • Valid driver's license and a driving record that conforms to company standards.
  • Preferred experience in retail agency, retail broker or wholesale brokerage.

Location

  • Remote

Travel Requirements

  • Travel up to 50% of working time to support partner engagement, business development activities, and company initiatives. Travel may include overnight stays and occasional short-notice business travel.

We are an equal opportunity employer/minority/female/disability/protected veteran.

Summer Internship Program

At Westfield, our interns are active contributors, not observers. Through meaningful projects, professional development opportunities, and collaboration with experienced professionals, you'll gain hands-on experience while making an impact across the business.

Our Summer Internship Program provides opportunities to explore careers in insurance, technology, analytics, finance, human resources, communications, and other business functions. Throughout the summer, interns build professional skills, grow their networks, and gain valuable insight into how a leading property & casualty insurance company serves its customers, agents, and communities.

What You'll Experience

As a Westfield Intern, you may:

  • Contribute to meaningful projects that support business goals and strategic initiatives.
  • Collaborate with professionals and leaders across the organization.
  • Develop technical, analytical, and professional skills through real-world work experiences.
  • Participate in networking events, learning sessions, and professional development opportunities.
  • Gain exposure to the insurance industry and the many career paths it offers.
  • Present your work and recommendations to business leaders and stakeholders.

Internship Opportunities

Actuarial
Actuarial Interns support key insurance functions including pricing, reserving, predictive modeling, and data analysis. Interns work alongside experienced actuaries to solve business problems, analyze trends, and help drive data-informed decisions that support Westfield's success.

Claims
Claims Interns gain exposure to the claims process and how Westfield delivers exceptional service to customers during important moments. Interns may assist with claim investigations, data analysis, process improvement initiatives, and projects that support operational excellence.

Communications
Communications Interns help tell Westfield's story through internal and external communications, content creation, employee engagement initiatives, and digital communication strategies. Interns gain experience supporting programs that strengthen relationships with employees, customers, agents, and communities.

Data Analytics & Reporting
Data Analytics & Reporting Interns work with data, reporting tools, and business stakeholders to deliver insights that support decision-making. Interns gain experience analyzing information, identifying trends, and helping transform data into meaningful business outcomes.

Data Science
Data Science Interns support the development of analytical and predictive solutions that address real-world business challenges. Interns work with large data sets, explore emerging analytical techniques, and help generate insights that influence strategic decision-making.

Finance & Accounting
Finance & Accounting Interns gain experience supporting financial operations, reporting, analysis, budgeting, and business planning activities. Interns develop a deeper understanding of how financial information supports organizational performance and strategic decision-making.

Government Relations
Government Relations Interns gain exposure to legislative, regulatory, and public policy issues impacting the insurance industry. Interns may research emerging topics, monitor industry developments, and support initiatives that help advance Westfield's business objectives.

Human Resources
Human Resources Interns support initiatives related to talent acquisition, employee experience, learning and development, compensation, benefits, and organizational effectiveness. Interns gain hands-on experience helping create a positive and engaging workplace culture.

Information Security
Information Security Interns assist with efforts to protect Westfield's systems, data, and digital assets. Interns gain exposure to cybersecurity practices, risk management, threat monitoring, and initiatives designed to strengthen the organization's security posture.

Information Technology
Information Technology Interns work with technology professionals to support systems, applications, infrastructure, and digital solutions that enable business success. Interns gain practical experience applying technology to solve business challenges and improve user experiences.

Internal Audit
Internal Audit Interns help evaluate business processes, internal controls, and risk management practices across the organization. Interns learn how organizations identify opportunities for improvement, strengthen controls, and support effective governance.

Risk Control
Risk Control Interns partner with professionals who help organizations identify, assess, and mitigate risk. Interns gain exposure to risk management strategies, safety practices, loss prevention activities, and customer-focused consulting services.

Customer Care Center 

Customer Care Center Interns will utilize strong analytical skills to assist the Leadership Team with consolidating and analyzing data across the contact center, billing,  and claims teams.  Interns will analyze trends, identify drivers of performance, and create reports for leaders leveraging tools such as Excel, PowerPoint, and contact center management software.

 Hospitality

Our hospitality internship program offers students the opportunity to gain hands-on, real-world experience in a premier golf and conference center environment. Interns can explore a variety of career paths, including golf course turfgrass management, event operations, guest services, and other hospitality operations. From preparing championship-quality playing surfaces to helping execute weddings, corporate events, tournaments, and special occasions, every day brings a new experience. Our interns work alongside experienced professionals and are trusted with meaningful responsibilities that build valuable skills and confidence. The program provides an inside look at the many career opportunities available within the golf, hospitality, events, and club management industries. Interns will develop professional relationships, expand their resumes, and gain practical experience that translates directly to future careers. Whether you are passionate about golf, events, hospitality, or operations, our program provides an opportunity to learn, contribute, and grow. Join our team and experience what it takes to create exceptional experiences for our guests and members.

Personal Lines

Personal Lines Internship provides the opportunity to join a team for a hands-on internship experience that provides exposure to both Underwriting and Product Management operations. You'll contribute to meaningful projects, support daily business activities, and gain valuable insight into how insurance products are developed, managed, and underwritten. This internship offers the opportunity to build industry knowledge, develop professional skills, and work alongside experienced professionals focused on protecting customers and driving profitable growth.  

What We're Looking For

  • Currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree from an accredited college or university.
  • Strong academic performance and a desire to learn.
  • Effective communication and collaboration skills.
  • Ability to think critically, solve problems, and take initiative.
  • Interest in gaining real-world business experience through a challenging and rewarding internship.
  • Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without employer sponsorship.

Why Westfield

At Westfield, you'll do meaningful work, build valuable professional relationships, and gain experience that helps prepare you for future career opportunities. We're committed to creating a supportive environment where interns can learn, contribute, and grow.

Behavioral Competencies:

  • Collaborates
  • Communicates Effectively
  • Customer Focus
  • Decision Quality
  • Nimble Learning

Job Summary

The Senior Underwriter, Reinsurance, will be part of the Westfield A&H Underwriting team. You will be responsible for underwriting Stop-Loss, Excess Reinsurance and other specialty products.

  • Reporting to the Chief Underwriting Officer A&H, you will be a key contributor to the overall analysis and management of our new and renewal business.

  • You will work directly with brokers to successfully price and design quotes to acquire individual accounts and business produced through MGA/MGU’s.

  • You will manage the relationship and profitability of program business written through assigned Managing General Underwriters.

  • The senior underwriter will propose effective underwriting strategies across various product lines.

  • You will be part of and present new and renewal opportunities to our Peer Review team (UW, Actuarial, Claims).

  • Contribute to the development and execution of our underwriting strategies.

  • Developing strong relationships with our business partners is a key goal for the department (Brokers, TPAs, vendors, etc.) You will manage specific assigned relationships.

  • Engage with brokers and customers in-person when needed

  •       Participate in new product development as part of the A&H team.

The salary range for this position is $100,000.00 to $170,000.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree, plus 8-10 years of professional experience in the A&H business with demonstrated knowledge of Stop Loss and Excess Reinsurance
  • Strong current technical knowledge of Employer Stop Loss 
  • Established broker relationships 
  • Program management experience

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Assist in the oversight of financial lines claims, including Private D&O, EPL, handled by a Managing General Underwriter (MGU).

  • Manage and oversee Plastic Card Fraud and Theft claims.

  • Monitor claim activity to ensure timely handling, appropriate investigation, reserving, and resolution consistent with company guidelines and delegated authority requirements.

  • Review claim bordereaux to understand claim developments, coverage considerations, exposure evaluations, and resolution strategies.

  • Escalate significant claim developments, coverage concerns, and high-exposure matters to management as appropriate.

  • Communicate regularly with MGU claim handlers regarding claim status, significant developments, reserve changes, and settlement activity.

  • Maintain accurate claim documentation and prepare written summaries, reports, and updates for management and business partners as needed.

  • Provide responsive and professional service to internal and external customers, business partners, brokers, and insureds.

  • Monitor compliance with applicable statutes, regulations, company guidelines, and delegated authority requirements.

  • Support mediations, settlement discussions, and claim resolution efforts by coordinating information and facilitating communication among stakeholders.

  • Participate in meetings with underwriting, brokers, insureds, and MGU partners as needed to support business relationships and claim-related discussions.

  • Assist in the coordination and management of outside vendors, including payment of defense counsel and other service providers, to support effective claim resolution.

Qualifications:

  • Minimum of 1 to 3 years of experience at either an insurance carrier and/or law firm.

  • Bachelor’s degree required.

  • Candidates will be required to obtain and maintain insurance adjuster licenses. 

  • Excellent written communication skills.

  • Excellent verbal and interpersonal communication skills, resulting in the ability to interact with all levels of management and employee population.

  • Strong analytic, investigative, listening and negotiation skills. 

  • Experience multi-tasking, prioritizing work and working effectively in a team environment, while maintaining attention to detail.

  • Experience working in a fast-paced environment, completing work with limited supervision.

  • Experience with Microsoft Windows, Outlook, and Excel or transferable software packages.

  • Ability and willingness to travel as needed.

The salary range for this position is $125,000.00 to $170,000.00.

Job.JobDescription:
Underwriters are responsible for underwriting a complex book of business, employing the methods necessary to meet projected profitability, gross written premium, and expense goals, management and growth of the overall portfolio of business, implementing proper underwriting discipline/guidelines, marketing and servicing of existing and potential clients.  This position is located in Chicago, IL and will report directly into VP, Cyber Liability Midwest Regional Leader.    

 RESPONSIBILITIES 

  • Develop, grow, and manage a profitable portfolio of Cyber Liability, Technology Errors & Omissions, and Miscellaneous Professional Liability business, with a strong focus on new business production and retention of key accounts.

  • Drive underwriting profitability through disciplined risk selection, pricing, coverage analysis, and portfolio management strategies.

  • Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with retail brokers to generate new business opportunities and increase market presence within the assigned territory.

  • Actively market products through broker meetings, industry events, presentations, conferences, lunches, dinners, and other networking activities to expand distribution channels and strengthen strategic partnerships.

  • Independently evaluate and underwrite complex risks by reviewing submissions, analyzing exposures, assessing financial and operational information, and determining appropriate pricing, terms, conditions, and coverage structures. 

  • Ensure compliance with underwriting guidelines, authority levels, systems, and operational procedures. 

  • Collaborate with Actuarial, Claims, Legal, and Product Development teams to support pricing strategies, address emerging cyber trends, and maintain portfolio profitability. 

  • Monitor industry developments, cyber threat trends, claims activity, and marketplace changes to identify opportunities and enhance underwriting strategies. 

  • Provide underwriting analysis, production updates, pipeline reporting, and portfolio performance metrics to senior management.

 

CANDIDATE SKILLS, EXPERIENCE 

  • Bachelor's degree required.

  • Minimum 3+ years of Cyber Liability and/or Technology E&O underwriting experience, with demonstrated production and broker-facing responsibilities strongly preferred.

  • Proven ability to build and maintain broker relationships and successfully generate new business opportunities.

  • Solid Writing and Communication Skills

  • Excellent organizational skills, and ability to multi-task

  • Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment

  • Willingness to travel

  • Must be able to think originally, be willing to challenge ideas and be receptive to constructive feedback

  • Ability to be onsite in office 4 days week, where applicable

Job Summary

The Legal Operations Analyst, working under general supervision, provides legal and operational support to the General Counsel and the Enterprise Legal team across a broad range of corporate legal matters. The role assists with legal research, corporate governance, matter management, and legal operations while supporting the department's technology and document management systems. The Legal Operations Analyst helps improve the efficiency and effectiveness of Enterprise Legal by preparing legal documents, maintaining corporate records, coordinating legal projects, and ensuring compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and internal processes.

Job Responsibilities

  • Legal Research & Document Preparation: Assists the General Counsel and the Enterprise Legal team by preparing legal documents, performing legal research and compiling data from statutes, regulations, case law, and other legal resources.
  • Corporate Governance Support: Provide support for corporate records, board resolutions, and subsidiary documentation. Assist with entity formation, dissolution, and compliance filings.
  • Cross-Functional Support: Assist with legal projects involving compliance, governance, licensing, litigation, and contracts. Coordinate with internal departments and external stakeholders as needed.
  • Legal Intake & Matter Management: Support the legal intake process for new matters, ensuring accurate setup in the legal matter management system. Assign appropriate naming conventions, categorize matters, and ensure proper routing to attorneys.
  • Legal Operations & Technology: Support and maintain the technology associated with the Enterprise Legal’s support tools including the creation of tools and techniques to automate the support process.
  • Document & Records Management: Utilize document and data management systems to prepare, monitor, and record all aspects of casework.
  • Data Analysis & Reporting: Compile and summarize large quantities of data for clients, managers, and reporting needs and gather and maintain confidential information.
  • Collaboration & Stakeholder Management: Coordinates with internal team members and partners, employees at all levels within the company as well as externally with outside counsel and vendors.

Job Qualifications

  • 2-5 years of experience in working as a Corporate Paralegal and administering Corporate Insurance Program, or a related field.

Role Description

We are seeking a detail-oriented and analytical individual to join our team as a Specialty Claims Quality Assurance and Compliance Senior Specialist. This role will report to the VP, Specialty Claims Compliance and will be responsible for supporting Specialty Claims through quality assurance, compliance oversight, claims governance, and operational reporting activities. You will help ensure claims are handled in accordance with regulatory requirements, internal quality standards, and industry best practices while coordinating key governance processes, including reinsurance reporting, large loss reporting, licensing compliance, and other critical reporting obligations.

The ideal candidate will possess strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and a comprehensive understanding of Specialty insurance claims best practices, procedures, and compliance regulations.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Provide quality assurance and compliance support to Specialty Claims operations, including one or more of the following:

  • Perform quality reviews and audits across Specialty insurance claims to ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance with internal standards, regulatory requirements, and best practices, with emphasis on higher-risk and more complex claim activity.

  • Evaluate claim handling practices in high-risk and complex claim areas to identify trends, control gaps, and areas of elevated regulatory, litigation, or E&O exposure.

  • Provide focused QA oversight for AI-enabled functionality used in claims, including reviewing outputs, identifying issues, and ensuring appropriate governance and controls are in place.

  • Partner with Claims leadership, Compliance, and Operations to address QA findings, support corrective actions, and improve consistency in claim handling.

  • Develop and deliver targeted training and guidance based on QA findings to reinforce expected claim handling practices and address recurring issues.

  • Prepare clear, actionable QA reports summarizing findings, trends, and recommendations and claims reporting activities for Claims leadership.

  • Monitor regulatory developments, industry trends, and emerging risks impacting Specialty claims and incorporate them into QA focus areas and training.

  • Ensure internal claims staff meet applicable licensing requirements and support related tracking and documentation.

  • Monitor reinsurance and large loss reporting processes to ensure timely and accurate internal/external reporting.

Qualifications:

  • Seven or more years of experience in Specialty insurance claims handling, quality assurance, compliance, or a related role.

  • Strong knowledge of Cyber, Financial Institutions, Management Liability, Professional Lines, and applicable state and federal insurance regulations.

  • Demonstrated experience reviewing complex claims and identifying quality, compliance, or control issues.

  • Ability to analyze claim data and QA results to identify patterns, trends, and areas of risk.

  • Strong attention to detail and sound judgment when evaluating claim handling decisions.

  • Working knowledge of claims systems and tools, including Guidewire ClaimCenter and related

  •  document management platforms.

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to provide constructive feedback and partner effectively with claim professionals and leadership.

  • Professional insurance or compliance designations preferred.

  • Ability and willingness to travel as needed.

Accident & Health Operations Manager

Position Overview

The Accident and Health Operations Manager is responsible for the onboarding, operational integration, and ongoing management of external program managers, administrators, intermediaries and fronting insurance companies (collectively, “MGUs”). This role ensures that MGUs are effectively integrated into company systems, processes, and compliance frameworks to support efficient policy issuance, regulatory adherence, and operational excellence.

In addition to execution, this role owns the MGU onboarding strategy, defining scalable frameworks, standards, and best practices for integrating new partners and programs.

This position serves as the primary day-to-day liaison between the company and its MGU partners, coordinating across underwriting, licensing, compliance, and operational teams. 

The Operations Manager plays a critical role in enabling business growth by ensuring new programs are launched efficiently and existing partnerships operate smoothly.

MGU Onboarding Strategy & Implementation

  • Own and continuously refine the MGU onboarding strategy, including standardized frameworks, operating models, and best practices for partner integration.
  • Design scalable onboarding processes to support growth across multiple MGUs, programs, and distribution channels.
  • Define onboarding timelines, milestones, and success criteria, ensuring consistency across all implementations.
  • Lead end-to-end onboarding of new MGU partners, including operational readiness, system integration, and process alignment.
  • Coordinate onboarding deliverables and dependencies across underwriting, legal, compliance, IT, and finance.
  • Establish workflows for submission intake, policy issuance, reporting, and escalation handling.
  • Ensure MGUs are trained on company processes, systems, and reporting expectations.

Policy Issuance & Operational Execution

  • Oversee and facilitate policy issuance processes for all written business, including non-MGU business, ensuring timeliness, accuracy, and compliance.
  • Coordinate setup and maintenance of products, policies, rating structures, and forms within policy administration systems.
  • Ensure proper handling of endorsements, cancellations, and renewals in alignment with underwriting guidelines.
  • Identify and resolve operational bottlenecks that impact service levels or customer experience.
  • Monitor policy lifecycle metrics and service-level adherence.

Licensing & Regulatory Compliance

  • Coordinate producer and entity licensing requirements, including across MGUs and jurisdictions.
  • Ensure compliance with state Department of Insurance requirements for policy issuance and distribution.
  • Partner with Legal and Compliance teams to support filings, approvals, and regulatory inquiries.
  • Maintain documentation and audit trails supporting MGU authority and operational compliance.
  • Support audits related to delegated authority, licensing, and operational processes.

MGU Relationship Management

  • Serve as the primary operational point of contact for MGUs, managing day-to-day requests and issue resolution.
  • Establish strong working relationships with MGU operational and underwriting teams.
  • Triage and coordinate responses to MGU inquiries across internal departments.
  • Facilitate regular operational reviews with MGUs to address performance, issues, and improvement opportunities.
  • Support escalation management and resolution of complex operational issues.
  • Process Optimization & Controls
  • Identify opportunities to streamline onboarding, policy issuance, and MGU servicing workflows.
  • Develop and implement standardized operating procedures across MGUs.
  • Establish operational controls to ensure adherence to delegated authority agreements.
  • Drive automation and system enhancements to improve efficiency and accuracy.
  • Monitor operational KPIs and recommend improvements based on performance trends.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner with Underwriting, Actuarial, Finance, Compliance, and IT teams to ensure cohesive program execution.
  • Support implementation of new products and program changes across MGUs.
  • Coordinate with Finance on premium flow, reporting, and reconciliation dependencies.
  • Collaborate with technology teams on system integrations, data flows, and platform enhancements.
  • Provide operational insights to leadership to support strategic decision-making.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Insurance, Operations, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in insurance operations, preferably within Accident & Health or specialty lines.
  • Experience working with MGUs, delegated authority models, or third-party administrators.
  • Strong knowledge of policy administration, policy lifecycle processes, and insurance operations.
  • Familiarity with licensing requirements and multi-state regulatory environments.
  • Excellent organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience designing or leading onboarding frameworks for MGUs or program business.
  • Knowledge of accident & health insurance products and regulatory frameworks.
  • Familiarity with policy administration systems and workflow tools.
  • Experience with operational KPIs and service-level management.
  • Strong project management and process improvement capabilities.

Success Indicators

  • Scalable, standardized onboarding framework adopted across MGU partnerships.
  • Timely and efficient onboarding of MGUs and new programs.
  • Accurate and compliant policy issuance across all MGU partners.
  • Strong, responsive relationships with MGUs and internal stakeholders.
  • Reduction in operational friction and processing delays.
  • Improved standardization, automation, and scalability of operational processes.

Accident & Health – Senior Financial Analyst

The Accident and Health Senior Financial Analyst implements financial processes supporting the core operations of the Accident and Health business unit, including premium billing and collection, commission payments, financial reporting, and internal controls.

This position engages with external program managers, administrators, intermediaries and fronting insurance companies (collectively, “MGUs”) to ensure processes are in place to receive accurate and timely financial and operational data that supports internal reporting requirements.

The role is responsible for ensuring financial accuracy and implementing effective internal controls. Working closely with Actuarial, Accounting, Claims Operations, and enterprise partners, this manager maintains the integrity of financial information across the organization and ensures compliance with enterprise financial and reporting standards.

Key Responsibilities

Premium, Commissions, and Claims Financial Operations

  • Develop processes for the receipt of premium, commission, and claims data from MGUs, and design controls to ensure reported amounts align with business expectations and regulatory requirements.

  • For business written without MGUs, ensure timely and accurate premium billing, collections, and commission payments.

  • Ensure accurate reporting to accounting and financial systems, including reconciliation between accounting systems and administrative systems and databases.

  • Oversee bordereaux ingestion, validation, and reconciliation processes to ensure data integrity.

  • Facilitate reporting to reinsurance and retrocession partners, including calculation of profit sharing and contingent commission arrangements.

  • Develop and maintain financial reporting for the Accident and Health business.

  • Coordinate reporting of claim activity between claims and actuarial.

  • Partner with Claims and Actuarial teams to identify anomalies, data gaps, and operational risks.

MGU Oversight & Governance

  • Establish financial reporting standards, controls, and service level expectations with MGUs.

  • Evaluate MGU financial reporting for completeness, accuracy, and timeliness.

  • Monitor premium receivables, cash flow timing, and remittance activity from MGUs.

  • Support MGU audits, due diligence, and performance reviews.

  • Assist in the analysis of profitability by MGU, program, and product, including loss ratios and expense performance.

Regulatory Compliance & Reporting

  • Ensure all data reporting complies with enterprise standards and Department of Insurance requirements.

  • Support the preparation of regulatory filings, financial exhibits, and audit requests.

  • Maintain strong internal controls aligned with SOX requirements and audit readiness.

  • Establish and test controls over delegated financial and underwriting authority.

Process Optimization

  • Identify and lead initiatives to streamline financial workflows.

  • Drive automation and efficiency improvements.

  • Establish and enhance standards of practice for billing, commissions, and other non-claim financial processes.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Coordinate closely with Actuarial, Underwriting, and Claims teams to provide financial insights that support reserving and pricing decisions.

  • Partner with enterprise FP&A and Accounting to lead budgeting and forecasting efforts for Accident and Health.

  • Communicate financial insights clearly to stakeholders at all levels.

  • Support onboarding and financial due diligence of new MGU or program relationships.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field (MBA or Master’s preferred).

  • 5+ years of experience in financial operations within health insurance or related insurance fields.

  • Strong understanding of premium billing, commission structures, bordereaux, and insurance financial flows.

  • Experience with regulatory financial reporting preferred.

  • Excellent analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills.

  • Prior leadership experience preferred.

Preferred Skills

  • Familiarity with actuarial concepts (IBNR, trend, MLR).

  • Advanced Excel and data tools (e.g., Power BI).

  • Experience working with insurance systems and data warehouses.

Success Indicators

  • Accurate and efficient processing of exposure, premium, commission, and claims data.

  • Timely and compliant internal and external reporting.

  • Strong partnerships with internal teams and external partners.

  • Improved automation and streamlined workflows.

  • High team engagement and performance.

Job Summary

We are seeking an Actuarial Analyst to provide actuarial pricing support for Westfield’s US Specialty lines of business. In this role, you will experience wide-ranging opportunities to develop your actuarial skillset on complex classes including Excess Casualty, Specialty Property, Financial Lines, and Professional Lines. Alongside a talented group of Pricing Actuaries, you will interact directly with our underwriting leaders to implement market-leading pricing and analytical capabilities which will directly influence strategic business decisions.

We are looking for innately curious, detail-oriented, innovative, and highly motivated individuals to join the Actuarial team in our New York or Chicago office.

Job Responsibilities

  • Assist in conducting profitability and segmentation analyses to identify profitable growth opportunities and areas requiring remediation.
  • Prepare monthly and quarterly reports on pricing and portfolio performance, monitoring key actuarial metrics including risk-adjusted rate change, actual vs. technical          price, and mix of business.
  • Assist in building and analyzing exposure profiles to assess portfolio composition and concentrations of risk.
  • Support regular improvements to technical pricing models including enhancements for unique structures and implementing more comprehensive data capture
  • Collaborate with underwriting teams to perform pricing / profitability evaluations for individual accounts as needed.
  • Partner with other functions to improve data quality and integration into pricing tools and analytical frameworks.
  • Contribute to actuarial studies and research projects aimed at improving pricing sophistication, drawing on predictive modeling techniques.
  • Assist in actuarial due diligence for new product launches and program opportunities, including development of pricing structures and regulatory support.
  • Improve efficiency of data extraction and manipulation processes for routine projects.
  • Communicate analytical insights to underwriting and business partners to inform decision-making and strategy.
     

Job Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree within Actuarial Science, Statistics, or similar technical field
  • At least 2 Exams toward qualification by the Casualty Actuarial Society or equivalent professional body
  • Actuarial or related internship experience at an insurance carrier, broker, or consultancy; understanding of actuarial concepts such as loss development and exposure     rating
  • Advanced skills in Microsoft Excel and familiarity with coding in SQL, VBA, or R/Python
  • Experience with statistical modeling and predictive analytics
  • Ability to work with large datasets and ensure data integrity
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and an ability to explain technical concepts to a wide audience
  • Ability to prioritize competing demands and requests to complete work within required time constraints
  • Self-starter that is energized by independent learning and research

Westfield offers a competitive Actuarial Study Program to support and reward you as you complete the Casualty Actuarial Society Exams.

We are an equal opportunity employer/minority/female/disability/protected veteran.

The Territory Leader (Western Zone) is responsible for driving profitable small business growth across a multi-state territory (AZ,NM,CO,IL,WI,MN), supporting both field and a national virtual sales model. This role provides leadership to sales teams operating within the assigned zone and ensures disciplined execution of Westfield’s Small Business strategy while delivering strong production and profitability results.

The Territory Leader serves as the primary sales leader for the zone, accountable for sales performance, talent development, agency engagement, and cross-functional alignment. This role plays a critical part in executing national and regional growth initiatives while building a high-performing, accountable sales culture.

Key Responsibilities:

Sales & Growth Leadership

People Leadership & Talent Development

Execution & Governance

  • Manage priorities, remove barriers, and ensure focus on the highest-impact activities.

The Senior Commercial Lines Territory Manager serves as a liaison between the company and agents, and acts as a relationship manager for our agents, regional underwriting team and corporate departments.  Incumbent is responsible for all commercial lines agency planning and agency management initiatives for assigned agents, to include providing collaboration and support to Underwriters and RVPs on small business, mid-market renewal decisions, and other branch initiatives. The Senior Commercial Lines Territory Manager is also responsible for the direct underwriting of mid-market new business as well as growth objectives for assigned commercial lines agents. Incumbent evaluates the strengths and weaknesses of assigned agents and facilitates new business action plans that drive profitable commercial lines growth in both premium volume and policy count. To leverage new business, the Incumbent provides necessary training to ensure assigned agents are familiar with Penn National Insurance commercial lines products, policies, procedures, and services. 

The territory for this position is Eastern PA. 

POSITION COMPETENCIES 

  • Business Acumen
  • Negotiation
  • Results Oriented 
  • Time & Priority Management 
  • Decision Making 

 ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Sales/Premium Growth

  • Develop the agency force to pre-qualify, rate, and bind profitable commercial lines business,
  • Utilize authority to assist agency partners in helping them write profitable business.
  • Review new business quote requests to determine acceptability using established underwriting authority and company guidelines.
  • Communicate underwriting decisions, techniques, and interpretation of policy forms and coverages with agents and company personnel regarding risk acceptability, incomplete information, etc.
  • Provide feedback to the Underwriting Manager and RVP on the quality of submissions and interactions with agency personnel.
  • Communicate underwriting and marketing philosophy or practices, to agents and policyholders and assist with education/training issues within agency.
  • Document the underwriting files where required, including the actions taken, reasons for decisions, and any follow-up diary needed.
  • Develop professional working relationships with agents, regional underwriting and claim teams and corporate departments.
  • Conduct thorough evaluation of all prospective agents and submit written recommendation to Regional Vice President.
  • Visits agencies to discuss underwriting matters, assist in the development of new business to strengthen agency relations.
  • Keeps two-way communication between agent and company continuously open and viable.
  • Drives profitable new business growth.
  • Monitors agency results and follows up with agent as to growth and compliance with company’s initiatives, procedures and policies
  • Stays alert for and shares industry information, new ideas, products, or changes in other carrier philosophies that could positively or adversely affect Penn National Insurance with appropriate colleagues.
  • Utilizes authority to make consistent underwriting decisions, adhere to company acceptability and pricing philosophies, and promote ease of doing business initiatives with Penn National Insurance.

Profitability

  • Profiles commercial lines book of business to assist in profitability analysis.
  • Develops and implements effective agency profitability plans when warranted.
  • Monitors agency results and follows up with agent as to profitability and compliance with company’s initiatives, procedures and policies.
  • Facilitate agency reviews with other team members to review agent’s performance as compared to established goals and implement corrective actions as needed.
  • Develop and implement agency action plans to achieve profitability.
  • Establishes appropriate account pricing in accordance with established underwriting authority and company guidelines.
  • Order and/or analyze loss control reports, financial reports, MVR’s, and other underwriting reports.
  • Evaluate the need for and secure appropriate facultative reinsurance in accordance with established company guidelines.
  • Contribute to the development of company underwriting policy, procedures, and guidelines to assure they reflect current market conditions and contribute to the attainment of Division goals.

Agency Management

  • Provide training to agency plant on programs, products, services, and systems.
  • Develop annual agency/company marketing plans.
  • Analyze territory profitability, premium growth, and agency representation, and implement corrective actions where appropriate.

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Applies data to solve common business problems.
  • Compiles, manipulates, and analyses data of varying complexity.
  • Knowledgeable and proficient about what tools are available for data analysis and when they are appropriate to use.
  • Performs other duties as may be assigned by the President-Partners Mutual or Regional Vice President.

 SPECIAL RELATIONSHIPS 

  • Direct contact with all levels of branch underwriting and supporting claims service office personnel
  • Direct contact with all levels of Home Office Underwriting Operations personnel
  • Direct contact with agents and insureds.

 QUALIFICATIONS

Education/Credentials 

  • Four year college degree preferred. 
  • Continuing education in specialized insurance courses such as IIA, AU, CPCU, and CIC, as well as other educational experiences that enhance product knowledge and technical business relations. 
  • Maintenance of an active agent’s P&C license in domiciled state preferred.

Experience 

  • Minimum of five years’ property/casualty commercial lines carrier underwriting and/or marketing experience required.    
  • Agency or broker experience with heavy concentration in underwriting exposure/risk and marketing may be given consideration in lieu of carrier experience.

Technical/Professional Knowledge

  • Must have technical underwriting knowledge of commercial lines of business written by Penn National Insurance
  • Effective oral and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate information of a highly technical nature
  • Proven sales, negotiations, and solution-selling skills
  • Working knowledge and skill in agency and Company automation systems, to include fundamental knowledge on the use of personal computers, with emphasis on Microsoft Office Suite
  • Exceptional customer service skills
  • Good financial analysis skills
  • Excellent time management skills
  • Strong commercial   lines underwriting analysis skills

The Claims Representative II investigates, evaluates and resolves assigned claims in a timely and accurate manner in order to achieve a best practices type settlement within legal statutes, policy provisions and Company standards of performance.

Job.JobDescription:
We are seeking a Personal Lines Underwriter who is responsible for making decisions on the acceptability of insurance risks through the application of various underwriting and risk selection techniques.  This position also assists in the management of assigned agents.

This is a hybrid role reporting to the Harrisburg, PA office. 

POSITION COMPETENCIES

  • Business Acumen
  • Negotiation 
  • Results Oriented 
  • Time & Priority Management
  • Decision Making 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Communicate underwriting decisions, techniques, and interpretation of policy forms and coverages with agents.
  • Document the underwriting file for all referred risks, including the actions taken, reasons for exception made, and any follow-up diary needed.
  • Communicate to the Underwriting Manager and Territory Manager any underwriting quality or integrity concerns with individual agents.
  • Provide input to the Branch Management team about individual agency underwriting performance. (i.e., Agency Review meeting, Quarterly Results Management meeting, etc.).
  • Provides underwriting and marketing philosophy or practices, to agents and assist with training issues within agency, making periodic physical visits.
  • Maintains documentation on risk exceptions and large losses based on certain agency-specific or policy specific information.
  • Identify product risks and recommend solutions to mitigate those risks. Advise Underwriting Manager on recommended risk reduction actions and solutions.
  • Exercise underwriting flexibility within the scope of authority in making appropriate exceptions, as warranted, based on agency relationships, results and Company strategies.
  • Leverage exceptions to achieve additional business opportunities from agencies.
  • Apply underwriting and risk selection techniques to determine the acceptability of new and renewal insurance risk referrals.
  • Conduct re-underwriting programs for selected agencies to improve the profitability of their books of business.
  • Complete Claim referrals.
  • Communicate underwriting and marketing philosophy or practices, to agents and assist with training issues within agency, making periodic physical visits.
  • Conduct special re-underwriting programs in conjunction with Branch and/or Home Office Management team[s] for selected agencies to improve the profitability of their books of business.
  • Provide support for prospective book transfers, including the gathering of policy, product, and underwriting information about a book transfer opportunity.
  • Ensure the proper risk placement and/or classification for referrals, to obtain adequate premium for the exposure.
  • Visits agents as necessary independently or jointly with other PNAT staff members.

 ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Applies data to solve common business problems.
  • Compiles, manipulates and analyses data of varying complexity.
  • Knowledgeable and proficient about what tools are available for data analysis and when they are appropriate to use.
  • Contribute to the training/mentoring of the Underwriter Trainee.
  • Contribute to the development of company underwriting policy, procedures and guidelines to assure they reflect current market conditions and contribute to the attainment of Division goals.
  • Work independently within established standards.
  • Respond to Insurance Department complaints and attend periodic hearings.
  • Performs other duties as may be assigned by the Personal Lines Underwriting Manager.

SPECIAL RELATIONSHIPS

  • Daily contact with agents and periodic physical visits to agency. Develop and maintain ongoing strong positive relationships with agents. 
  • Maintain a strong communication with Territory Manager to keep them abreast of agency interactions. Contributes to the development of unit and agency plans, enforcement of the objectives and monitoring of results to assure they reflect attainment of goals and current market conditions. 
  • Interacts with internal customers, external customers and insurance related entities, ie., Department of Insurance.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education/Credentials 

  • 4 - year degree preferred.
  • Continuing education in specialized insurance courses such as IIA & AU preferred

Experience 

  • Completion of Underwriter Trainee curriculum; or a minimum of 1 year experience in a property/casualty underwriting position such as a Personal Lines Assistant Underwriter.

Technical/Professional Knowledge

  • Good working knowledge of underwriting and pricing risks
  • Good working knowledge of company underwriting standards and philosophy
  • Good working knowledge of all insurance coverages
  • Good math aptitude

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Workers' Compensation Adjuster, Claims, Claims Representative
Job.JobDescription:
These positions investigate, evaluate and dispose of assigned claims in a timely manner in order to achieve best practices type settlements within legal statutes, policy provisions and Company and/or client guidelines. 

Candidates may reside in any of the approved hiring markets, provided they can report to our Harrisburg, PA, Pittsburgh, PA or Waukesha, WI office on a hybrid basis. 

 POSITION COMPETENCIES 

  • Business Acumen
  • Negotiation 
  • Results Oriented
  • Time & Priority Management 
  • Decision Making

 ESSENTIAL DUTIES

  • Independently manage a dedicated caseload of complex, lost-time/indemnity, and litigated Workers' Compensation files.
  • Gather factual and medical evidence, interview stakeholders, evaluate coverage, and determine claim compensability.
  • Establish and adjust accurate financial reserves based on real-time claim developments and exposure analysis within company guidelines.
  • Coordinate with defense counsel, handle hearing/mediation representation, negotiate settlements, and manage Medicare Set-Asides (MSAs) or liens.
  • Identify and refer files for subrogation, fraud investigation (SIU), and structured return-to-work or modified-duty programs.
  • Serve as a primary liaison between injured workers, employers, policyholders, medical providers, and agents.
  • Maintains statutory and regulatory compliance by accurately and timely completing required workers’ compensation forms, EDI transactions, and jurisdictional filings throughout the life of the claim.
  • Initiates self-development and training, in order to improve upon, maintain or acquire skills prescribed as promoting professional and personal growth in claims handling 
  • Develops claims files from initial assignment to disposition.
  • Prepares claim file documentation accurately and completely in order to justify all actions taken and to provide an effective audit trail. 
  • Achieves a best practices type settlement in the disposition of claims.
  • Completes actions on a timely basis, such as verifying coverages, setting or adjusting reserves, making appropriate contacts.
  • Collaborates with Team Leader, Manager and Home Office as necessary to develop case strategy, moving the investigation along and disposing of the claim, in order to keep management, claimants, insureds and other interested parties satisfied that effective efforts are being made toward claim settlement.
  • Performs other duties as may be assigned by the Reporting managers listed above.

SPECIAL RELATIONSHIPS

  • In Penn National Insurance, these positions report to the Team Leader; Claims Manager and Director of Workers’ Compensation and Managed Care 
  • Direct contact with branch underwriting and/or claims service office personnel;
  • Direct contact with Home Office claims personnel;
  • Direct contact with agents, insureds, claimants, medical and legal professionals.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education/Credentials 

  • Continuing education in insurance-related courses such as IIA Certificate in General Insurance, Senior Claims Law Associate, and Associate in Claims courses 
  • Bachelor’s Degree preferred or insurance related experience and/or coursework.
  • Adjuster's license or be willing to obtain one as required

Experience 

  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in workers' compensation claims handling

Technical/Professional Knowledge

  • Must have a good understanding of state statutes applicable to assigned claims, the Unfair Claims Settlement Act and insurance policy coverages and provisions
  • Must have a good understanding of terminology applicable to workers’ compensation 
  • Good communication skills, both oral and written
  • Good inter-personal skills
  • Good negotiation skills
  • Good customer service skills
  • Good analysis and evaluation skills
  • Good decision-making skills
  • Must have a strong sense of urgency
  • Good PC skills, with an emphasis on Microsoft Office Products
  • Good planning and organization skills

  • Must be able to work independently as well as a member of a team

The Manager, Financial Reporting is responsible for the management of the financial reporting function.  The incumbent manages the preparation and analysis of the internal and external financial reports, regulatory and compliance filings and state and local premium taxes. 

This is a hybrid role reporting to the Harrisburg, PA office. 

POSITION COMPETENCIES 

  • Coaching & Influencing 
  • Facilitating Change
  • Ability to Grow & Adapt 
  • Conflict Management 
  • Strategic Planning 
  • Embraces Data Analytics 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Develop, direct and coach assigned staff, to include establishing performance objectives and clear success criteria, as well as monitoring performance outcomes and addressing issues appropriately.
  • Lead by example in communicating with staff. Encourage open dialogue in staff meetings and 1:1 discussions.
  • Develops, implements, and monitors practices, procedures and guidelines for reporting, reconcilement, interpretation and analysis of accounting information.
  • Evaluates staffing needs, assigns work and mentors employees to ensure full utilization of staff.
  • Determines training emphasis, develops educational programs and materials for Financial Reporting staff and delivers training.
  • Quickly modifies daily behavior and tries new approaches to deal effectively with changes; does not persist with ineffective methods; leverages available resources to ease transition.
  • Manages the corporate accounting function responsible for the Statutory and GAAP financial reporting including individual company, consolidated and combined financial statements; comprehensive internal results management and board of directors reporting; regulatory financial filings including quarterly and annual statements; audited financial statements; various general ledger entries and reconciliations; and proper allocation of expense to line of business and expense groups.
  • Manages the internal preparation of various state and local premium tax returns.
  • Completes and/or ensures that staff completes ad hoc assignments or projects on time and with the appropriate level of resources and quality in order to ensure optimally meeting the objectives of the assignment or project.
  • Maintains the general ledger system including the monthly and annual closing process, opening new periods and changing workflow approvals.
  • Responsible for preparing and/or posting entries and preparing, reviewing, and approving account reconciliations.
  • Identifies the key tasks and resources needed to achieve strategic objectives.

 ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Must keep abreast of statutory reporting requirement changes, accounting automation concepts, GAAP practices and principles and industry trends in order to be able to adequately lead or train staff, remain technologically current and apply the latest technology to an accounting system(s), procedural problem and issue of financial reports.
  • Actively seeks information (from coworkers, leaders, customers, competition, technologies, and regulations) to understand the rationale and implications for changes.
  • Treats new situations as opportunities for learning or growth; actively seeks to identify and communicate the benefits of changes; collaborates with others to implement changes.
  • May serve on ad-hoc teams relating to incumbent’s functional area.  This could include leading the team, reviewing requirements, coordination of the test results verification and resolution of issues.
  • Performs other duties as may be assigned by the Director, Financial Reporting.

 SPECIAL RELATIONSHIPS 

  • The incumbent supervises the Financial Analyst and Senior Accountant.
  • Interacts with all levels of internal staff as well as external entities such as auditors, various state insurance departments, and local municipalities. 

QUALIFICATIONS

Education/Credentials

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting required.

  • AIAF insurance designation preferred.

Experience 

  • Minimum of five years of experience in public accounting (auditing insurance companies) and/or insurance accounting required.
  • Previous supervisory experience preferred.

Technical/Professional Knowledge 

  • High level of knowledge relating to Statutory insurance accounting and finance principles preferred
  • High level of knowledge relating to GAAP insurance accounting and finance principles
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Strong organizational skills

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word and Outlook
